objects.description: Enumeration of interpolation modes for animation keys (step, linear, spherical linear, cubic spline). Used by aiVectorKey and aiQuatKey to indicate how to interpolate between consecutive keys.
Time-stamped 3D vector key for translation or scaling tracks, with per-key interpolation mode.
Time-stamped quaternion rotation key with per-key interpolation mode.
Time-stamped key referencing an AnimMesh index within a mesh’s mAnimMeshes array for vertex-based animation switching.
Time-stamped morph/blendshape key with parallel arrays of target indices and weights; owns arrays and deletes them in destructor when present.
Enumeration for pre/post behavior outside key range for node animation channels: default, constant, linear extrapolation, or repeat.
Animation channel for a single node/bone with arrays of position, rotation, and scaling keys plus pre/post behaviors. Owns its key arrays and deletes them in the destructor.
Vertex animation channel for a mesh or mesh group using aiMeshKey frames that reference anim-mesh indices. Owns its mKeys array and deletes it on destruction.
Morph/blendshape animation channel for a mesh or mesh group using aiMeshMorphKey frames. Owns its mKeys array and deletes it on destruction.
Top-level animation object aggregating node, mesh, and morph animation channels with duration and tick rate. Owns arrays of channel pointers and deletes each channel and array in destructor.

Axis-aligned bounding box with minimum and maximum 3D corners. Intended to enclose geometry in world or local space. The fields mMin and mMax are 3D vectors (aiVector3D) giving the box extents. Constructors/destructor are provided in C++ for convenience; in C you allocate and set mMin/mMax manually.

Virtual camera descriptor used by Assimp. It is a scene-graph node-backed camera with position, up, and look-at vectors defined relative to its corresponding node, plus projection parameters (horizontal FOV, near/far clip planes, aspect ratio) and optional orthographic width. In C++ builds it includes a default-initializing constructor and a helper to compute a right-handed view matrix from the camera parameters. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the encompassing scene; this header does not define constructors in the C API beyond the plain struct layout.
Concrete 4-channel color type. In C++ this is an alias of aiColor4t<float>; in C it is a plain struct with float r, g, b, a.
Bitmask enumeration listing removable components for aiProcess_RemoveComponent. Values combine to specify which scene/mesh data parts to strip during post-processing.

Scalar real-number type used throughout Assimp. It is float by default, or double when ASSIMP_DOUBLE_PRECISION is defined. Intended for coordinates, vectors, matrices, angles, etc. Text I/O precision is controlled by ASSIMP_AI_REAL_TEXT_PRECISION macro elsewhere in this header.
Signed integer companion type to ai_real. Width depends on precision mode: 64-bit in double-precision builds, 32-bit otherwise.
Unsigned integer companion type to ai_real. Width depends on precision mode: 64-bit in double-precision builds, 32-bit otherwise.

C-API structure providing file system callbacks used by Assimp to open and close files. Users can supply custom implementations to read from non-standard sources (e.g., archives, memory). The UserData field allows passing arbitrary context to callbacks.

C-API structure wrapping file operation callbacks (read, write, tell, size, seek, flush). Used by Assimp to perform I/O via user-supplied backends. UserData can carry per-file context for the callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef size_t          (*aiFileWriteProc) (C_STRUCT aiFile*,   const char*, size_t, size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for writing to a file. Parameters resemble fwrite: (file, buffer, size, count). Returns number of elements written.

objects.definition: typedef size_t          (*aiFileReadProc)  (C_STRUCT aiFile*,   char*, size_t,size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for reading from a file. Parameters resemble fread: (file, buffer, size, count). Returns number of elements read.

objects.definition: typedef size_t          (*aiFileTellProc)  (C_STRUCT aiFile*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for retrieving the current file position or the file size (when used as FileSizeProc). Returns a byte offset/size.

objects.definition: typedef void            (*aiFileFlushProc) (C_STRUCT aiFile*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for flushing buffered file data to the underlying storage.

objects.definition: typedef C_ENUM aiReturn (*aiFileSeek)      (C_STRUCT aiFile*, size_t, C_ENUM aiOrigin);
objects.description: Function pointer type for seeking within a file. Moves the cursor to an offset relative to the given origin; returns aiReturn status.

objects.definition: typedef C_STRUCT aiFile* (*aiFileOpenProc)  (C_STRUCT aiFileIO*, const char*, const char*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for opening a file. Takes the file system, a path, and an access mode string, and returns an aiFile*.

objects.definition: typedef void             (*aiFileCloseProc) (C_STRUCT aiFileIO*, C_STRUCT aiFile*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for closing a previously opened aiFile.

objects.definition: typedef char* aiUserData;
objects.description: Opaque user-defined data blob passed through to callback implementations. Typically cast to user-specific context types.

enum aiLightSourceType {

objects.description: Enumeration of supported light source kinds used by Assimp to classify aiLight instances (directional, point, spot, ambient, and area).

Light source description used in Assimp scenes. Holds name (matching a scene node), type, transform-relative position/direction/up, attenuation factors, diffuse/specular/ambient colors, spot cone angles, and area size. Defaults provided in C++ ctor; C users must initialize explicitly. Several members are undefined depending on light type (e.g., position for directional, direction for point).
Enumeration of texture layer blend operations used when combining multiple textures within a material.
Enumeration of UV wrapping modes describing how out-of-range texture coordinates are handled.
Enumeration describing how texture coordinates are generated or interpreted for a texture.

objects.description: Enumeration of semantic purposes for textures within a material, covering legacy and PBR workflows.

objects.definition:
enum aiShadingMode {
    aiShadingMode_Flat = 0x1,
    aiShadingMode_Gouraud = 0x2,
    aiShadingMode_Phong = 0x3,

objects.description: Enumeration of shading models; includes classic models and a generic PBR BRDF mode.
Bitflags modifying texture sampling behavior, such as inverting color channels or handling alpha.
Enumeration defining how source material color blends with destination framebuffer color.
Helper struct describing translation, scaling, and rotation applied to texture UVs for a material texture slot.
Internal RTTI enum describing storage type of a material property value buffer.
Represents a single key-value material property. Stores name, texture semantics, index, type info, and raw data buffer.
Key-value material container. In C++ it provides getters/setters and texture helpers; in C it is a POD holding an array of aiMaterialProperty pointers.
Enum-like status/result code used by Assimp API functions. Only referenced here; not defined in this header. Definition missing in this file.

C++ class representing a material in Assimp. Member function inline definitions for getters/setters are provided here, but the class definition itself is not present in this header. Definition missing in this file.
Enumeration of texture semantic types (diffuse, specular, etc.). Only referenced in this file; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Assimp string struct used for material/string properties. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Enumeration describing texture coordinate mapping. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Enumeration describing texture blend operation. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Enumeration describing texture address/wrap mode. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Enumeration specifying the stored data type of a material property (buffer, float, double, integer). Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Struct describing a single material property (key, semantic, index, type, data). Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Typedef for the real-number scalar used by Assimp (float or double depending on build). Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
4-component color type used by Assimp materials. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
3-component color type used by Assimp materials. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
Struct describing UV transform (translation, scaling, rotation). Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.
3D vector type used by Assimp. Only referenced; not defined here. Definition missing in this file.

Row-major 3x3 matrix template with common operations (multiplication, transpose, inverse, determinant) and factory methods for rotations, translation (2D), and constructing from/to vectors. Elements are stored as a1..c3 in row-major order. Default constructor initializes to identity. In C++ builds, aiMatrix3x3 is an alias of aiMatrix3x3t<ai_real>.

C-build layout of a row-major 3x3 matrix with ai_real elements. In C++ builds, aiMatrix3x3 is a typedef alias of aiMatrix3x3t<ai_real> instead of this struct. Provides no methods; fields are public for direct access.
Concrete vector alias/type used in FromToMatrix for temporaries. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.

Row-major 4x4 homogeneous transformation matrix template with utilities for construction from components, decomposition, inversion, determinant, and common factory methods (rotation, translation, scaling). Alias aiMatrix4x4 binds TReal to ai_real. Intended for 3D geometry transforms in Assimp.
C struct layout of a row-major 4x4 matrix for non-C++ builds, matching the memory layout of aiMatrix4x4t<ai_real>. Used to represent homogeneous transformation matrices in C APIs.
Represents a polygonal face by holding an array of vertex indices. Manages its own index array in C++ (copying, deletion).
A single bone influence on a vertex: vertex index and weight (0..1).
A mesh bone with name, vertex weights, and offset matrix (inverse bind pose). Optionally links to armature/node when populated.
Bitflags enumerating supported primitive kinds and an NGON encoding flag. Used in aiMesh::mPrimitiveTypes.
Per-vertex override data for a host mesh at a particular morph target; includes positions, normals, tangents, colors, UVs, and a weight.
Enumeration of morph target blending methods used by meshes with anim-meshes.

Primary mesh structure: per-vertex streams, faces, bones, material index, morph targets, morphing method, AABB, and optional UV set names. C++ destructor owns and deletes allocated arrays and contained bones/anim meshes.
Represents a bone in a skeleton hierarchy, including parent index, optional armature/node links, weights affecting a mesh, and matrices for bind pose and local transform.
A skeleton consisting of a set of bones forming a hierarchy. Holds name, bone count, and array of bone pointers. Owns the array but not necessarily the bones themselves.

objects.description: Enumeration of bit flags selecting Assimp post-processing steps to apply during import. Each value is a mask bit that can be ORed together and passed to import functions (e.g., Assimp::Importer::ReadFile or aiImportFile) to request specific conversions/optimizations on the loaded scene. The header provides extensive per-flag behavior notes. Construction is by value; typical usage is as bitmask constants rather than variables of this enum type.

Template quaternion class representing a rotation as four components (w, x, y, z). Provides constructors from components, rotation matrix, Euler angles, axis-angle, and normalized vec3; operations include normalization, conjugation, rotation of a vector, multiplication, equality checks, and spherical interpolation. The alias aiQuaternion binds TReal to ai_real. Some constructors and methods are declared here but defined elsewhere.
C struct representation of a quaternion with components w, x, y, z, available when compiling as C (i.e., not __cplusplus). Minimal POD without methods.

Hierarchy node of an imported scene. Holds a name, transform relative to parent, optional children, mesh index list, and optional metadata. Provides C++ helpers to find nodes by name and locate the node corresponding to a given bone, and to add children. Lifetime is owned by the aiScene that references it.

Root container describing an imported scene. Aggregates the scene graph root node, arrays of meshes, materials, animations, embedded textures, lights, cameras, optional skeletons, and scene-wide metadata and name. Provides C++ helpers to query presence of arrays, locate embedded textures by name or index token, and find a bone across meshes. Ownership is typically handled by Assimp importers/exporters; clients should not free these pointers manually.

objects.definition:
typedef enum aiMetadataType {
    AI_BOOL = 0,
    AI_INT32 = 1,
    AI_UINT64 = 2,
    AI_FLOAT = 3,
    AI_DOUBLE = 4,
    AI_AISTRING = 5,
    AI_AIVECTOR3D = 6,
    AI_AIMETADATA = 7,
    AI_INT64 = 8,
    AI_UINT32 = 9,
    AI_META_MAX = 10,

#ifndef SWIG
    FORCE_32BIT = INT_MAX
#endif
} aiMetadataType;
objects.description: Enumeration of metadata value types used to discriminate the runtime type stored in aiMetadataEntry::mData. Includes scalar primitives, aiString, aiVector3D, nested aiMetadata, and sentinel values. FORCE_32BIT ensures the enum is 32-bit on some toolchains.

A single metadata key's value holder. mType indicates the concrete type of the value and mData points to a dynamically allocated instance of that type (or nullptr if unset). The struct is POD in C; in C++ it has a default constructor. Memory ownership of mData is managed by aiMetadata, which allocates, copies, and deletes it based on mType.

Key-value metadata container. Holds parallel arrays of keys (aiString) and values (aiMetadataEntry). Provides C++ helpers for allocation, deallocation, add/set/get, comparisons, and nested metadata. Owns and manages the lifetime of mKeys, mValues, and the dynamically allocated mData inside each aiMetadataEntry based on mType.

Represents a single texel stored in ARGB8888-like layout (fields stored as b,g,r,a bytes). Used by aiTexture for uncompressed pixel data. Provides C++ comparison operators and conversion to aiColor4D. Memory layout is packed as controlled by PACK_STRUCT; consumers should treat it as 4 bytes per texel in the order b,g,r,a.

Describes an embedded texture stored within a scene. If mHeight != 0, pcData points to an array of uncompressed aiTexel with dimensions mWidth x mHeight; achFormatHint may describe channel order/bitness (e.g., "rgba8888"). If mHeight == 0, the texture is stored as compressed file bytes; then mWidth is the byte size, pcData is a byte buffer (reinterpret_cast from aiTexel*), and achFormatHint usually contains a file extension like "jpg" or zeroed. In C++ builds, the destructor deletes[] pcData, implying ownership when allocated with new[].

Internal helper base to ensure objects are allocated/freed using Assimp's heap (safe across DLL boundaries). Provides custom new/delete (scalar and array). Implementation not shown here. Typically used as a base for types that must be deallocated by Assimp.
Represents a plane in 3D Euclidean space using coefficients a,b,c,d of the plane equation ax + by + cz + d = 0.
Represents a 3D ray with origin (pos) and direction (dir). Direction is not guaranteed to be normalized.
RGB color with float components r,g,b in [0,1] typically. Provides arithmetic and comparison helpers.

UTF-8, zero-terminated string type with fixed maximum buffer size AI_MAXLEN (including terminator). Holds binary length (bytes) and storage. Provides utilities to set/append/clear. Not a std::string to support C API.
Standard return code enum for Assimp API calls: success, failure, and out-of-memory. The final enumerator enforces 32-bit enum size.
Seek origin enum for virtual file system operations (begin, current, end).
Predefined log destinations used by logging utilities (file, stdout, stderr, debugger).
Holds per-category memory usage (bytes) of an imported scene: textures, materials, meshes, nodes, animations, cameras, lights, and total. Used by Importer::GetMemoryRequirements().
Simple read-only in-memory buffer view defined by two pointers [data, end). No ownership semantics defined here.

objects.definition: typedef int32_t ai_int32;
objects.description: Typedef alias for 32-bit signed integer used by Assimp. Pointer type refers to ai_int32*.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ai_uint32;
objects.description: Typedef alias for 32-bit unsigned integer used by Assimp. Pointer type refers to ai_uint32*.

Templated 2D vector class with components x and y and typical vector operations (length, normalization, arithmetic, comparisons). The canonical runtime typedef is aiVector2D = aiVector2t<ai_real>. In C compilation mode, aiVector2D is defined as a plain struct with two ai_real fields. Methods are declared but defined elsewhere. ai_real and ai_epsilon come from defs.h. Some behavioral details (normalization behavior on zero length, bounds of operator[]) are not specified here.

C ABI representation/name for a 3D vector when compiling as C (non-C++). In C++ builds, aiVector3D is a typedef alias to aiVector3t<ai_real>; in C builds, it is a plain struct with x, y, z of type ai_real.
C-API log stream object carrying a callback and a user data pointer. Attach/detach instances to receive Assimp log messages. The callback is invoked for each log line with the provided user pointer.
Opaque handle to a set of importer configuration properties. Although defined with a sentinel member here, it should be treated as opaque and created/destroyed via the API.

objects.definition: typedef int aiBool;
objects.description: Assimp’s C boolean typedef. Use AI_TRUE (1) and AI_FALSE (0).

objects.definition: typedef void (*aiLogStreamCallback)(const char * /* message */, char * /* user */);
objects.description: Function pointer type for log callbacks receiving a message string and the user data pointer stored in aiLogStream.

objects.definition: struct aiScene;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the imported scene object. Full definition is not present in this header; treat as opaque pointer managed by the import APIs.

objects.definition: struct aiTexture;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a texture container embedded in scenes. Not defined here; retrieval via aiGetEmbeddedTexture.

objects.definition: struct aiFileIO;
objects.description: Forward declaration of custom file I/O interface used by import functions. Definition resides in aiFileIO.h.

Function pointer type alias representing an assertion handler callback in the Assimp namespace. The pointed-to function receives the failed expression text, the source file name, and the line number. Intended to be installed via setAiAssertHandler to customize assertion handling.

Bitflag enumeration describing characteristics of an importer implementation (e.g., whether it supports text, binary, compressed flavors; is limited or experimental). Intended to populate aiImporterDesc::mFlags.

Metadata structure describing an importer: human-readable name, authorship, comments, supported feature flags, min/max loadable format versions, and supported file extensions. Typically returned by aiGetImporterDesc and used for UI or capability queries.

C++ front-end to Assimp’s import pipeline. Manages configuration properties, IO and progress handlers, and performs file or memory imports to produce an aiScene. Owns the loaded scene until released via GetOrphanedScene. Not thread-safe per instance. Deleted copy/assign; uses a pimpl for implementation hiding.

objects.definition: class ImporterPimpl;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared implementation detail for Assimp::Importer (pimpl idiom). No definition provided here.

objects.definition: class IOStream;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an IO stream interface used by Assimp for custom file access. No definition here.

objects.definition: class IOSystem;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the IO system abstraction used to open/read files. No definition here.

objects.definition: class ProgressHandler;
objects.description: Forward declaration of progress reporting/abort callback interface used during import. No definition here.

objects.definition: class BaseImporter;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a plugin base class for format importers. No definition here.

objects.definition: class BaseProcess;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a post-process step base class in Assimp’s pipeline. No definition here.

objects.definition: class SharedPostProcessInfo;
objects.description: Forward declaration for shared post-process context/info passed among steps. No definition here.

objects.definition: class BatchLoader;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an API for batching multiple import operations. No definition here.

objects.definition: struct aiScene;
objects.description: C API scene root structure holding imported meshes, materials, nodes, etc. Only forward-declared here; full definition is external.

objects.definition: struct aiImporterDesc;
objects.description: C API structure describing an importer’s capabilities and metadata. Forward declaration only; full definition in <assimp/importerdesc.h>.

Primary logging facility implementation for Assimp. Implements Logger and manages attachment of LogStream outputs, message dispatch by severity, and a singleton-style global logger instance. By default a NullLogger is active; create() replaces it with a DefaultLogger using optional default streams and IOSystem. Thread-safe stream list when multithreading is enabled. Construction is private; use create() or set() to activate. Unknown details include exact formatting and stream info structure, which are defined elsewhere.

Abstract base class in namespace Assimp for receiving progress updates during file import, post-processing, and export. Users subclass ProgressHandler and implement Update(float) to receive progress notifications. UpdateFileRead/UpdatePostProcess/UpdateFileWrite provide default mappings to the single Update callback. No exceptions should be thrown from callbacks and non-const Importer methods must not be called. Construction/destruction: defaulted, no resources owned here. Note: when not built for SWIG, the class inherits from Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap to allocate from Assimp's heap.

Abstract C++ interface for file I/O used by Assimp. Implementations provide read/write/seek/tell/size/flush for backing stores (e.g., disk files, memory). Constructor is protected; instances are typically produced by an IOSystem implementation. May derive from Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap when not building with SWIG. No concrete implementation is defined in this header.

C++ abstract interface representing a filesystem handler used by Assimp. Provides virtual methods to check existence, open/close files (via IOStream), path comparison, and simple directory stack and filesystem operations (create/change/delete). Intended to be subclassed to integrate custom I/O backends. Inherits from Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap when not compiled with SWIG. Note: IOStream is only forward-declared here and must be provided elsewhere. Some methods have inline std::string overloads for backward compatibility. CurrentDirectory() is declared but its definition is not present in this header; it is expected to be defined in a corresponding source file.

Abstract base class for Assimp logging. Provides severity-based logging APIs, stream attachment/detachment, and virtual sinks (OnDebug/OnVerboseDebug/OnInfo/OnWarn/OnError) to be implemented by concrete loggers. Manages severity threshold and takes ownership of attached LogStream instances. Contains two nested enums (LogSeverity, ErrorSeverity). Note: OnWarn parameter name has a typo in this header (const char* essage).
Enumeration nested in Assimp::Logger that selects the global logging verbosity level used by a Logger instance.
Bitmask flags nested in Assimp::Logger used to filter which message classes a LogStream receives. Combine flags with bitwise OR when attaching/detaching streams.

Abstract base class for output log streams in Assimp’s C++ API. Users subclass LogStream and implement write(const char*) to route log messages to a destination (file, console, custom sink). Instances can also be obtained via createDefaultStream for several built-in stream types. The class is allocated from Assimp’s heap when not building for SWIG. Destruction is virtual. The purpose is to receive formatted log lines; messages may be multi-line though typically are single lines ending with \n.

A no-op logger implementation in namespace Assimp that derives from Logger. All logging methods discard input and return false for stream attachment/detachment. Used as the default logger when none is provided. Construction/destruction behavior is inherited from Logger; this header does not define constructors or members. Details of Logger and LogStream are declared in Logger.hpp and not part of this header.
Describes an exportable file format in Assimp: a short unique ID, a human-readable description, and a recommended lowercase file extension.

Holds a blob of exported scene data owned by Assimp. The primary blob (empty name) contains the main file data; additional blobs in a linked list (next) may represent auxiliary files. In C++ builds it auto-frees its data and the chained blobs in the destructor. Do not free with user allocators; use aiReleaseExportBlob for C API.

C++ interface to Assimp's export functionality. Manages IO and progress handlers, provides exporting to files or in-memory blobs, enumerates and registers exporter backends, and manages the lifetime of the last produced export blob. Not copy semantics specified; pimpl hides implementation.
Internal record describing a single export format: its public aiExportFormatDesc, the function pointer that performs the export, and enforced pre-processing flags to run prior to export.

Container for exporter configuration key-value properties across multiple types (int/bool, float, string, matrix, callback). Properties are looked up by hashed keys derived from string names. Used to pass options to exporter backends.

objects.definition: class ExporterPimpl;
objects.description: Forward-declared private implementation type for Assimp::Exporter, defined elsewhere. Incomplete here; used as a pointer member to hide implementation details.

objects.definition: class IOSystem;
objects.description: Forward declaration of Assimp IOSystem interface, defined elsewhere. Here it is only referenced for dependency injection of custom file I/O backends.

objects.definition: class ProgressHandler;
objects.description: Forward declaration of progress callback interface, defined elsewhere. Used by Exporter to report progress and allow cancellation.

Concrete IOStream implementation in namespace Assimp that uses C stdio (fopen/fread/fwrite/etc.) for file access. Instances may exist without a valid FILE handle; in that case, operations fail safely. It stores a FILE*, filename string, and a cached size. It derives from IOStream (declared elsewhere) and is typically created by DefaultIOSystem. Construction is protected; creation is intended via friend IO systems.

Concrete final implementation of Assimp's IOSystem that uses standard C file functions to provide file existence checks, open/close, and path utilities. It overrides the IOSystem interface methods and adds static helpers for path manipulation. Construction is default; lifetime is managed by the caller. No additional ownership semantics are declared in this header.

IOSystem implementation that treats a ZIP archive as a virtual filesystem, allowing Assimp to open files within the archive via the standard IOSystem interface. It supports checking existence, opening/closing streams from inside the ZIP, and listing contained files or those with a specific extension. Uses a PIMPL (Implement) to hide zlib/zip details.

Helper data structure describing which aiNode in a master scene an imported scene (aiScene) should be attached to during merging operations. Holds raw pointers to the scene and the attachment node; lifetime is not owned here.

Helper for SceneCombiner graph attachment. Couples a source aiNode with a target attachment node, tracks whether the attachment has been resolved, and stores the source index to correlate with input arrays. Does not own the nodes.

Aggregates a hashed bone name (uint32_t) and pointer to aiString (via base pair) with a list of source bone references from multiple meshes. Used by MergeBones/BuildUniqueBoneList to deduplicate and merge bones.

Utility holder for operations on a scene: stores a scene pointer, an identifier prefix buffer and length, and a set of name hashes to detect duplicates. Provides operator-> to access the underlying aiScene. Does not manage ownership of aiScene.

Static-only utility class providing merging and copying operations for Assimp scenes, nodes, meshes, materials, bones, and related structures. Constructors are deleted to prevent instantiation. Methods operate on ai* types; no ownership of inputs unless documented by methods (e.g., MergeScenes deletes source scenes).

objects.definition: using BoneSrcIndex = std::pair<aiBone *, unsigned int> ;
objects.description: Type alias pairing a bone pointer with a source index (e.g., mesh index) to track origin of a bone during merge operations.

Union representing the raw IEEE-754 bit layout of a 32-bit float. Provides access to the sign, exponent, and fraction fields via the nested IEEE bitfield struct, and to the interpreted floating value via Float. Useful for detecting NaN/Inf and other bit-level inspections.

Union representing the raw IEEE-754 bit layout of a 64-bit double. Provides access to the sign, exponent, and fraction fields via the nested IEEE bitfield struct, and to the interpreted floating value via Double. Enables bit-level checks for NaN/Inf and related conditions.

Abstract base class for all Assimp importer workers. Provides capability checks (CanRead), file import orchestration (ReadFile calling InternReadFile), error/exception reporting, extension utilities, and various helper utilities for text/binary detection and buffer copying. Derived importers implement CanRead, GetInfo, and InternReadFile. Holds scaling parameters and a progress handler pointer.
Enumeration used by text file helper APIs to indicate whether empty text files are acceptable (ALLOW_EMPTY) or should be treated as an error (FORBID_EMPTY).

objects.definition: using UByteBuffer = std::vector<uint8_t>;
objects.description: Type alias for a vector of unsigned bytes (uint8_t). Useful as a raw byte buffer for file data and utilities.

objects.definition: using ByteBuffer = std::vector<int8_t>;
objects.description: Type alias for a vector of signed bytes (int8_t). Useful as a raw signed byte buffer for file/text processing.
Alias for a 32-bit unsigned integer from stdint.h. Note: This header only uses uint32_t; it does not define it.
Alias for a 16-bit unsigned integer from stdint.h. Note: This header only uses uint16_t; it does not define it.
Alias for an 8-bit unsigned integer from stdint.h. Note: This header only uses uint8_t; it does not define it.
Pointer to character data used by the SuperFastHash function. Not defined here; standard C type.

Concrete IOStream that reads from a provided memory buffer. It supports read, seek, tell, and filesize; writing and flushing are unsupported (assert). If constructed with own=true, it deletes the buffer with delete[] in the destructor, otherwise it does not manage the buffer lifetime.

IOSystem implementation that exposes a single in-memory stream when opened with the magic filename "$$$___magic___$$$". Delegates all other IO operations to an existing IOSystem if provided. Manages created MemoryIOStream instances and deletes them on Close when they were created by this system. Does not own the input buffer; it only stores a pointer and size.

Template class that wraps an Assimp IOStream and provides buffered reads of POD values with optional byte swapping for endianness. It reads the remainder of the stream into an internal buffer on construction and offers typed getters (Get<T>() and convenience methods) plus read limits and pointer-style navigation. Template parameters: SwapEndianness determines whether bytes are swapped relative to host; RuntimeSwitch allows runtime selection of little-endian input via the le ctor parameter. Typedefs provide fixed LE/BE readers and a runtime-selectable variant.

Template class that buffers binary writes to an Assimp IOStream with controlled endianness. Provides typed Put methods and string writes, internal buffering with flush-on-destruction, and optional runtime endianness selection. SwapEndianness controls whether to swap bytes when writing; RuntimeSwitch enables the constructor flag 'le' to indicate little-endian target. Destructor flushes remaining buffer. Usage requires valid IOStream and that ByteSwapper support exists for written types.

Typedef alias for a StreamWriter with fixed endianness matching little-endian outputs regardless of platform. On big-endian builds it maps to StreamWriter<true> (swap when writing), on little-endian builds to StreamWriter<false> (no swap).
Typedef alias for a StreamWriter with fixed big-endian output. On big-endian builds it maps to StreamWriter<false> (no swap), on little-endian builds to StreamWriter<true> (swap).

objects.definition: typedef StreamWriter<true,true> StreamWriterAny;
objects.description: Typedef alias for a StreamWriter that allows runtime selection of target endianness via constructor parameter 'le'. Always performs conditional swapping at runtime.

A spatial sorting helper for locating vertices near a given position with awareness of smoothing groups. Provides insertion of vertices with their smoothing group, prepares an internal plane-based sort, and queries for nearby vertices sharing smoothing constraints. Internal data are stored as sorted Entries by distance to a reference plane. Construction details outside this header (e.g., plane selection) are not specified here.

Spatially sorted index over a set of 3D positions to accelerate proximity queries. It stores copies of positions with their source indices, projects them onto a reference plane for sorting, and supports finding nearby or identical positions and building a vertex mapping table. Requires Finalize before queries if data was appended with pFinalize=false.
direct_api_constructors: Assimp::SpatialSort::SpatialSort(const aiVector3D *, unsigned int, unsigned int)

objects.description: Helper class that constructs a dummy mesh reflecting the node hierarchy of an aiScene, useful for formats that contain only animation data and no mesh. The constructor processes the provided scene, optionally starting at a given root node, and builds vertices, faces, and bones; it can create the mesh and a dummy material. Details of how data are assembled are not present in this header.

Helper struct for faces that carry a smoothing group id. Holds three vertex indices (32-bit) and a 32-bit smoothing group bitmask/id. Default constructor zero-initializes the smoothing group and, in debug builds, fills indices with 0xFFFFFFFF to catch uninitialized use.

Non-instantiable helper class within Assimp that provides static factory/generator methods to build aiMesh instances and position arrays for standard geometric primitives (hexahedron, icosahedron, dodecahedron, octahedron, tetrahedron, sphere, cone/cylinder, circle). It has a private default constructor to prevent instantiation and exposes only static methods.

Non-instantiable helper class in the Assimp namespace providing static utilities to strip single-line and multi-line comments from mutable C-string buffers. Constructors/destructor are deleted, so use only the provided static functions. Expected to replace comment regions with a specified character (default space). Details of in-place modification and edge cases beyond comments not nested are not specified here.

Abstract helper class for evaluating subdivision surfaces within Assimp. It exposes a factory (Create) to instantiate a concrete subdivider implementing a specified Algorithm (currently only CATMULL_CLARKE). It provides two pure-virtual Subdivide overloads to subdivide a single mesh or multiple meshes, possibly deleting inputs to reuse memory. Destruction is virtual and defaulted. Concrete implementations live elsewhere.
Enumeration of supported subdivision algorithms for Assimp::Subdivider. Currently provides CATMULL_CLARKE. Used as a selector when creating a Subdivider instance.
Forward declaration of Assimp mesh structure referenced by Subdivider methods. The full definition is not present in this header.

Interleaved vertex aggregate used by Assimp to collect all possible vertex components (position, normal, tangent, bitangent, per-channel texture coordinates, per-channel vertex colors) in a single struct, with arithmetic operators to support interpolation, subdivision, and scaling. It can be constructed directly from aiMesh or aiAnimMesh at a given vertex index and written back using SortBack. Uses aiVector3D and aiColor4D for components; array sizes depend on AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS and AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_COLOR_SETS.

Helper class that iterates line-by-line over a StreamReaderLE input, providing tokenization utilities and lightweight pseudo-iterator semantics. It maintains current line text, a zero-based line index, and options for skipping empty lines and trimming. Construct with a StreamReaderLE reference; increment with operator++ to advance to the next line; access tokens using operator[] or get_tokens; access the current line via operator-> or operator*; use match_start to test prefixes. Destruction is trivial; the underlying stream is not owned. Copy/move are disabled. Note: operator bool() returns true while there is remaining data in the underlying stream; dereferencing beyond end throws logic_error on increment. Token access throws range_error on EOL. The mEnd pointer is used as an upper bound for parsing helpers; it is set relative to an internal string buffer.
direct_api_constructors: Assimp::LineSplitter::LineSplitter(Assimp::StreamReaderLE& stream, bool skip_empty_lines = true, bool trim = true)

objects.description: Templated lightweight formatter that wraps std::basic_ostringstream to build strings via operator<<. Special-cases std::exception-derived tokens to stream .what(). Provides implicit conversion to std::basic_string and supports both const and non-const operator<<. The provided typedef format is an alias for basic_formatter<char>. Intended for easy logging and message construction without boost::format. Construction is trivial; object owns an internal stringstream. Copying is implemented manually for certain compiler versions; moving is supported except on older GCC where it falls back to streaming the source string. No destructor or special lifetime rules beyond standard C++ semantics.

Wide-character specialization of the same basic_formatter template when instantiated with wchar_t. The typedef wformat aliases basic_formatter<wchar_t>. Intended for building std::wstring messages via operator<< with the same exception handling and conversion semantics.

objects.definition: typedef basic_formatter< char > format;
objects.description: Alias typedef for basic_formatter<char>. Provides a convenient name for narrow-character formatting.

objects.definition: typedef basic_formatter< wchar_t > wformat;
objects.description: Alias typedef for basic_formatter<wchar_t>. Provides a convenient name for wide-character formatting.

A lightweight profiling utility class in namespace Assimp::Profiling that measures elapsed time between BeginRegion and EndRegion calls for named regions and logs start/end events via Assimp's DefaultLogger. Stores start timestamps per region in an internal map. Construction and destruction are trivial; no dynamic ownership semantics are exposed.

Helper class for constructing and writing BMP bitmaps from embedded Assimp textures. Provides a static Save function to serialize an aiTexture to an IOStream in BMP format. Contains internal Header and DIB structures mirroring BMP file and DIB headers, plus helpers to write them and the pixel data. Lifetime is not managed; all methods are static.

Predicate functor that matches a pugi::xml_node by name. Stores the target name and returns true when invoked with a node whose name equals mName. Useful with pugixml search APIs like find_node and find_child.

Templated XML parser wrapper around pugixml for reading and querying XML content. Manages a pugi::xml_document pointer (owned) and a buffer of loaded data when parsing from IOStream. Provides helpers to query nodes and attributes and retrieve text values. Alias XmlParser binds TNodeType to pugi::xml_node.

Iterator utility that flattens the descendants of a parent XmlNode (pugi::xml_node) into a vector either in pre-order or post-order, and provides sequential access via getNext. It holds a reference to the parent and does not own nodes.

Final IOStream implementation that captures written data into a dynamically grown memory buffer and exposes it as an aiExportDataBlob. Read is unsupported (returns 0). Seek/Tell/FileSize behave like a write-only file. On destruction it hands its accumulated blob back to the owning BlobIOSystem via OnDestruct. Intended for exporters to write out to memory blobs instead of disk files.

Final IOSystem implementation that intercepts write-only file operations and produces a chain of aiExportDataBlob objects representing all opened/written files. Tracks created filenames, owns collected blobs until GetBlobChain is called, then returns a master blob with linked list of additional blobs and relinquishes ownership.

objects.definition: #define AI_BLOBIO_MAGIC "$blobfile"
objects.description: Preprocessor macro defining the default magic master filename used by BlobIOSystem. Although a macro, it serves as a named constant string used to identify the master blob file when no explicit base name is provided.

Base class for all Assimp fatal error exceptions. Inherits from std::runtime_error and provides variadic-formatting constructors using Assimp::Formatter to build the error message. The non-template constructor taking Assimp::Formatter::format is only declared here; its body is defined elsewhere.

Exception for importer plugins to signal unrecoverable errors during import. Returning nullptr scenes is expected by callers when this is thrown and caught by helper macros. Provides constructors that format messages using Assimp::Formatter.
Final exception type for exporter plugins to signal unrecoverable errors during export. Uses Assimp::Formatter-based variadic constructor to build the error message.

Full specialization of ExceptionSwallower for aiReturn. Re-throws the current exception to map bad_alloc to aiReturn_OUTOFMEMORY and any other exception to aiReturn_FAILURE. Requires invocation within a catch-all context where an exception is active.
Full specialization of ExceptionSwallower for void return type; operator() does nothing, enabling functions with void return to swallow exceptions cleanly.

Utility class providing static functions to byte-swap 2-, 4-, and 8-byte values and typed overloads for common integral and floating types. It also offers a templated Swapped() that returns a value with bytes swapped at compile-time-selected width. Construction is private; use static methods only. No ownership semantics; pure helper.
Alias from <stdint.h> for an 8-bit unsigned integer type. Referenced but not defined here; included for clarity that no custom typedefs are introduced in this header.

functions.name: aiVectorKey::operator==
functions.description: Compares two aiVectorKey instances for equality by comparing their mValue (aiVector3D) fields. Times and interpolation modes are ignored.
requirements: Both this and rhs must be valid, initialized aiVectorKey objects.
Equality is based solely on mValue; mTime and mInterpolation are not considered.

functions.name: aiVectorKey::operator!=
functions.description: Returns true if the aiVector3D values (mValue) of the two aiVectorKey instances differ. Times and interpolation modes are ignored.

Inequality is based solely on mValue; mTime and mInterpolation are not considered.

functions.description: Orders aiVectorKey instances by their time stamp (mTime). Useful for chronological sorting.
requirements: Both operands must be valid, initialized aiVectorKey objects.
Comparison uses only mTime; mValue and mInterpolation are not considered.

functions.description: Orders aiVectorKey instances by their time stamp (mTime), returning true if this key’s time is greater than rhs.mTime.

Comparison uses only mTime; mValue and mInterpolation are not considered.

requirements: Both operands must be valid, initialized aiQuatKey objects.
Comparison uses only mTime; mValue and mInterpolation are not considered.

requirements: Both operands must be valid, initialized aiMeshKey objects.

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<aiQuaternion>::operator()
functions.signature: void Assimp::Interpolator<aiQuaternion>::operator()(aiQuaternion &out, const aiQuaternion &a, const aiQuaternion &b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Interpolates between two quaternions a and b and writes the result to out. Uses aiQuaternion::Interpolate (spherical linear interpolation). Intended for animation blending.
requirements: out must be a valid reference to an aiQuaternion to receive the result.
a and b must be valid quaternions.
d should be a finite scalar (typically in [0,1] for interpolation; larger/smaller values imply extrapolation).

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<unsigned int>::operator()
functions.signature: void Assimp::Interpolator<unsigned int>::operator()(unsigned int &out, unsigned int a, unsigned int b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Interpolates between two unsigned integer values by selecting a or b depending on whether d > 0.5f (nearest selection). Writes the chosen value to out.
requirements: out must be a valid reference to an unsigned int to receive the result.
No other constraints; selection is purely based on whether d > 0.5f.

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<aiVectorKey>::operator()
functions.signature: void Assimp::Interpolator<aiVectorKey>::operator()(aiVector3D &out, const aiVectorKey &a, const aiVectorKey &b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Interpolates linearly between two vector keys by interpolating their mValue (aiVector3D) components and writes the result to out. Time stamps are not used here.
requirements: out must be a valid reference to an aiVector3D to receive the result.
a and b must be valid aiVectorKey objects; only their mValue fields are used.
d should be a finite scalar (typically in [0,1] for interpolation).

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<aiQuatKey>::operator()
functions.signature: void Assimp::Interpolator<aiQuatKey>::operator()(aiQuaternion &out, const aiQuatKey &a, const aiQuatKey &b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Interpolates between two quaternion keys by slerping their mValue (aiQuaternion) components and writes the result to out. Time stamps are not used here.
requirements: out must be a valid reference to an aiQuaternion to receive the result.
a and b must be valid aiQuatKey objects; only their mValue fields are used.
d should be a finite scalar (typically in [0,1] for interpolation).

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<aiMeshKey>::operator()
functions.signature: void Assimp::Interpolator<aiMeshKey>::operator()(unsigned int &out, const aiMeshKey &a, const aiMeshKey &b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Interpolates between two mesh index keys by choosing one of the indices (nearest selection via the unsigned int specialization) and writes it to out. Time stamps are not used here.
requirements: out must be a valid reference to an unsigned int to receive the result.
a and b must be valid aiMeshKey objects; only their mValue fields are used.
Selection is based on d > 0.5f (choose b) otherwise a.

functions.name: Assimp::Interpolator<T>::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T> void Assimp::Interpolator<T>::operator()(T &anim_out, const T &a, const T &b, ai_real d) const
functions.description: Generic interpolation functor. Performs linear interpolation between a and b and writes the result to anim_out using the expression anim_out = a + (b - a) * d. For types with dedicated specializations (e.g., aiQuaternion, aiVectorKey, aiQuatKey, aiMeshKey, unsigned int), those are used instead.
requirements: T must support the operations: subtraction (b - a), scalar multiplication by ai_real, and addition to assign into anim_out.
anim_out must be a valid reference to T to receive the result.
a and b must be valid instances of T.
d should be a finite scalar (typically in [0,1] for interpolation).

functions.name: Assimp::aiAssertViolation
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void Assimp::aiAssertViolation(const char* failedExpression, const char* file, int line);
functions.description: Handles an assertion failure in Assimp debug builds. Intended to be invoked by the ai_assert(...) macro when an expression evaluates to false, passing the failed expression text, source file, and line number. The concrete behavior is customizable (see AssertHandler.h) and may log, break, or otherwise report the violation; exact side effects are not specified here. Typical usage is indirect through ai_assert(expr); direct calls are mainly for custom testing or integrating a bespoke assertion pipeline. Only declared/available when ASSIMP_BUILD_DEBUG is defined.
requirements: Available only when compiled with ASSIMP_BUILD_DEBUG defined; callers must not rely on this symbol in release builds.
Callers should prefer using the ai_assert(expression) macro instead of invoking this function directly, unless intentionally integrating a custom assertion flow.
failedExpression must be a valid, null-terminated C string describing the expression (typically provided by the macro); nullptr is not permitted (inferred from usage and C string expectations).
file must be a valid, null-terminated C string giving the source file path (typically __FILE__); nullptr is not permitted (inferred).
line must be a non-negative integer representing the source line (typically __LINE__).
This function returns void; any error signaling or termination behavior is implementation-defined and not documented here (behavior customizable; see AssertHandler.h).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified/unknown; callers should not assume this function is thread-safe.

functions.name: aiCamera::aiCamera
functions.description: Default constructor for aiCamera. Initializes a right-handed camera with default parameters: mUp = (0,1,0), mLookAt = (0,0,1), mHorizontalFOV = 0.25*PI, mClipPlaneNear = 0.1, mClipPlaneFar = 1000, mAspect = 0, mOrthographicWidth = 0. Intended for C++ use to create a camera with sensible defaults that can then be customized before use.
requirements: C++ only (constructor is available in the C++ section of the header).
No arguments; constructs an object in a valid but default-initialized state.
Does not throw (AI_NO_EXCEPT).

functions.name: aiCamera::GetCameraMatrix
functions.description: Computes and writes a right-handed view (camera) matrix from this aiCamera’s position and orientation into the provided out matrix. It normalizes mLookAt and mUp, computes the right vector as mUp ^ mLookAt, and fills the matrix such that it can be used as a view transform. Use when you need the camera’s local view matrix derived from its parameters (node transforms must be applied separately, as noted in the header comments).
requirements: out must be a valid, writable aiMatrix4x4 reference.
mLookAt must be a non-zero vector (it is normalized internally).
mUp must be a non-zero vector (it is normalized internally).
mUp and mLookAt must not be parallel or anti-parallel (their cross product is used and must be non-zero).
Produces a right-handed view matrix; callers expecting left-handed matrices must convert accordingly.
Function is const and has no side effects beyond writing to out.

functions.name: aiColor4t::operator+=
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
const aiColor4t<TReal>& aiColor4t<TReal>::operator+=(const aiColor4t<TReal>& o);
functions.description: Adds the RGBA components of another color to this color in-place. Intended for accumulating color values component-wise. Returns a const reference to this color to allow chaining. Implementation details (clamping or normalization) are not shown in the header; behavior for values outside [0,1] is unknown.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Caller must provide a valid aiColor4t<TReal> argument.
Color component values are documented to range from 0 to 1; callers should ensure inputs respect this range to avoid undefined or implementation-specific behavior.
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent mutation of the same instance must be externally synchronized.

const aiColor4t<TReal>& aiColor4t<TReal>::operator-=(const aiColor4t<TReal>& o);

requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Caller must provide a valid aiColor4t<TReal> argument.
Color component values are documented to range from 0 to 1; callers should ensure inputs respect this range to avoid undefined or implementation-specific behavior.
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent mutation of the same instance must be externally synchronized.

template <typename TReal>
const aiColor4t<TReal>& aiColor4t<TReal>::operator*=(TReal f);
functions.description: Multiplies all RGBA components of this color by a scalar in-place. Useful for scaling intensity/alpha. Returns a const reference to this color for chaining. Clamping behavior is not defined in the header.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Scalar f must be a valid value of TReal (finite); behavior for NaN or infinities is unspecified.
Color component values are documented to range from 0 to 1; callers should ensure resulting values meet their expected range constraints.
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent mutation of the same instance must be externally synchronized.

const aiColor4t<TReal>& aiColor4t<TReal>::operator/=(TReal f);
functions.description: Divides all RGBA components of this color by a scalar in-place. Returns a const reference to this color for chaining. No clamping behavior is specified in the header.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Scalar f must be non-zero to avoid division by zero; behavior for zero, NaN, or infinities is unspecified.
Color component values are documented to range from 0 to 1; callers should ensure resulting values meet their expected range constraints.
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent mutation of the same instance must be externally synchronized.

bool aiColor4t<TReal>::operator==(const aiColor4t<TReal>& other) const;
functions.description: Compares two colors for equality. Likely performs component-wise equality. The exact handling of floating-point comparisons (exact vs. epsilon) is not specified in the header.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Caller must provide a valid aiColor4t<TReal> argument.
Floating-point equality semantics are unknown; do not assume epsilon-based comparison unless verified in the implementation.

requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.

bool aiColor4t<TReal>::operator<(const aiColor4t<TReal>& other) const;
functions.description: Orders two colors. The specific ordering (e.g., lexicographic by r,g,b,a or by luminance) is not documented in the header and is unknown. Intended to allow use in ordered containers (e.g., std::map, std::set).
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Caller must provide a valid aiColor4t<TReal> argument.
Exact ordering criterion is unspecified; do not rely on a particular ordering without checking the implementation.

functions.name: aiColor4t::operator[]
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
TReal aiColor4t<TReal>::operator[](unsigned int i) const;
functions.description: Returns the i-th component of the color in RGBA order for a const instance. Valid indices are expected to be 0-based: 0->r, 1->g, 2->b, 3->a. Out-of-range handling is not documented and likely undefined.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Index i must be in the range [0, 3]; behavior for other values is unspecified/likely undefined.
Callers must not assume bounds checking or exceptions on invalid indices.

functions.signature:

TReal& aiColor4t<TReal>::operator[](unsigned int i);
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the i-th component of the color in RGBA order for a non-const instance. Valid indices are expected to be 0-based: 0->r, 1->g, 2->b, 3->a. Out-of-range handling is not documented and likely undefined.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Index i must be in the range [0, 3]; behavior for other values is unspecified/likely undefined.
Callers must not assume bounds checking or exceptions on invalid indices.
When writing through the returned reference, maintain component values in the documented [0,1] range to preserve color validity.

functions.name: aiColor4t::IsBlack
functions.description: Checks whether the color is (close to) black. The exact threshold or comparison method is not provided in the header; likely tests whether RGB components are zero or near zero. Alpha handling is unspecified.
requirements: C++ only: aiColor4t is available when compiling as C++.
Exact tolerance/threshold is unknown; do not rely on a specific epsilon without checking the implementation.

The object must be a valid, initialized aiColor4t<TReal>.

functions.description: Compares two colors for component-wise inequality (true if any of r,g,b,a differ).
requirements: other must reference a valid aiColor4t<TReal> object.

functions.signature: template <typename TReal> bool aiColor4t<TReal>::operator<(const aiColor4t<TReal>& other) const
functions.description: Provides a strict weak ordering by lexicographically comparing r, then g, then b, then a.
requirements: other must reference a valid aiColor4t<TReal> object.

functions.name: aiTextureTypeToString

functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for a given aiTextureType value. Use when inspecting or logging material texture semantics.
