functions.name: aiMaterial::aiMaterial
functions.description: Default constructor for aiMaterial. Initializes an empty material with no properties.

functions.name: aiMaterial::~aiMaterial
functions.description: Destructor for aiMaterial. Releases internal storage for material properties.
requirements: All pointers previously returned that reference internal property buffers become invalid after destruction.

functions.name: aiMaterial::GetName
functions.description: Returns the material's name as an aiString.

functions.name: aiMaterial::Get
functions.signature: template <typename Type> aiReturn aiMaterial::Get(const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int idx, Type* pOut, unsigned int* pMax) const;
functions.description: Retrieves an array of values of arbitrary Type for a specific material key into a caller-provided buffer. Intended to query AI_MATKEY_XXX properties by key/type/index.
requirements: pKey must be a valid key string, typically one of the AI_MATKEY_XXX macros.
type and idx must match the semantic and index as defined/used by the key (often provided by AI_MATKEY_XXX).
pOut must point to a buffer large enough to hold up to *pMax items of Type when pMax is non-null.
If pMax is non-null on input, it specifies the capacity (in number of Type items); on return it receives the number of values written.
If the key is not found, the function returns an error (aiReturn != AI_SUCCESS) and the output buffer remains unmodified; if pMax is provided, it is set to 0.

Only types compatible with the stored property type can be requested; implicit conversions are performed by the material system for numeric types as documented in comments (float/integer conversions).

functions.name: aiMaterial::GetTextureCount
functions.description: Returns the number of textures present in the material for the specified aiTextureType.
requirements: type must be a valid aiTextureType.

functions.name: aiMaterial::GetTexture
functions.signature: aiReturn aiMaterial::GetTexture(aiTextureType type, unsigned int index, C_STRUCT aiString* path, aiTextureMapping* mapping = NULL, unsigned int* uvindex = NULL, ai_real* blend = NULL, aiTextureOp* op = NULL, aiTextureMapMode* mapmode = NULL) const;
functions.description: Convenience helper that retrieves all common parameters for a specific texture slot (by type and index): the path, mapping, UV source index, blend factor, texture operation, and mapping modes.
requirements: index must be less than GetTextureCount(type).
path may be NULL in this C++ method variant; if non-null, it receives the texture path or an embedded-texture key (a '*' followed by the numeric id).
If provided, mapmode must point to an array that can hold 3 aiTextureMapMode values (UVW/XYZ order) as documented.
All optional output pointers (mapping, uvindex, blend, op, mapmode) may be NULL if the caller is not interested.
Returns AI_SUCCESS on success; otherwise outputs are left unmodified.

functions.name: aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty
functions.signature: aiReturn aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty(const void* pInput, unsigned int pSizeInBytes, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, aiPropertyTypeInfo pType);
functions.description: Adds a raw binary property to the material under the given key, with explicit size and type information. Use when adding arbitrary-typed data blobs.
requirements: pInput must point to a buffer of at least pSizeInBytes bytes; the data will be copied into the material.
pSizeInBytes must be > 0.
pKey must be a valid key string (typically an AI_MATKEY_XXX).
type and index must be set consistently with how the key is defined (usually via AI_MATKEY_XXX).
pType must describe the layout of the data for internal checks and conversions.

functions.name: aiMaterial::AddProperty
functions.signature: aiReturn aiMaterial::AddProperty(const aiString* pInput, const char* pKey, unsigned int type = 0, unsigned int index = 0);
functions.description: Adds a string property to the material under the given key.
requirements: pInput must be a valid pointer to an aiString; its contents are copied.
pKey must be a valid key string.
type and index must correspond to the intended usage (per AI_MATKEY_XXX where applicable).

functions.name: aiMaterial::RemoveProperty
functions.signature: aiReturn aiMaterial::RemoveProperty(const char* pKey, unsigned int type = 0, unsigned int index = 0);
functions.description: Removes the property designated by key/type/index from the material, if present.
requirements: pKey must be a valid key string.
type and index must match the property to remove.
Function fails (aiReturn != AI_SUCCESS) if the key is not found.

functions.name: aiMaterial::Clear
functions.description: Removes all properties from the material, leaving the internal array allocated for fast subsequent additions.

functions.name: aiMaterial::CopyPropertyList
functions.signature: static void aiMaterial::CopyPropertyList(aiMaterial* pcDest, const aiMaterial* pcSrc);
functions.description: Static helper to copy the entire property list from pcSrc to pcDest.
requirements: pcDest must be a valid, initialized aiMaterial pointer.
pcSrc must be a valid aiMaterial pointer.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialProperty
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialProperty(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, const aiMaterialProperty** pPropOut);
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to an aiMaterialProperty matching key/type/index from the material.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string.
pPropOut may be non-null to receive the property pointer; on failure, it receives NULL.
On success, *pPropOut points to internal storage owned by the material; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialFloatArray
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialFloatArray(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, ai_real* pOut, unsigned int* pMax);
functions.description: Retrieves an array of floating-point values for the specified key into a caller-provided buffer. pMax supplies capacity (in elements) and receives the number of values written.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string (typically AI_MATKEY_XXX).
pOut must point to storage for at least *pMax ai_real values when pMax is non-null.
If the key is not found, the function returns an error, leaves pOut unmodified, and sets *pMax to 0 when pMax is non-null.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialFloat
functions.signature: static inline aiReturn aiGetMaterialFloat(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, ai_real* pOut);
functions.description: Retrieves a single floating-point material property value. Thin wrapper over aiGetMaterialFloatArray that passes NULL for pMax.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string.
pOut must be non-null.
On failure the output float remains unmodified.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialIntegerArray
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialIntegerArray(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, int* pOut, unsigned int* pMax);
functions.description: Retrieves an array of integer values for the specified key into a caller-provided buffer. pMax supplies capacity (in elements) and receives the number of values written.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string.
pOut must point to storage for at least *pMax int values when pMax is non-null.
If the key is not found, the function returns an error, leaves pOut unmodified, and sets *pMax to 0 when pMax is non-null.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialInteger
functions.signature: static inline aiReturn aiGetMaterialInteger(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, int* pOut);
functions.description: Retrieves a single integer material property value. Thin wrapper over aiGetMaterialIntegerArray that passes NULL for pMax.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string.
pOut must be non-null.
On failure the output integer remains unmodified.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialColor
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialColor(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, aiColor4D* pOut);
functions.description: Retrieves a color value (RGBA) for the specified key into pOut.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must be a valid key string for a color property.
pOut must be non-null.
On failure pOut remains unmodified.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialUVTransform
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialUVTransform(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, aiUVTransform* pOut);
functions.description: Retrieves an aiUVTransform for the specified key into pOut.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must refer to a UV transform property.
pOut must be non-null.
On failure pOut remains unmodified.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialString
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialString(const aiMaterial* pMat, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index, aiString* pOut);
functions.description: Retrieves a string value for the specified key into pOut.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
pKey must refer to a string property.
pOut must be non-null.
On failure pOut remains unmodified.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialTextureCount
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API unsigned int aiGetMaterialTextureCount(const aiMaterial* pMat, aiTextureType type);
functions.description: Returns the number of textures of the given type on the material.
requirements: pMat must be non-null.
type must be a valid aiTextureType.

functions.name: aiGetMaterialTexture
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiGetMaterialTexture(const aiMaterial* mat, aiTextureType type, unsigned int index, aiString* path, aiTextureMapping* mapping = NULL, unsigned int* uvindex = NULL, ai_real* blend = NULL, aiTextureOp* op = NULL, aiTextureMapMode* mapmode = NULL, unsigned int* flags = NULL);
functions.description: Convenience function to retrieve a texture slot’s common parameters from a C material interface: path (or embedded key), mapping, UV channel index, blend factor, texture operation, mapping modes, and texture flags.
requirements: mat must be non-null.
index must be less than aiGetMaterialTextureCount(mat, type).
path must be non-null; on success receives a path or an embedded-texture key ('*' followed by the numeric id).
Optional outputs (mapping, uvindex, blend, op, mapmode, flags) may be NULL if not needed.
If mapmode is provided, it must point to an array capable of holding two aiTextureMapMode values (UV order) as documented in this C variant.
Returns AI_SUCCESS on success; otherwise outputs are left unmodified.

functions.name: ai_real_to_property_type_info
functions.description: Maps a float ai_real value to the corresponding aiPropertyTypeInfo enumeration (aiPTI_Float). Used internally to select the correct material property storage type when adding properties involving ai_real-based types.
requirements: Input is a float value; no additional constraints.
Intended for dispatching/storage typing; does not modify state; pure mapping function.

functions.name: aiMaterial::GetTexture
functions.signature: aiReturn aiMaterial::GetTexture(aiTextureType type, unsigned int index, C_STRUCT aiString* path, aiTextureMapping* mapping /*= NULL*/, unsigned int* uvindex /*= NULL*/, ai_real* blend /*= NULL*/, aiTextureOp* op /*= NULL*/, aiTextureMapMode* mapmode /*= NULL*/) const;
functions.description: Retrieves a texture entry from the material for a given texture type and index. Fills out the provided path (required) and optionally mapping, UV channel index, blend factor, operation, and mapping mode. This is a thin C++ wrapper over aiGetMaterialTexture.
requirements: path must be a valid, non-null pointer to aiString to receive the texture path.
mapping, uvindex, blend, op, and mapmode may be NULL; when non-null they must point to valid writable storage for a single value of their respective types.
index should refer to an existing texture slot for the given type (typically 0 <= index < GetTextureCount(type)); out-of-range indices will cause a failure return.
Check the returned aiReturn; only AI_SUCCESS indicates outputs are valid.

functions.name: aiMaterial::GetTextureCount
functions.description: Returns the number of textures of the specified aiTextureType attached to this material. Wrapper over aiGetMaterialTextureCount.
requirements: type must be a valid aiTextureType value.

functions.name: aiMaterial::Get
functions.signature: template <typename Type> aiReturn aiMaterial::Get(const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int idx, Type* pOut, unsigned int* pMax) const;
functions.description: Generic getter that reads a raw material property addressed by (pKey, type, idx) into a caller-provided buffer. Expects the underlying property to be stored as a raw buffer (aiPTI_Buffer). Copies up to min(*pMax, available) elements of Type.
requirements: pKey must be a valid, non-null C-string key identifying the material property.
pOut must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for at least the number of elements indicated (see pMax).
If pMax is non-null on input, *pMax specifies the maximum number of Type elements to read; on success it is updated to the number of elements actually written.
The addressed property must exist and have mType == aiPTI_Buffer and mDataLength >= sizeof(Type) for at least one element; otherwise AI_FAILURE is returned.
Caller must check the returned aiReturn before using outputs.

functions.name: aiMaterial::AddProperty
functions.signature: template <class TYPE> aiReturn aiMaterial::AddProperty(const TYPE* pInput, const unsigned int pNumValues, const char* pKey, unsigned int type, unsigned int index);
functions.description: Adds a material property with arbitrary raw data (buffer) to the material, addressed by (pKey, type, index). The data is treated as a generic buffer (aiPTI_Buffer).
requirements: pInput must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least pNumValues elements of TYPE (or to pNumValues*sizeof(TYPE) bytes).
pNumValues specifies the element count; it may be zero to add an empty buffer (behavior depends on AddBinaryProperty).
pKey must be a valid, non-null C-string identifying the property.
type and index select the property namespace and occurrence; they must match how the property will be queried.
Caller must check aiReturn for success.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator*=
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator*=(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m);
functions.description: In-place 3x3 matrix multiplication. Multiplies this matrix by m (this = this * m) and returns a reference to this. Use to compose transformations without creating a temporary matrix.
requirements: This object (the left-hand side) must be a valid, initialized aiMatrix3x3t instance.
Argument m must be a valid aiMatrix3x3t with the same scalar type TReal.
No specific range or state constraints are documented beyond normal 3x3 matrix multiplication semantics.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator*
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator*(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m) const;
functions.description: Returns the product of this 3x3 matrix and m (this * m) as a new matrix. Does not modify either operand.
requirements: Both operands must be valid, initialized aiMatrix3x3t instances with the same scalar type TReal.
No additional documented constraints.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator[]
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
TReal* aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator[](unsigned int p_iIndex);
functions.description: Row access operator (mutable). Returns a pointer to the first element of the specified row to allow element indexing like m[row][col]. The matrix is row-major.
requirements: p_iIndex must refer to a valid row index. Inferred from 3x3 layout: valid indices are 0, 1, or 2. Behavior for out-of-range indices is undefined.
The returned pointer is valid as long as the matrix object remains alive and unmodified in ways that would invalidate references.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator[]
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
const TReal* aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator[](unsigned int p_iIndex) const;
functions.description: Row access operator (const). Returns a const pointer to the first element of the specified row for read-only element access like m[row][col]. The matrix is row-major.
requirements: p_iIndex must refer to a valid row index. Inferred from 3x3 layout: valid indices are 0, 1, or 2. Behavior for out-of-range indices is undefined.
The returned pointer remains valid while the matrix object is alive.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator==
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
bool aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator==(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m) const;
functions.description: Element-wise equality comparison of two 3x3 matrices. Returns true if all corresponding elements compare equal.
requirements: Both matrices must be valid aiMatrix3x3t instances of the same scalar type TReal.
Floating-point comparisons may be exact; no epsilon is applied by this operator (use Equal for tolerant comparison).

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator!=
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
bool aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator!=(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m) const;
functions.description: Element-wise inequality comparison of two 3x3 matrices. Returns true if any corresponding elements differ.
requirements: Both matrices must be valid aiMatrix3x3t instances of the same scalar type TReal.
Floating-point comparisons may be exact; no epsilon is applied by this operator (use Equal for tolerant comparison).

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Equal
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
bool aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::Equal(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m, TReal epsilon = ai_epsilon) const;
functions.description: Approximate equality check with tolerance. Returns true if this and m are equal within the given epsilon tolerance per element.
requirements: Both matrices must be valid aiMatrix3x3t instances of the same scalar type TReal.
epsilon is a tolerance value; no explicit constraints are documented.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator aiMatrix3x3t
functions.description: Conversion operator that produces a new aiMatrix3x3t with a different scalar type (e.g., float to double). Each element is converted to TOther.
requirements: TOther must be constructible from TReal without throwing or with acceptable conversion semantics.
Resulting precision/overflow behavior depends on the TReal -> TOther conversion.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::aiMatrix3x3t
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
explicit aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>(const aiMatrix4x4t<TReal>& pMatrix);
functions.description: Constructs a 3x3 matrix from the upper-left 3x3 portion of a 4x4 matrix. The remaining parts of the 4x4 are ignored.
requirements: pMatrix must be a valid aiMatrix4x4t with the same scalar type TReal.
Only the 3x3 submatrix is used; translation/projection components of pMatrix are ignored.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Transpose
functions.description: Transposes the matrix in place and returns a reference to this matrix.
requirements: This object must be a valid, initialized aiMatrix3x3t.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Inverse
functions.description: Inverts the matrix in place. If the matrix is not invertible, all elements are set to qnan. Use (f != f) to check whether a TReal f is qnan.
requirements: This object must be a valid, initialized aiMatrix3x3t.
Callers should handle the non-invertible case by checking for qnan as documented.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Determinant
functions.description: Computes and returns the determinant of the 3x3 matrix.
requirements: This object must be a valid, initialized aiMatrix3x3t.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::RotationZ
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
static aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::RotationZ(TReal a, aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& out);
functions.description: Generates a rotation matrix for a rotation around the Z axis by angle a (in radians) and writes it to out. Returns out.
requirements: Parameter a is an angle in radians (as documented).
out must be a valid reference to an aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> to receive the result.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Rotation
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
static aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::Rotation(TReal a, const aiVector3t<TReal>& axis, aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& out);
functions.description: Generates a rotation matrix for a rotation by angle a (in radians) around the given axis and writes it to out. Returns out.
requirements: Parameter a is an angle in radians (as documented).
axis must be a valid aiVector3t<TReal>. No normalization requirement is documented.
out must be a valid reference to an aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> to receive the result.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::Translation
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
static aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::Translation(const aiVector2t<TReal>& v, aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& out);
functions.description: Generates a 2D translation matrix embedded in 3x3 form using the translation vector v and writes it to out. Returns out.
requirements: v must be a valid aiVector2t<TReal>.
out must be a valid reference to an aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> to receive the result.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::FromToMatrix
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
static aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::FromToMatrix(const aiVector3t<TReal>& from, const aiVector3t<TReal>& to, aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& out);
functions.description: Builds a rotation matrix that rotates vector from into vector to. Based on Möller and Hughes (1999).
requirements: from must be a normalized, non-zero vector (explicitly documented).
to must be a normalized, non-zero vector (explicitly documented).
out must be a valid reference to an aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> to receive the result.
The output is described as a 3x3 matrix in column-major form in the comment, while the class stores row-major; callers should be aware of this note.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::aiMatrix3x3t
functions.description: Constructs a 3x3 matrix from the upper-left 3x3 block of a 4x4 matrix. The remaining parts of the 4x4 matrix are ignored. Useful for extracting rotation/scale from a homogeneous 4x4 transform.
requirements: pMatrix must be a valid, initialized aiMatrix4x4t<TReal> instance.
Only the a1..a3, b1..b3, c1..c3 fields of pMatrix are read; translation/last row/column are ignored.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator*=
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator*=(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m)
functions.description: In-place matrix-by-matrix multiplication. Updates this matrix with the product of the current matrix and m (as implemented).
requirements: Both matrices must be initialized before use.
Result overwrites the left-hand side matrix.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator aiMatrix3x3t
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
template <typename TOther>
aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator aiMatrix3x3t<TOther>() const
functions.description: Implicit/explicit templated conversion operator that produces a matrix of the same shape with each element cast to TOther. Useful for changing scalar precision (e.g., float to double).
requirements: TOther must be a type that can be statically cast from TReal.
Conversion may lose precision or overflow depending on TOther; callers should ensure ranges are appropriate.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator*
functions.signature:
template <typename TReal>
aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>::operator*(const aiMatrix3x3t<TReal>& m) const
functions.description: Returns the matrix product of this matrix with m, leaving the operands unmodified. Implemented via a temporary and operator*=.
requirements: Both operands must be initialized before use.

functions.name: aiMatrix3x3t::operator[]
functions.signature:

No preconditions on inputs.

functions.name: aiBone::copyVertexWeights
functions.description: Utility used by aiBone copy operations to deep-copy the vertex weights array from another aiBone. Allocates a new mWeights array sized to other.mNumWeights and memcpy’s the contents; or clears weights if the source is empty.
requirements: If other.mWeights is nullptr or other.mNumWeights == 0, the destination’s mWeights is set to nullptr and mNumWeights to 0.
If destination already has mWeights, it is deleted before allocation.

Do not call with &other == this; doing so would delete this->mWeights and then read from other.mWeights (dangling) causing undefined behavior. This function is designed for internal use where self-assignment is guarded beforehand.

functions.name: aiBone::operator=
functions.description: Assignment operator that deep-copies name, weight count, offset matrix, and the vertex weights array from another aiBone. Existing destination weights are released and replaced.
requirements: If this == &other, returns immediately.
mArmature and mNode pointers are not copied/assigned (remain unchanged or null per configuration); only mName, mNumWeights, mOffsetMatrix, and mWeights are updated.
After assignment, destination owns its mWeights array and will delete[] it in the destructor.

functions.name: aiBone::operator==
functions.description: Compares two aiBone instances by name, weight count, and all vertex weights. Returns true only if mName, mNumWeights, and every element of mWeights are equal.
requirements: Assumes both bones’ mWeights arrays have at least mNumWeights entries when mNumWeights > 0.
Does not compare mOffsetMatrix, mArmature, or mNode; equality is strictly by name and weights.

functions.name: aiAnimMesh::HasPositions
functions.description: Returns true if this animation mesh overrides the host mesh’s vertex positions (i.e., mVertices != nullptr).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.
True implies the array length matches mNumVertices per the struct’s contract.

functions.name: aiAnimMesh::HasNormals
functions.description: Returns true if this animation mesh overrides the host mesh’s normals (i.e., mNormals != nullptr).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.

functions.name: aiAnimMesh::HasTangentsAndBitangents
functions.description: Returns true if this animation mesh overrides tangents (and implicitly bitangents) of the host mesh (i.e., mTangents != nullptr).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.
Per documentation, tangents and bitangents always go together.

functions.name: aiAnimMesh::HasVertexColors
functions.description: Checks whether this anim mesh overrides the specified vertex color set of its host mesh.
requirements: pIndex must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_COLOR_SETS to be considered; if pIndex >= AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_COLOR_SETS the function returns false.
True indicates mColors[pIndex] != nullptr and the array is expected to have mNumVertices elements.

functions.name: aiAnimMesh::HasTextureCoords
functions.description: Checks whether this anim mesh overrides the specified texture coordinate set (UV) of its host mesh.
requirements: pIndex must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS; if pIndex >= AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS the function returns false.
True indicates mTextureCoords[pIndex] != nullptr and the array is expected to have mNumVertices elements.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasPositions
functions.description: Returns true if the mesh has vertex positions and a non-zero vertex count (mVertices != nullptr && mNumVertices > 0).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.
In typical scenes, positions should be present unless AI_SCENE_FLAGS_INCOMPLETE is set.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasFaces
functions.description: Returns true if the mesh has faces and a non-zero face count (mFaces != nullptr && mNumFaces > 0).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasNormals
functions.description: Returns true if the mesh has vertex normals and a non-zero vertex count (mNormals != nullptr && mNumVertices > 0).
requirements: Normals may be undefined for point/line-only meshes; presence does not guarantee meaningful values for those primitives.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasTangentsAndBitangents
functions.description: Returns true if both tangents and bitangents exist and there is at least one vertex (mTangents != nullptr && mBitangents != nullptr && mNumVertices > 0).
requirements: Tangents and bitangents are expected to be present together; the function enforces both be non-null.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasVertexColors
functions.description: Checks whether the mesh contains a vertex color set at the given index.
requirements: index must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_COLOR_SETS; otherwise returns false.
True indicates mColors[index] != nullptr and mNumVertices > 0.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasTextureCoords
functions.description: Checks whether the mesh contains a texture coordinate (UV) set at the given index.
requirements: index must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS; otherwise returns false.
True indicates mTextureCoords[index] != nullptr and mNumVertices > 0.

functions.name: aiMesh::GetNumUVChannels
functions.description: Counts and returns the number of UV channels with non-null pointers in mTextureCoords[0..AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS-1].
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.
Counts channels purely by non-null pointers, not by mNumUVComponents values.

functions.name: aiMesh::GetNumColorChannels
functions.description: Returns the number of contiguous vertex color channels starting from index 0 where mColors[n] is non-null. Stops counting at the first null.
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.
Only counts leading contiguous channels; non-contiguous later channels are not included by this implementation.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasBones
functions.description: Returns true if the mesh has a non-null bone array and a non-zero bone count (mBones != nullptr && mNumBones > 0).
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call anytime.

functions.name: aiMesh::HasTextureCoordsName
functions.description: Checks whether a name is assigned to the UV set at the given index (mTextureCoordsNames exists and mTextureCoordsNames[pIndex] != nullptr).
requirements: pIndex must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS; otherwise returns false.
mTextureCoordsNames may be nullptr if no names were ever set; in that case returns false.

functions.name: aiMesh::SetTextureCoordsName
functions.signature: void aiMesh::SetTextureCoordsName(unsigned int pIndex, const aiString &texCoordsName)
functions.description: Assigns or clears the name for the UV set at pIndex. Lazily allocates the mTextureCoordsNames array if needed. Passing an empty name clears the entry at pIndex.
requirements: If pIndex >= AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS the function returns without making changes (no-op).
If mTextureCoordsNames is nullptr, the function allocates an array of size AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS and initializes entries to nullptr.
If texCoordsName.length == 0, the existing name at pIndex (if any) is deleted and the entry set to nullptr.
On set, ownership of the stored name is internal; caller retains its texCoordsName object.

functions.name: aiMesh::GetTextureCoordsName
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the name of the UV set at the given index, or nullptr if not set or out of range.
requirements: index must be less than AI_MAX_NUMBER_OF_TEXTURECOORDS; otherwise returns nullptr.

mTextureCoordsNames must be non-null and the entry non-null to return a valid pointer. The returned pointer is owned by the mesh and remains valid until modified or the mesh is destroyed; do not free it.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes the quaternion to the identity rotation (w=1, x=y=z=0). Use when you need a neutral rotation or a known initial state.
requirements: No arguments required.
Constructed quaternion represents identity; safe to use immediately.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.signature: aiQuaterniont<TReal>::aiQuaterniont(TReal pw, TReal px, TReal py, TReal pz)
functions.description: Constructs a quaternion from its scalar (w) and vector (x,y,z) components. Use when you already have component values.
requirements: Caller must supply values of type TReal for all four components.
No normalization is performed by the constructor; if a unit quaternion is required, caller should normalize explicitly.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.description: Constructs a quaternion from a 3x3 rotation matrix. Intended to convert an orthonormal rotation matrix into a quaternion representation.
requirements: pRotMatrix is expected to be an orthonormal rotation matrix; the result is undefined otherwise (per comment).
Input must be a 3x3 matrix of the same TReal type.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.signature: aiQuaterniont<TReal>::aiQuaterniont(TReal roty, TReal rotz, TReal rotx)
functions.description: Constructs a quaternion from Euler angles. The parameters are labeled roty, rotz, rotx, indicating the order/significance of the angles used by this constructor. Exact convention (order, units) is not documented here; typical usage is to supply angles matching the library’s expectations.
requirements: Caller must provide three angles of type TReal.
Angle units and rotation order are not specified in this header; callers must ensure they match the implementation’s expectations (unknown in this context).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.description: Constructs a quaternion from an axis-angle pair. Creates a rotation of magnitude 'angle' about the given 'axis'.
requirements: Caller must supply an axis vector and an angle of type TReal.
Whether the axis must be normalized is not specified; if a unit rotation is required, the caller should ensure axis normalization or verify the implementation’s behavior (unknown here).
Angle units are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::GetMatrix
functions.description: Returns the 3x3 rotation matrix representation of this quaternion.
requirements: For a pure rotation matrix, the quaternion should be normalized; not enforced here, but non-unit quaternions may yield scaled/sheared matrices (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator==
functions.description: Exact equality comparison of two quaternions' components. Useful for checks where bitwise equality is acceptable.
requirements: Performs exact component-wise equality; no tolerance is applied. Use Equal() for epsilon-based comparison if needed.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator!=
functions.description: Exact inequality comparison of two quaternions' components. Logical negation of operator==.
requirements: Performs exact component-wise inequality; no tolerance is applied.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator*=
functions.description: Applies a 4x4 matrix transformation to this quaternion in place. Comment indicates vector-by-matrix transform, but here it updates the quaternion using the matrix. Exact semantics depend on implementation (e.g., transforming orientation by a transform matrix).
requirements: Input must be a 4x4 matrix of the same TReal type.
Behavior with non-rotation/shear/scaling matrices is unspecified in this header (unknown).
Result overwrites the current quaternion.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Equal
functions.signature: bool aiQuaterniont<TReal>::Equal(const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& o, TReal epsilon = ai_epsilon) const
functions.description: Returns true if this quaternion and 'o' are approximately equal within the given epsilon tolerance. Useful for floating-point comparisons.
requirements: epsilon should be non-negative; default is ai_epsilon.
Approximate comparison semantics (e.g., component-wise vs. norm) are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Normalize
functions.description: Normalizes this quaternion to unit length in place, making it suitable for representing pure rotations.
requirements: Behavior for zero-length or near-zero-length quaternions is not specified here; callers should avoid normalizing a zero quaternion (unknown handling).
Modifies the object in place and returns a reference to it.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Conjugate
functions.description: Replaces this quaternion with its conjugate (negates the vector part, keeps the scalar part). Useful for inverting unit quaternions or computing inverse rotations when normalized.
requirements: For the conjugate to represent the inverse rotation, the quaternion should be normalized; not enforced here.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Rotate
functions.description: Rotates a 3D point/vector by this quaternion and returns the rotated vector.
requirements: Input is a 3D vector of type TReal.
For a proper rotation (without scaling), this quaternion should be normalized; not enforced here.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator*
functions.description: Multiplies this quaternion by another, returning the composed rotation. The multiplication order corresponds to the class’s operator* definition (implementation-dependent).
requirements: Operand 'two' must be a quaternion of the same TReal type.
If using for rotation composition, both quaternions should be normalized for best results; not enforced here.
Be aware of multiplication order conventions when composing rotations (unspecified here).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Interpolate
functions.signature: static void aiQuaterniont<TReal>::Interpolate(aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pOut, const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pStart, const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pEnd, TReal pFactor)
functions.description: Performs spherical interpolation (slerp) between pStart and pEnd and writes the result into pOut.
requirements: pFactor is expected to be in [0, 1]; values outside this range yield undefined results (per comment).
pOut must be a valid reference to receive the result.
Input quaternions are typically expected to represent rotations (ideally normalized), though not enforced here.

functions.name: operator*
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> aiQuaterniont<TReal> operator*(const aiMatrix4x4t<TReal>& pMatrix, const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pQuaternion)
functions.description: Transforms a quaternion treated as a 4D vector by a 4x4 matrix and returns the resulting quaternion (component-wise multiplication with the matrix rows). Intended for cases where a quaternion is embedded in homogeneous space, not for combining rotations.
requirements: Template type parameters for aiMatrix4x4t<TReal> and aiQuaterniont<TReal> must match (same TReal).
No explicit range constraints; inputs are used directly without validation.
Result represents a linear transform of (x,y,z,w); this is not quaternion multiplication (caller should not use this to compose rotations).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator==
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> bool aiQuaterniont<TReal>::operator==(const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& o) const
functions.description: Exact component-wise equality comparison between two quaternions. Returns true only if x, y, z, and w are all exactly equal.
requirements: Both quaternions must share the same template parameter TReal.
Comparison is exact (no epsilon); floating-point round-off will cause inequality.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator!=
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> bool aiQuaterniont<TReal>::operator!=(const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& o) const
functions.description: Logical negation of operator==. Returns true if any component differs.
requirements: Both quaternions must share the same template parameter TReal.
Relies on exact component-wise comparison semantics of operator==.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator*=
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> aiQuaterniont<TReal>& aiQuaterniont<TReal>::operator*=(const aiMatrix4x4t<TReal>& mat)
functions.description: Transforms this quaternion (treated as a 4D vector) by a 4x4 matrix in place. Equivalent to *this = mat * (*this).
requirements: Template type parameters for aiMatrix4x4t<TReal> and aiQuaterniont<TReal> must match (same TReal).
This performs linear 4D transformation, not quaternion rotation composition.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Equal
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> bool aiQuaterniont<TReal>::Equal(const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& o, TReal epsilon) const
functions.description: Approximate component-wise equality check using an absolute tolerance epsilon for each component.
requirements: epsilon should be non-negative (inferred); negative values invert the intended tolerance semantics.
Both quaternions must share the same template parameter TReal.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::aiQuaterniont
functions.description: Constructs a quaternion from a 3x3 rotation matrix using a branch-stable algorithm based on the matrix trace and diagonal dominance.
requirements: pRotMatrix is expected to represent a valid rotation matrix (orthonormal with determinant +1) to avoid numerical issues (inferred).
Template parameters for aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> and aiQuaterniont<TReal> must match (same TReal).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::GetMatrix
functions.description: Returns the 3x3 rotation matrix corresponding to this quaternion using the standard quaternion-to-matrix formula.
requirements: For the result to be a proper rotation matrix, the quaternion should be normalized beforehand (inferred).
Template parameters for aiMatrix3x3t<TReal> and aiQuaterniont<TReal> must match (same TReal).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Interpolate
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> static void aiQuaterniont<TReal>::Interpolate(aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pOut, const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pStart, const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& pEnd, TReal pFactor)
functions.description: Performs spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) between pStart and pEnd at parameter pFactor and writes the result to pOut. Falls back to linear interpolation when the quaternions are nearly identical.
requirements: pFactor in [0,1] for standard interpolation; values outside this range extrapolate (inferred).
For pure rotational interpolation, pStart and pEnd should be normalized (inferred).
pOut may alias pStart or pEnd; the implementation does not read from pOut before writing.
All operands must share the same template parameter TReal.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Normalize
functions.description: Normalizes the quaternion in place to unit length if magnitude is non-zero. If the magnitude is zero, the quaternion is left unchanged.
requirements: No preconditions; if all components are zero, the quaternion remains unchanged.
Caller should ensure non-zero magnitude when unit quaternions are required (inferred).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::operator*
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> aiQuaterniont<TReal> aiQuaterniont<TReal>::operator*(const aiQuaterniont<TReal>& t) const
functions.description: Quaternion multiplication (Hamilton product). Useful for composing rotations: result represents applying this rotation followed by t (per implementation order).
requirements: Both operands must share the same template parameter TReal.
For rotation composition without scaling, operands should be normalized (inferred).

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Conjugate
functions.description: Conjugates the quaternion in place by negating the vector part (x, y, z), leaving w unchanged.
requirements: No preconditions. For unit quaternions, conjugate equals inverse.

functions.name: aiQuaterniont::Rotate
functions.signature: template <typename TReal> aiVector3t<TReal> aiQuaterniont<TReal>::Rotate(const aiVector3t<TReal>& v) const
functions.description: Rotates a 3D vector by this quaternion using q * (0,v) * q^{-1} (with q^{-1} implemented as conjugate). Returns the rotated vector’s components from the resulting quaternion.
requirements: For a pure rotation (no scaling), this quaternion should be normalized (inferred).
The input vector v can be any finite 3D vector.
Template parameters for aiVector3t<TReal> and aiQuaterniont<TReal> must match (same TReal).

functions.name: aiNode::aiNode
functions.description: Default constructor for aiNode. Initializes a node with empty name, identity transformation, no parent, no children, no meshes, and no metadata (details of initialization are per implementation, but intent is to zero/empty-initialize).
requirements: May be called in C++ context only (constructor).
Resulting object must be destroyed via aiNode::~aiNode or when its owning aiScene is destroyed (as appropriate).

functions.name: aiNode::aiNode
functions.description: Constructs an aiNode with the provided name. Other members are initialized as in the default constructor.
requirements: The name string may be empty; non-ASCII or special characters are allowed.
May be called in C++ context only (constructor).

functions.name: aiNode::~aiNode
functions.description: Destructor for aiNode. Releases resources owned by the node and its members as implemented by Assimp.
requirements: Only destroy nodes you own; nodes from aiScene are typically managed by Assimp.
Do not use the aiNode after destruction.

functions.name: aiNode::FindNode
functions.signature: const aiNode* aiNode::FindNode(const aiString& name) const
functions.description: Searches (starting at this node) for a node with the given name and returns a const pointer to it if found; otherwise returns nullptr. Convenience overload that forwards to the char* version.
requirements: May be called on any valid aiNode pointer.
The search is name-based and may match multiple nodes in a scene hierarchy; this returns the first match found in a depth-first traversal starting at this node (exact ordering not guaranteed).

functions.name: aiNode::FindNode
functions.description: Mutable overload of FindNode. Searches for a node with the given name and returns a non-const pointer if found; nullptr otherwise. Forwards to the char* version.
requirements: May be called on any valid aiNode pointer.
Name matching is exact on aiString contents; multiple identical names can exist; this returns the first match found.

functions.name: aiNode::FindNode
functions.signature: const aiNode* aiNode::FindNode(const char* name) const
functions.description: Searches (starting at this node) for a node whose name equals the provided C-string. Returns a const pointer to the node if found; nullptr otherwise.
requirements: The name pointer should refer to a null-terminated C string; if null or empty, the function will not find a node and should return nullptr (exact handling of null is not documented in this header).
May be called on any valid aiNode pointer.

functions.name: aiNode::FindNode
functions.description: Mutable overload of FindNode taking a C-string. Returns a non-const pointer to the node if found; nullptr otherwise.
requirements: The name pointer should refer to a null-terminated C string; if null or empty, the function will not find a node and should return nullptr (exact handling of null is not documented in this header).
May be called on any valid aiNode pointer.

functions.name: aiNode::addChildren
functions.signature: void aiNode::addChildren(unsigned int numChildren, aiNode** children)
functions.description: Appends new child nodes to this node. The children array contains pointers to the nodes to add.
requirements: children must point to an array of at least numChildren aiNode* entries.
Each pointer in children should be a valid aiNode* (non-null) intended to be attached to this node.
Do not add the same child to multiple parents unless the library explicitly supports shared nodes (not indicated here).
After addition, external code should not assume previous parent pointers of those children remain unchanged.

functions.name: aiScene::aiScene
functions.description: Default constructor for aiScene. Initializes all members to 0/nullptr (empty scene).
requirements: May be called in C++ context only (constructor).
Resulting scene is empty until populated by an importer or by user code.

functions.name: aiScene::~aiScene
functions.description: Destructor for aiScene. Frees resources owned by the scene, including nodes, meshes, materials, animations, textures, lights, cameras, metadata, and skeletons as implemented by Assimp.
requirements: Only destroy aiScene instances you own; scenes returned by Assimp importers are usually destroyed via Assimp API (e.g., aiReleaseImport).
Do not access scene contents after destruction.

functions.name: aiScene::HasMeshes
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one mesh (mMeshes != nullptr and mNumMeshes > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasMaterials
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one material (mMaterials != nullptr and mNumMaterials > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasLights
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one light (mLights != nullptr and mNumLights > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasTextures
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one embedded texture (mTextures != nullptr and mNumTextures > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasCameras
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one camera (mCameras != nullptr and mNumCameras > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasAnimations
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one animation (mAnimations != nullptr and mNumAnimations > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::HasSkeletons
functions.description: Returns true if the scene contains at least one skeleton (mSkeletons != nullptr and mNumSkeletons > 0).
requirements: None beyond having a valid aiScene pointer.

functions.name: aiScene::GetShortFilename
functions.signature: static const char* aiScene::GetShortFilename(const char* filename)
functions.description: Utility to strip a full path and return a pointer to the short filename component after the last path separator ('/' or '\').
requirements: filename must be a non-null, null-terminated C string valid for strrchr and pointer arithmetic.
Returned pointer is into the provided string; the caller must ensure the original buffer remains alive as long as the returned pointer is used.

functions.name: aiScene::GetEmbeddedTexture
functions.signature: const aiTexture* aiScene::GetEmbeddedTexture(const char* filename) const
functions.description: Looks up and returns a pointer to an embedded texture matching the given filename or texture ID reference. If not found, returns nullptr. Convenience wrapper around GetEmbeddedTextureAndIndex.
requirements: filename may be either a short/long filename or an Assimp texture ID string of the form "*<index>" (e.g., "*0").
filename may be null; in that case, the function returns nullptr.
Returned pointer is owned by the aiScene; do not free it.

functions.name: aiScene::GetEmbeddedTextureAndIndex
functions.signature: std::pair<const aiTexture*, int> aiScene::GetEmbeddedTextureAndIndex(const char* filename) const
functions.description: Finds an embedded texture by ID ("*<index>") or by filename (compared using the short filename) and returns a pair of (texture pointer, index). On failure, returns (nullptr, -1).
requirements: filename may be null; if null, returns (nullptr, -1).
When using ID form, index must be within [0, mNumTextures).
When using filename form, comparison is done using short filenames extracted from both inputs.
Returned texture pointer is owned by the aiScene; do not free it.

functions.name: aiScene::findBone
functions.description: Searches all meshes in the scene for a bone whose name matches the given name and returns a pointer to it if found; otherwise nullptr.
requirements: May be called on any valid aiScene pointer.
Name matching is exact on aiString contents; multiple bones with the same name across meshes may exist; this returns the first match encountered in mesh/bone iteration order.

functions.name: GetAiType
functions.description: Returns the aiMetadataType enum value corresponding to a bool. Used to tag aiMetadataEntry values with their runtime type.
requirements: Argument can be any boolean value; it is inspected only for type.
No side effects; purely returns AI_BOOL.

functions.name: aiMetadata::Alloc
functions.description: Allocates an aiMetadata instance with storage for the specified number of properties (keys and values). Initializes all keys and values to defaults.
requirements: numProperties must be greater than 0; if 0, the function returns nullptr.
Caller owns the returned object and must free it using aiMetadata::Dealloc (or delete) when done.
After allocation, the arrays mKeys and mValues are valid and sized to numProperties, but contain default-initialized entries that the caller should fill via Set/Add.

functions.name: aiMetadata::Dealloc
functions.description: Destroys a previously allocated aiMetadata object and releases all owned memory, including any dynamically allocated per-entry data.
requirements: metadata must be a pointer returned by aiMetadata::Alloc or otherwise heap-allocated; passing nullptr is safe (delete on nullptr is a no-op).
Must not use the metadata pointer after deallocation.

functions.name: aiMetadata::Add
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline void aiMetadata::Add(const std::string &key, const T &value)
functions.description: Appends a new key/value pair to the metadata, growing the internal arrays by one and storing a dynamically allocated copy of the value. The entry’s type is recorded using GetAiType(value).
requirements: key must not be empty; empty keys are not allowed.
T must correspond to a supported aiMetadataType (as per available GetAiType overloads: bool, int32_t, uint32_t, int64_t, uint64_t, float, double, aiString, aiVector3D, aiMetadata).
The aiMetadata instance must be valid (constructed) before calling.
On success, mNumProperties increases by 1 and the new entry is placed at the new last index.

functions.name: aiMetadata::Set
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline bool aiMetadata::Set(unsigned index, const std::string &key, const T &value)
functions.description: Sets the key and value at a specific index. Records the value’s runtime type and stores a dynamically allocated copy (or assigns if already allocated). Returns true on success, false on out-of-range index or empty key.
requirements: index must be less than mNumProperties.
key must not be empty.
T must correspond to a supported aiMetadataType (as per GetAiType overloads).
If an existing value object is present, it will be overwritten via memcpy for non-aiMetadata types, assigned for AI_AIMETADATA, or deleted and reallocated as needed.

functions.name: aiMetadata::Get
functions.signature: template <typename T> inline bool aiMetadata::Get(unsigned index, T &value) const
functions.description: Retrieves the value at the specified index into the output parameter if the stored type matches T. Returns true on success, false if the index is out of range or the type does not match.
requirements: index must be less than mNumProperties.
T must match the stored type exactly (GetAiType(value) must equal the entry’s mType).
value must be a valid reference to receive the result.

functions.name: aiMetadata::HasKey
functions.description: Checks whether a metadata entry exists whose key matches the given C-string exactly (using length-limited strncmp with the stored key length).
requirements: key must not be nullptr.
Comparison is performed against each stored key’s length (aiString::length); the input must match exactly to return true.

functions.name: CompareKeys
functions.signature: friend bool CompareKeys(const aiMetadata &lhs, const aiMetadata &rhs)
functions.description: Compares two aiMetadata objects for key equality only (same number of properties and same keys in the same order).
requirements: Both lhs and rhs must be valid aiMetadata objects.

functions.name: CompareValues
functions.signature: friend bool CompareValues(const aiMetadata &lhs, const aiMetadata &rhs)
functions.description: Compares two aiMetadata objects for equality of value types and contents for each property (assumes identical property counts and indices).
requirements: Both lhs and rhs must be valid aiMetadata objects.
Returns false if mNumProperties differs, if any corresponding mType differs, or if any corresponding value differs according to its type.

functions.name: operator==
functions.signature: friend bool operator==(const aiMetadata &lhs, const aiMetadata &rhs)
functions.description: Equality operator for aiMetadata. Returns true only if both keys and values are equal (delegates to CompareKeys and CompareValues).
requirements: Both operands must be valid aiMetadata objects.
Relies on CompareKeys and CompareValues semantics.

functions.name: operator!=
functions.signature: friend bool operator!=(const aiMetadata &lhs, const aiMetadata &rhs)
functions.description: Inequality operator for aiMetadata. Returns the logical negation of operator==.
requirements: Both operands must be valid aiMetadata objects.

functions.name: aiTexel::operator==
functions.description: Compares two aiTexel values for exact component-wise equality (b, r, g, a). Intended for checking if two texels are identical in ARGB8888 byte space.
requirements: other must reference a valid aiTexel object.
No side effects; does not modify either operand.
Equality is strict byte-wise equality on components b, r, g, a.

functions.name: aiTexel::operator!=
functions.description: Inverse of operator==; returns true if any component (b, r, g, a) differs between the two aiTexel values.
requirements: other must reference a valid aiTexel object.
No side effects; does not modify either operand.
Inequality is determined by byte-wise comparison of b, r, g, a.

functions.name: aiTexel::operator aiColor4D
functions.description: Converts this texel from 8-bit-per-channel ARGB8888 to a floating-point aiColor4D with components in [0,1], mapping r,g,b,a by dividing by 255.f. Useful for color computations on normalized floats.
requirements: aiColor4D type must be available (included via assimp/types.h).
No preconditions on component values; conversion always succeeds.

functions.name: aiTexture::CheckFormat
functions.description: Checks whether the embedded texture's format hint matches the given string. For compressed textures (mHeight == 0) this typically checks an extension like "jpg" or "png"; for uncompressed textures it may contain packing info such as "rgba8888".
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
Comparison is performed using strncmp over sizeof(achFormatHint) bytes (up to 9 including terminator); matching is case-sensitive.
For meaningful extension checking, the texture should be compressed (mHeight == 0) and achFormatHint is expected to be a short, lower-case extension without dot (e.g., "jpg").
If mHeight != 0, achFormatHint encodes channel order/bitness (e.g., "rgba8888"); callers should pass comparable strings when using this mode.

functions.name: aiTexture::aiTexture
functions.description: Default constructor for aiTexture. Initializes mWidth and mHeight to 0, pcData to nullptr, clears achFormatHint to all zeros, and default-constructs mFilename. Prepares an empty texture object.
requirements: No arguments or special initialization required.
After construction, if the texture is to own pixel data, pcData should be assigned memory allocated with new[] compatible with delete[] (see destructor).
When representing a compressed texture, set mHeight to 0 and mWidth to the byte size of pcData, and set achFormatHint appropriately (e.g., "jpg\0").

When representing an uncompressed texture, set mWidth and mHeight to pixel dimensions and pcData to an array of mWidth * mHeight aiTexel entries, and set achFormatHint to describe packing if non-default.

functions.name: aiTexture::~aiTexture
functions.description: Destructor for aiTexture. Releases owned pixel buffer by calling delete[] on pcData. Does not free or modify any external resources beyond pcData.
requirements: pcData, if non-null, must have been allocated with new[] and point to a buffer compatible with delete[] (typically aiTexel[mWidth * mHeight] or a byte buffer for compressed data).
Do not manually delete[] pcData before destruction to avoid double-free; ownership is assumed by aiTexture.
After the destructor runs, the aiTexture instance must not be used.
If pcData points to externally managed memory, set it to nullptr before destruction to prevent unintended deletion.

functions.name: Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator new
functions.description: Class-specific operator new allocating memory from Assimp's internal heap. Used to safely share objects across DLL boundaries by ensuring deallocation uses the matching heap.
requirements: num_bytes should be the size of the object being allocated (typically provided by the compiler).
On failure this overload may throw std::bad_alloc (no exception specification is enforced in the declaration).
Objects allocated with this operator must be deallocated with Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator delete for single objects (or the class’s delete invoked implicitly).
Do not mix allocation/deallocation with different heaps or global operators.

functions.name: Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator new[]

requirements: num_bytes should represent the total size for the array allocation (computed by the compiler).
On failure this overload may throw std::bad_alloc (no exception specification is enforced in the declaration).
Arrays allocated with this operator must be deallocated with Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator delete[] (or via delete[] on the class).
Do not mix allocation/deallocation with different heaps or global operators.

functions.name: Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator delete
functions.description: Class-specific operator delete to free memory previously allocated by the corresponding class operator new, using Assimp's internal heap.
requirements: data must be a pointer previously returned by Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator new for a single object of this class or a derived class.
Passing nullptr is permitted (standard delete semantics).
Do not use this to free memory allocated by other allocators or global new.

functions.name: Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator delete[]
functions.description: Class-specific array operator delete to free memory previously allocated by the corresponding class array operator new, using Assimp's internal heap.
requirements: data must be a pointer previously returned by Assimp::Intern::AllocateFromAssimpHeap::operator new[] for an array of this class or a derived class.
Passing nullptr is permitted (standard delete[] semantics).
Do not use this to free memory allocated by other allocators or global new[].

requirements: Modifies the object; callers relying on the original value should copy first.

requirements: mat must be a valid 4x4 matrix.

functions.name: aiGetLegalString
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a static, multi-line C string containing Assimp’s copyright and licensing information. Typical usage: print or embed the returned text in About dialogs or logs. Do not attempt to free or modify the returned string; it is managed by the library.
requirements: Must not attempt to modify or free the returned string (it points to static storage).
The returned pointer is valid for the lifetime of the process unless otherwise documented.
Thread-safety of the returned storage is not stated; callers should treat it as read-only.

functions.name: aiGetVersionPatch
functions.description: Returns the patch version number of the Assimp runtime linked at build/load time. Use together with aiGetVersionMinor/Major to construct the full semantic version.
requirements: No arguments required; can be called at any time after the library is loaded.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the patch component; no specific range guarantees beyond unsigned int.

functions.name: aiGetVersionMinor
functions.description: Returns the minor version number of the Assimp runtime linked at build/load time. Combine with aiGetVersionMajor and aiGetVersionPatch for the full version.
requirements: No arguments required; can be called at any time after the library is loaded.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the minor component; no specific range guarantees beyond unsigned int.

functions.name: aiGetVersionMajor
functions.description: Returns the major version number of the Assimp runtime linked at build/load time. Combine with aiGetVersionMinor and aiGetVersionPatch for the full version.
requirements: No arguments required; can be called at any time after the library is loaded.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the major component; no specific range guarantees beyond unsigned int.

functions.name: aiGetVersionRevision
functions.description: Returns the repository revision of the Assimp runtime the application was linked/built against. Intended primarily for diagnostics and support.
requirements: No arguments required; can be called at any time after the library is loaded.
Return value is an unsigned integer representing the repository revision; semantics beyond that are not specified.

functions.name: aiGetBranchName
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a static C string with the current Assimp branch name used for the runtime. Useful for diagnostics and debugging.
requirements: Must not attempt to modify or free the returned string (it points to static storage).
The returned pointer is expected to remain valid for the life of the process unless otherwise documented.
Content and presence of a branch name may depend on how the library was built; callers should handle empty or null-like strings defensively.

functions.name: aiGetCompileFlags
functions.description: Returns a bitwise combination of ASSIMP_CFLAGS_* indicating how Assimp was compiled (e.g., shared build, debug, single-threaded). Callers should test bits using the defined ASSIMP_CFLAGS_* constants.
requirements: Interpret the returned value by masking with defined ASSIMP_CFLAGS_* constants (ASSIMP_CFLAGS_SHARED, ASSIMP_CFLAGS_STLPORT, ASSIMP_CFLAGS_DEBUG, ASSIMP_CFLAGS_NOBOOST, ASSIMP_CFLAGS_SINGLETHREADED, ASSIMP_CFLAGS_DOUBLE_SUPPORT).
No arguments required; can be called at any time after the library is loaded.
Do not assume undefined bits have meaning; only rely on documented ASSIMP_CFLAGS_* constants.

functions.name: aiImportFile
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiImportFile(const char *pFile, unsigned int pFlags);
functions.description: Reads a model file from disk and returns a read-only aiScene owned by Assimp. Apply optional post-process flags at import time. On failure returns NULL; retrieve details via aiGetErrorString(). Release with aiReleaseImport() when done.
requirements: pFile must be a non-null, null-terminated C string path to the input file.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps; 0 is allowed.
The returned aiScene pointer is read-only and owned by the library until aiReleaseImport() is called.
Call aiReleaseImport(pScene) to free resources when finished.
Do not free or modify pointers inside the returned aiScene.

functions.name: aiImportFileEx
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiImportFileEx(const char *pFile, unsigned int pFlags, C_STRUCT aiFileIO *pFS);
functions.description: Imports a model file using a user-provided aiFileIO for file access. Returns a read-only aiScene on success, or NULL on failure. Errors can be retrieved via aiGetErrorString().
requirements: pFile must be a non-null, null-terminated file path.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps; 0 is allowed.
pFS may be NULL to use Assimp’s default IO; otherwise it must point to a valid aiFileIO implementation (see aiFileIO.h).
Returned aiScene is read-only and owned by the library; free it via aiReleaseImport().

functions.name: aiImportFileExWithProperties
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiImportFileExWithProperties(const char *pFile, unsigned int pFlags, C_STRUCT aiFileIO *pFS, const C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *pProps);
functions.description: Imports a model file using an optional custom IO and a property store of importer settings. Returns a read-only aiScene or NULL on failure.
requirements: pFile must be a non-null, null-terminated path.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps.
pFS may be NULL for default IO; otherwise must be a valid aiFileIO.
pProps may be NULL or a valid aiPropertyStore created with aiCreatePropertyStore and configured with aiSetImportProperty* calls.
Returned aiScene is read-only and must be released with aiReleaseImport().

functions.name: aiImportFileFromMemory
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiImportFileFromMemory(const char *pBuffer, unsigned int pLength, unsigned int pFlags, const char *pHint);
functions.description: Imports a model from a single memory buffer. Optionally provide a file-extension hint to select a loader. Returns a read-only aiScene or NULL on failure. Not suitable for formats that need external files (e.g., OBJ, MD3) unless custom IO is used.
requirements: pBuffer must be non-null and point to pLength bytes of model data.
pLength is the size in bytes of pBuffer and must match the actual buffer length.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps; 0 is allowed.
pHint may be NULL or an optional non-empty extension string (e.g., "obj", ".obj").
Returned aiScene is read-only and must be released with aiReleaseImport().

functions.name: aiImportFileFromMemoryWithProperties
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiImportFileFromMemoryWithProperties(const char *pBuffer, unsigned int pLength, unsigned int pFlags, const char *pHint, const C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *pProps);
functions.description: Imports a model from memory with optional extension hint and a property store of importer settings. Returns a read-only aiScene or NULL on failure.
requirements: pBuffer must be non-null; pLength must be the buffer size in bytes.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps.
pHint may be NULL or a loader extension hint string.
pProps may be NULL or a valid aiPropertyStore created/configured via aiCreatePropertyStore and aiSetImportProperty* APIs.
Returned aiScene is read-only and must be released with aiReleaseImport().

functions.name: aiApplyPostProcessing
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiScene *aiApplyPostProcessing(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pScene, unsigned int pFlags);
functions.description: Applies Assimp post-processing steps to an already imported scene. Operates in-place and returns the (same) scene pointer, or NULL if a step invalidates the scene (e.g., aiProcess_ValidateDataStructure).
requirements: pScene must be a valid aiScene previously returned by an Assimp import call.
pFlags is a bitwise OR of aiPostProcessSteps.
Caller must handle the case that the returned pointer can be NULL if processing fails.

functions.name: aiGetPredefinedLogStream
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API C_STRUCT aiLogStream aiGetPredefinedLogStream(C_ENUM aiDefaultLogStream pStreams, const char *file);
functions.description: Returns a predefined log stream descriptor for convenient logging (e.g., to file or stdout). If creation fails, the callback in the returned aiLogStream is NULL.
requirements: pStreams must be one of aiDefaultLogStream values.
If pStreams == aiDefaultLogStream_FILE, file must be a valid path (non-null). For other stream types, pass file == NULL.
Check the returned aiLogStream.callback for NULL before attaching.

functions.name: aiAttachLogStream
functions.description: Attaches a custom or predefined log stream to Assimp’s logging system. Multiple streams can be attached. May slightly reduce import performance.
requirements: stream must be a non-null pointer to a valid aiLogStream with a non-null callback.
Caller is responsible for later detaching this exact stream via aiDetachLogStream() or using aiDetachAllLogStreams() before shutdown.

functions.name: aiEnableVerboseLogging
functions.description: Enables or disables verbose logging (debug details and statistics). Verbose mode can strongly impact performance and memory usage.
requirements: d must be AI_TRUE to enable or AI_FALSE to disable.

functions.name: aiDetachLogStream
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API C_ENUM aiReturn aiDetachLogStream(const C_STRUCT aiLogStream *stream);
functions.description: Detaches a previously attached log stream from the logging system.
requirements: stream must point to the same aiLogStream that was previously attached via aiAttachLogStream().
Check the return value (aiReturn) for success or failure.

functions.name: aiDetachAllLogStreams
functions.description: Detaches all active log streams and frees logging resources to ensure proper logging system shutdown.

functions.name: aiReleaseImport
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with a scene previously returned by an import call.
requirements: pScene may be NULL; if non-null it must be a pointer previously returned by an Assimp import function.
Do not use the scene or its contents after calling this function.

functions.name: aiGetErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the last import error, or NULL if there was no error. If a previous import returned a non-NULL aiScene, there is no error.
requirements: Return value points to an internal, read-only string; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: aiIsExtensionSupported
functions.description: Checks whether a given file extension is supported by the current Assimp build.
requirements: szExtension must be a non-null C string that includes the leading dot (e.g., ".obj").

functions.name: aiGetExtensionList
functions.description: Fills an aiString with a semicolon-separated list of supported file patterns (e.g., "*.3ds;*.obj;*.dae").
requirements: szOut must be non-null and point to a valid aiString to receive the list.

functions.name: aiGetMemoryRequirements
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiGetMemoryRequirements(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pIn, C_STRUCT aiMemoryInfo *in);
functions.description: Computes an approximate memory footprint breakdown for an imported scene and writes it to aiMemoryInfo.
requirements: pIn must be a valid, imported aiScene pointer.
in must be non-null and point to a valid aiMemoryInfo structure to be filled.

functions.name: aiGetEmbeddedTexture
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiTexture *aiGetEmbeddedTexture(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pIn, const char *filename);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an embedded texture referenced by the given material texture path, or NULL if not found.
requirements: pIn must be a valid aiScene.
filename should be a texture path extracted from aiGetMaterialString or similar; must be non-null for meaningful lookup.
Returned aiTexture pointer is owned by the scene; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: aiCreatePropertyStore
functions.description: Creates a new, empty property store object for importer configuration.
requirements: The returned store must be released with aiReleasePropertyStore().

functions.name: aiReleasePropertyStore
functions.description: Deletes a property store previously created with aiCreatePropertyStore().
requirements: p must be a property store created by aiCreatePropertyStore(); may be NULL if caller wishes to no-op (unspecified in header, pass non-null to be safe).
Do not use the property store after releasing it.

functions.name: aiSetImportPropertyInteger
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiSetImportPropertyInteger(C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *store, const char *szName, int value);
functions.description: Sets an integer configuration property in a property store (global in C API). Public property keys are defined in config.h (AI_CONFIG_*).
requirements: store must be a valid aiPropertyStore created with aiCreatePropertyStore().
szName must be a non-null, null-terminated key string matching a supported property name.
value is the integer to set.

functions.name: aiSetImportPropertyFloat
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiSetImportPropertyFloat(C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *store, const char *szName, ai_real value);
functions.description: Sets a floating-point configuration property in a property store (global in C API).
requirements: store must be a valid aiPropertyStore.
szName must be non-null and match a supported property key.
value is the floating-point value to set.

functions.name: aiSetImportPropertyString
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiSetImportPropertyString(C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *store, const char *szName, const C_STRUCT aiString *st);
functions.description: Sets a string configuration property in a property store.
requirements: store must be a valid aiPropertyStore.
szName must be non-null and match a supported property key.
st must be a valid aiString pointer.

functions.name: aiSetImportPropertyMatrix
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiSetImportPropertyMatrix(C_STRUCT aiPropertyStore *store, const char *szName, const C_STRUCT aiMatrix4x4 *mat);
functions.description: Sets a 4x4 matrix configuration property in a property store.
requirements: store must be a valid aiPropertyStore.
szName must be non-null and match a supported property key.
mat must be a valid pointer to a 4x4 matrix.

functions.name: aiCreateQuaternionFromMatrix
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiCreateQuaternionFromMatrix(C_STRUCT aiQuaternion *quat, const C_STRUCT aiMatrix3x3 *mat);
functions.description: Builds a quaternion representing the rotation of a 3x3 matrix.
requirements: quat must be non-null and will receive the result.
mat must be a non-null pointer to a valid 3x3 rotation matrix.

functions.name: aiDecomposeMatrix
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiDecomposeMatrix(const C_STRUCT aiMatrix4x4 *mat, C_STRUCT aiVector3D *scaling, C_STRUCT aiQuaternion *rotation, C_STRUCT aiVector3D *position);
functions.description: Decomposes a 4x4 transform matrix into scaling, rotation (quaternion), and translation components.
requirements: mat must be non-null.
scaling, rotation, and position must be non-null pointers to receive outputs.

functions.name: aiTransposeMatrix4
functions.description: Transposes a 4x4 matrix in place.
requirements: mat must be a non-null pointer to a 4x4 matrix.

functions.name: aiTransposeMatrix3
