functions.name: Assimp::setAiAssertHandler
functions.description: Installs a custom assert handler callback for Assimp. Use this to intercept assertion failures raised by the library and route them to your own logging/handling code. The handler must match AiAssertHandler (void(*)(const char*, const char*, int)). Details about thread-safety or default-reset behavior are not specified in this header.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer matching Assimp::AiAssertHandler (void (*)(const char*, const char*, int)).
The lifetime of the function pointed to by handler must extend through all potential invocations by the library.
Behavior when passing a null handler is unknown (not specified here); provide a valid handler to avoid undefined behavior.
The installed handler should be async-signal-safe or reentrant if it may be called from various contexts (not specified; infer caution due to typical assert handling).

functions.name: Assimp::defaultAiAssertHandler
functions.signature: void Assimp::defaultAiAssertHandler(const char* failedExpression, const char* file, int line)
functions.description: The library’s built-in assert handler. It writes a diagnostic message to stderr and terminates the process (abort). Marked as non-returning. Typically used as the default handler or as a reference implementation; you normally don’t call it directly unless intentionally aborting after an assertion failure.
requirements: failedExpression must point to a valid null-terminated C string describing the failed expression.
file must point to a valid null-terminated C string with the source filename.
line should be the corresponding source line number; use a non-negative integer.
This function does not return and will terminate the process; callers must not expect control to continue past the call.

functions.name: Assimp::aiAssertViolation
functions.signature: void Assimp::aiAssertViolation(const char* failedExpression, const char* file, int line)
functions.description: Dispatches an assertion violation to the currently installed assert handler. Typically invoked by Assimp’s internal assertion macros; external code can call it to route an assertion failure through the configured handler.
requirements: failedExpression must be a valid null-terminated C string describing the failed expression.
file must be a valid null-terminated C string naming the source file.
line should be the source line number; use a non-negative integer.
Should be called in response to an assertion failure condition; semantics outside that context are not defined by this header.
If a custom handler is installed, it will be invoked with these parameters; ensure the handler can safely handle them.

functions.name: aiGetImporterDesc
functions.description: Returns a read-only importer description for a given file extension. Use this to query metadata (name, author, flags, supported versions, and extensions) about the importer that would handle files with the specified extension. If no importer is associated with the extension, the function returns nullptr.
requirements: extension must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
Provide only the file extension token (no leading dot) and in lower-case to match Assimp’s mFileExtensions convention (e.g., "dae", "obj").
Caller must check the return value for nullptr before dereferencing the pointer.
The returned aiImporterDesc pointer refers to const data owned by the library; do not modify or free it.

requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property (properties are defined in aiConfig.h with AI_CONFIG_*).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetPropertyBool
functions.description: Sets a boolean configuration property. Booleans are stored on the integer stack and can be queried via GetPropertyBool() or GetPropertyInteger(). Returns true if a previous value existed and was replaced.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetPropertyFloat
functions.description: Sets a floating-point configuration property identified by name. Returns true if a previous value existed and was replaced.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetPropertyString
functions.description: Sets a string configuration property identified by name. Returns true if a previous value existed and was replaced.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetPropertyMatrix
functions.description: Sets a matrix (aiMatrix4x4) configuration property identified by name. Returns true if a previous value existed and was replaced.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetPropertyPointer
functions.description: Sets a pointer configuration property identified by name. Returns true if a previous value existed and was replaced.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a known property.
Caller is responsible for the lifetime and validity of the pointer value unless otherwise documented by the specific property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyInteger
functions.description: Retrieves an integer configuration property by name. Returns iErrorReturn (default 0xFFFFFFFF/AI_PROPERTY_WAS_NOT_EXISTING) if not set.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyBool
functions.signature: bool Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyBool(const char *szName, bool bErrorReturn = false) const
functions.description: Retrieves a boolean configuration property by name. Returns bErrorReturn if the property is not set. Internally reads from the integer stack.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyFloat
functions.signature: ai_real Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyFloat(const char *szName, ai_real fErrorReturn = 1.0e11) const
functions.description: Retrieves a floating-point configuration property by name. Returns fErrorReturn (default 1.0e11) if not set.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyString
functions.signature: std::string Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyString(const char *szName, const std::string &sErrorReturn = std::string()) const
functions.description: Retrieves a string configuration property by name. Returns sErrorReturn if not set. The returned string remains valid until the property is modified.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyMatrix
functions.signature: aiMatrix4x4 Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyMatrix(const char *szName, const aiMatrix4x4 &sErrorReturn = aiMatrix4x4()) const
functions.description: Retrieves a matrix configuration property by name. Returns sErrorReturn if not set. The returned value remains valid until the property is modified.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetPropertyPointer
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer configuration property by name. Returns sErrorReturn if not set. The returned pointer remains valid until the property is modified.
requirements: szName must point to a null-terminated C string naming a property.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetIOHandler
functions.description: Sets a custom IOSystem for file access. Importer takes ownership and deletes the previously assigned handler. Pass nullptr to reset to the default handler and take back ownership of your current custom handler.
requirements: If pIOHandler is non-null, it must be a valid heap-allocated IOSystem instance.
Do not delete pIOHandler after passing it; ownership transfers to Importer.

Passing nullptr resets to the default IO handler and returns ownership of the previous custom handler to the caller (the previous handler is not deleted in this case per note: "Pass nullptr to take again ownership of your IOSystem and reset Assimp to use its default implementation.").

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetIOHandler
functions.description: Returns the currently set IOSystem. It is guaranteed to return a valid interface (never nullptr).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::IsDefaultIOHandler
functions.description: Returns true if the default IO handler is active (i.e., no custom IO handler has been set).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetProgressHandler
functions.description: Sets a custom ProgressHandler used for progress reporting and to allow aborting loading. Pass nullptr to disable progress reporting. Importer uses, but does not document ownership transfer for this pointer.
requirements: pHandler may be nullptr to disable progress reporting.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetProgressHandler
functions.description: Returns the currently set ProgressHandler. It is guaranteed to return a valid interface (never nullptr); if none was set, the default handler is returned.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::IsDefaultProgressHandler
functions.description: Returns true if the default ProgressHandler is active (i.e., no custom handler has been set).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ValidateFlags
functions.description: Checks if a given aiPostProcess flag combination is supported (e.g., not mutually exclusive and available in the current build).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ReadFile
functions.signature: const aiScene* Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(const char *pFile, unsigned int pFlags)
functions.description: Loads a model file from disk and returns a pointer to the imported aiScene on success, or nullptr on failure. The Importer retains ownership of the scene; it is read-only and will be destroyed when the Importer is destroyed or FreeScene() is called. Previous scene (if any) is deleted during this call. On failure, GetErrorString() provides a human-readable error.
requirements: pFile must be a pointer to a null-terminated path string.
pFlags is a bitwise combination of aiPostProcessSteps; use ValidateFlags() if unsure.
Caller must not write to the returned aiScene.
Do not assume thread-safety; one Importer instance is not thread-safe across threads.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ReadFile
functions.signature: const aiScene* Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(const std::string &pFile, unsigned int pFlags)
functions.description: Convenience overload that forwards to ReadFile(const char*, unsigned). Loads a model from a file path string object.
requirements: pFile must contain a valid path string.
pFlags is a bitwise combination of aiPostProcessSteps; use ValidateFlags() if unsure.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory
functions.signature: const aiScene* Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(const void *pBuffer, size_t pLength, unsigned int pFlags, const char *pHint = "")
functions.description: Loads a model from a memory buffer and returns a pointer to the imported aiScene on success, or nullptr on failure. Ownership semantics and error reporting are identical to ReadFile(). Does not affect the active IOSystem. pHint can suggest the file extension to choose the loader.
requirements: pBuffer must be a valid pointer to the entire file data.
pLength must be the exact size of the data in bytes.
pFlags is a bitwise combination of aiPostProcessSteps; use ValidateFlags() if unsure.
If provided, pHint should be a non-empty extension string without wildcards; its maximum length is limited by Assimp::Importer::MaxLenHint (200).
This API does not resolve external resources referenced by formats that use multiple files; use a custom IOSystem and ReadFile() for such formats.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ApplyPostProcessing
functions.description: Applies a set of aiPostProcess steps to the currently loaded scene. Returns the (same) scene pointer, or nullptr if post-processing fails (rare; e.g., with aiProcess_ValidateDS). No-op if no scene is currently loaded.
requirements: pFlags is a bitwise combination of aiPostProcessSteps.
A scene must be loaded for any effect; otherwise the call does nothing.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::ApplyCustomizedPostProcessing
functions.description: Applies a custom post-processing pipeline starting at the provided root process. Optionally requests validation. Returns the post-processed scene pointer (same owned scene) or nullptr on failure. Details of the custom pipeline are not documented in this header.
requirements: rootProcess requirements are not documented; likely must be a valid BaseProcess chain. Unknown ownership transfer semantics.
If requestValidation is true, the implementation may validate the data; specifics are not documented.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::FreeScene
functions.description: Frees the currently loaded scene, if any. Automatically called by the destructor and by subsequent successful ReadFile()/ReadFileFromMemory() calls.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetErrorString
functions.description: Returns a description of the last error that occurred in ReadFile()/ReadFileFromMemory(); returns an empty string if no error occurred. The returned pointer remains valid until the next ReadFile() or FreeScene().

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetException
functions.description: Returns the last exception captured during import (if any). The reference remains valid until the next ReadFile() or FreeScene().

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetScene
functions.description: Returns the scene loaded by the last successful ReadFile()/ReadFileFromMemory() call, or nullptr if no scene is loaded. The Importer retains ownership; the scene is read-only.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetOrphanedScene
functions.description: Releases ownership of the currently loaded scene and returns it to the caller. After this call, GetScene()/GetOrphanedScene() will return nullptr until a new scene is loaded. The caller becomes responsible for deleting the scene.
requirements: Call only if a scene is currently loaded; otherwise returns nullptr.
After taking ownership, the caller must delete the aiScene when done. Deallocation must be compatible with Assimp’s allocation (see note in docs). Use with caution.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::IsExtensionSupported
functions.description: Returns whether a given file extension is supported by any registered importer.
requirements: szExtension must include a leading dot (e.g., ".3ds", ".md3"). Case-insensitive.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::IsExtensionSupported
functions.description: Convenience overload that forwards to IsExtensionSupported(const char*).
requirements: szExtension should include a leading dot (e.g., ".3ds"). Case-insensitive.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetExtensionList
functions.description: Writes the list of all supported file extensions into szOut in the format "*.ext1;*.ext2;...". Useful for file dialogs and capability checks.
requirements: szOut must be a valid aiString reference to receive the result.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetExtensionList
functions.description: Convenience overload that forwards to GetExtensionList(aiString&), then copies into std::string.
requirements: szOut must be a valid std::string reference to receive the extension list.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetImporterCount
functions.description: Returns the number of importers currently registered with Assimp.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetImporterInfo
functions.description: Returns the importer metadata (aiImporterDesc) for the importer at the given index, or nullptr if the index is out of range or the importer does not provide metadata.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, GetImporterCount()).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetImporter
functions.description: Returns the importer instance at the given index, or nullptr if the index is out of range.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, GetImporterCount()).

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetImporterIndex
functions.description: Returns the index of the importer that handles the given extension, or (size_t)-1 if none is found. Recognized input forms include "BAH", ".bah", and "*.bah" (case-insensitive).
requirements: szExtension must be a null-terminated C string.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::GetMemoryRequirements
functions.description: Fills the provided aiMemoryInfo with the memory used by the currently loaded scene (user data sizes only; heap overhead not included).
requirements: in must be a valid aiMemoryInfo reference to receive the data.
Meaningful only if a scene is currently loaded; otherwise values may be zero.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::SetExtraVerbose
functions.description: Enables or disables extra-verbose mode, which validates the data structure after each post-processing step. Intended for debugging, not production.

functions.name: Assimp::Importer::Pimpl
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal implementation (pimpl). Marked as private/do not use.
requirements: Intended for internal use only; external callers should not rely on this API.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::create
functions.signature: static Assimp::Logger* Assimp::DefaultLogger::create(const char* name = ASSIMP_DEFAULT_LOG_NAME, LogSeverity severity = NORMAL, unsigned int defStreams = aiDefaultLogStream_DEBUGGER | aiDefaultLogStream_FILE, Assimp::IOSystem* io = nullptr)
functions.description: Creates and installs the library’s primary logger, replacing the default NullLogger with a DefaultLogger. Allows choosing a log file name, severity level, default output streams (bitwise OR of aiDefaultLogStream values), and an IOSystem for file access. If aiDefaultLogStream_FILE is included but an empty name is provided, no file is created. Typical usage is to call this once at startup to enable logging and then attach additional LogStream instances as needed.
requirements: If aiDefaultLogStream_FILE is specified in defStreams and a log file should be created, the name parameter must be non-empty; otherwise no log file will be created (per header comment).
severity controls verbosity: DEBUG enables debug messages; VERBOSE enables all messages (per header comment).
io may be nullptr to use the default IO implementation (per header comment).
Calling this replaces the current logger instance with a DefaultLogger (per header comment).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::set
functions.description: Installs a custom Logger implementation as the library’s primary logger. Use when DefaultLogger does not meet specific needs. When passing nullptr, the logger is reset to a NullLogger. Users supplying a custom logger are responsible for its lifetime management.
requirements: When installing a custom logger (non-null), the caller is responsible for its instantiation and destruction (per header comment).
Before deleting a custom logger supplied via set(), the caller must call set(nullptr) to detach it (per header comment).
Passing nullptr sets up a default NullLogger (per header comment).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::get
functions.description: Returns the current primary logger instance. It is never null; it may be a NullLogger if logging has not been enabled via create() or set(). Use isNullLogger() to check whether the returned logger is a NullLogger.
requirements: None beyond the function being callable at any time; the returned pointer is guaranteed non-null but may refer to a NullLogger (per header comment).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::isNullLogger
functions.description: Reports whether the current primary logger is a NullLogger. Use this to determine if logging has been configured via create() or set().
requirements: None explicitly stated.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::kill
functions.description: Destroys the current primary logger instance and replaces it with a NullLogger. Use to turn logging off and release the logger resources.
requirements: None explicitly stated in the header.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::attachStream
functions.description: Attaches a LogStream to the logger for the specified severity mask, enabling messages matching the mask to be forwarded to the stream. This is the DefaultLogger’s implementation of Logger::attachStream.
requirements: pStream should refer to a valid LogStream object for the duration of its attachment (inferred from typical Logger patterns; exact lifetime rules not documented here).
severity is a bitmask of severities to route to the stream (inferred from Logger/DefaultLogger usage; exact constants not documented here).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultLogger::detachStream
functions.description: Detaches a previously attached LogStream from the logger for the specified severity mask, stopping delivery of matching messages to that stream. This is the DefaultLogger’s implementation of Logger::detachStream.
requirements: pStream should be a LogStream that was previously attached; passing an unattached stream may result in a no-op (inferred; exact behavior not documented here).
severity should match the severity mask used for attachment to remove the intended routing (inferred; exact constants not documented here).

functions.name: Assimp::ProgressHandler::~ProgressHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Assimp::ProgressHandler. Cleans up resources for custom progress handlers. Typically invoked by deleting a ProgressHandler instance owned by an Assimp::Importer. No special action is required by callers.
requirements: Object must be a valid instance of Assimp::ProgressHandler when the destructor runs.
Caller must ensure no further calls are made to this object after destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::ProgressHandler::Update
functions.description: Primary progress callback. Called by the importer/exporter to report an estimate of the current progress in percent, or -1.0f if an estimate is not available. Return false to request abort of the ongoing operation; the importer/exporter may perform cleanup and Importer::ReadFile() will return nullptr if aborted. Intended to be overridden by user-defined handlers; the default base is pure virtual.
requirements: percentage is an estimate in percent (typically 0.0f to 100.0f) or exactly -1.0f to indicate an unavailable estimate.
Implementations of this method must not throw exceptions (as documented).
Implementations of this method must not call non-const Assimp::Importer methods (as documented).
Callers should check the return value: false indicates the operation should be aborted at the next possible occasion.

functions.name: Assimp::ProgressHandler::UpdateFileRead
functions.signature: virtual void UpdateFileRead(int currentStep, int numberOfSteps)
functions.description: Progress callback for file loading phases. Reports the current step of reading/parsing relative to the total number of steps. The default implementation scales and forwards the progress to Update() to represent roughly the first half of the overall progress.
requirements: numberOfSteps is the total number of file-read steps; it should be non-negative.
currentStep is the index of the current step to run, or equal to numberOfSteps if all have finished.
Across successive calls in a single operation, currentStep is strictly monotone increasing (not necessarily by 1).
Callers should pass values consistent with the documented semantics; the default implementation will call Update((currentStep/(float)numberOfSteps) * 0.5f) with 1.0f used if numberOfSteps is 0.

functions.name: Assimp::ProgressHandler::UpdatePostProcess
functions.signature: virtual void UpdatePostProcess(int currentStep, int numberOfSteps)
functions.description: Progress callback for post-processing steps after import. Reports the current post-process step relative to the total number of steps. The default implementation scales and forwards the progress to Update() to represent roughly the second half of the overall progress.
requirements: numberOfSteps is the total number of post-processing steps; it should be non-negative.
currentStep is the index of the current step to run, or equal to numberOfSteps if all have finished.
Across successive calls in a single operation, currentStep is strictly monotone increasing (not necessarily by 1).

Callers should pass values consistent with the documented semantics; the default implementation will call Update((currentStep/(float)numberOfSteps) * 0.5f + 0.5f) with 1.0f used if numberOfSteps is 0.

functions.name: Assimp::ProgressHandler::UpdateFileWrite
functions.signature: virtual void UpdateFileWrite(int currentStep, int numberOfSteps)
functions.description: Progress callback for export (file writing) phases. Reports the current step of writing relative to the total number of steps. The default implementation scales and forwards the progress to Update().
requirements: numberOfSteps is the total number of export steps; it should be non-negative.
currentStep is the index of the current step to run, or equal to numberOfSteps if all have finished.
Across successive calls in a single operation, currentStep is strictly monotone increasing (not necessarily by 1).
Callers should pass values consistent with the documented semantics; the default implementation will call Update((currentStep/(float)numberOfSteps) * 0.5f) with 1.0f used if numberOfSteps is 0.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::~IOStream
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Assimp::IOStream. Deleting an IOStream closes the underlying file/handle; alternatively, IOSystem::Close() may be used to release it. Intended to be invoked via a pointer/reference to IOStream (polymorphic destruction).
requirements: The IOStream instance must be a valid object created by IOSystem::Open() or a compatible factory before destruction.
After destruction, the object must not be used.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::Read
functions.signature: virtual size_t Assimp::IOStream::Read(void* pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount) = 0;
functions.description: Reads data from the stream into the caller-provided buffer. Semantics are analogous to C fread(). This operation will fail for write-only streams. Returns the number of items successfully read (up to pCount).
requirements: pvBuffer must point to a valid writable memory region of at least pSize * pCount bytes.
pSize and pCount define the item size and count, respectively; either may be zero to perform a no-op read that returns 0.
The stream must be opened in a mode that permits reading; otherwise the read will fail (0 items read).
On short reads (e.g., EOF), the return value may be less than pCount; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::Write
functions.signature: virtual size_t Assimp::IOStream::Write(const void* pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount) = 0;
functions.description: Writes data from the caller-provided buffer to the stream. Semantics are analogous to C fwrite(). This operation will fail for read-only streams. Returns the number of items successfully written (up to pCount).
requirements: pvBuffer must point to a valid readable memory region of at least pSize * pCount bytes.
pSize and pCount define the item size and count, respectively; either may be zero to perform a no-op write that returns 0.
The stream must be opened in a mode that permits writing; otherwise the write will fail (0 items written).
Callers must check the return value to detect short writes or errors.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::Seek
functions.signature: virtual aiReturn Assimp::IOStream::Seek(size_t pOffset, aiOrigin pOrigin) = 0;
functions.description: Sets the read/write cursor position in the stream, analogous to C fseek(). The documentation notes that the offset is negative for aiOrigin_END, indicating positions relative to the end of file.
requirements: pOrigin specifies the reference point (e.g., aiOrigin_SET, aiOrigin_CUR, aiOrigin_END from assimp/types.h).

For aiOrigin_END, the intended offset is described as negative; however, pOffset is size_t (unsigned), so how negative offsets are represented is implementation-defined/ambiguous. Callers should consult the concrete IOStream implementation or avoid using negative offsets where not supported.
The stream must support seeking; otherwise the function will return a non-success aiReturn value.
Callers must check the aiReturn result for success/failure.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current read/write cursor position in the stream, analogous to C ftell().
requirements: The stream must be in a valid state; undefined behavior if called after the stream is closed/destroyed.
Callers should expect the returned position to be in bytes from the beginning (typical ftell semantics), but exact units are determined by the implementation.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::FileSize
functions.description: Returns the size of the underlying file or stream in bytes.
requirements: The stream must reference a seekable resource that can report its size; for non-regular streams, the behavior is implementation-defined.
Callers must not assume the size fits within platform int; size_t is used.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStream::Flush
functions.description: Flushes any buffered output to the underlying sink, analogous to C fflush(). Primarily relevant for writable streams.
requirements: Only meaningful for streams opened for writing; calling on read-only streams may be a no-op or error depending on implementation.
Callers should handle any errors via the specific implementation’s error reporting (this interface does not return a status).

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::IOSystem
functions.description: Default constructor for a custom file-system handler used by Assimp. Instantiate your derived IOSystem and pass it to Assimp::Importer::SetIOHandler().
requirements: Must be called in C++ (header enforces C++).
Caller typically assigns the instance to an Assimp::Importer before importing.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::~IOSystem
functions.description: Virtual destructor. Allows safe deletion via base pointer and ensures resources allocated on Assimp’s heap are released correctly.
requirements: Object must be destroyed only once.
No further calls should be made on the object after destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::Exists
functions.signature: virtual bool Assimp::IOSystem::Exists(const char* pFile) const = 0
functions.description: Checks whether a file exists at the given path (C-string). Pure virtual; concrete IOSystem implementations must provide the check.
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
The path is interpreted according to the concrete IOSystem’s semantics (absolute/relative handling is implementation-defined).

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::getOsSeparator
functions.description: Returns the platform-specific directory separator character (e.g., '/' or '\\'). Pure virtual; concrete implementations must provide it.
requirements: No special preconditions; callable at any time on a valid IOSystem instance.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::Open
functions.signature: virtual Assimp::IOStream* Assimp::IOSystem::Open(const char* pFile, const char* pMode = "rb") = 0
functions.description: Opens a file using the given mode and returns an IOStream for I/O. Pure virtual; concrete IOSystem must implement this to open files from its backing store.
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated C string path.
pMode must be a valid, null-terminated C string. Implementations are required to support at least: "wb", "w", "wt", "rb", "r", "rt".
Returned IOStream* must be closed via Close() (or by letting the IOStream’s virtual destructor run) to release resources.
Returns nullptr on failure (implementation-defined); callers should check for null before use.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::Close
functions.description: Closes a file previously opened via this IOSystem::Open and releases associated resources.
requirements: pFile must be a non-null pointer previously returned by this IOSystem’s Open().
Do not pass pointers not created by this IOSystem implementation.
After Close(), the IOStream pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::ComparePaths
functions.signature: virtual bool Assimp::IOSystem::ComparePaths(const char* one, const char* second) const
functions.description: Compares two paths and checks whether they refer to the same file. Default implementation performs case-insensitive comparison and may resolve relative to absolute paths in default IOSystem; behavior may be overridden by custom implementations.
requirements: one and second must be valid, null-terminated C strings.
The compared files need not exist; comparison is path-based.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::PushDirectory
functions.description: Pushes a directory path onto an internal directory stack, making it the current top.
requirements: path must be non-empty; the function returns false if empty.
The provided path string is stored internally; ensure it represents a valid directory for your use-case (not enforced here).

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::CurrentDirectory
functions.description: Returns the directory on the top of the internal stack. If no directory was pushed, an empty value is returned. Implementation is not provided in this header; exact empty-return mechanics (e.g., reference to an empty string) are unknown.
requirements: Call is valid at any time; if the stack is empty, the returned reference corresponds to an empty directory state (implementation-specific).
Do not assume the reference outlives the IOSystem instance.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::StackSize
functions.description: Returns the number of directories currently stored on the internal stack.
requirements: No special preconditions.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::PopDirectory
functions.description: Pops the top directory from the internal stack.
requirements: The directory stack must be non-empty for the function to return true; returns false if already empty.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::CreateDirectory
functions.description: Creates a new directory at the given path using platform APIs (_mkdir on Windows, mkdir on POSIX). Returns false if the path is empty; otherwise returns the platform call’s success status as implemented here.
requirements: path must be non-empty; function returns false if empty.
The path must be valid and the process must have permissions to create directories at the target location.
On many platforms mkdir/_mkdir return 0 on success; callers should not rely on undocumented inversion semantics—check the boolean return from this function directly.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::ChangeDirectory
functions.description: Changes the current process working directory to the given path using platform APIs (_chdir/chdir). Returns false if path is empty; otherwise returns the platform call’s success status as implemented here.
requirements: path must be non-empty; function returns false if empty.
The path must exist and be accessible; appropriate permissions are required.
Changing the process working directory affects subsequent relative path resolutions globally in the process.

functions.name: Assimp::IOSystem::DeleteFile
functions.description: Deletes the specified file using std::remove. Returns true if the file was deleted (remove returned 0), false otherwise.
requirements: file must be non-empty; function returns false if empty.
The path must refer to a file the process has permission to delete.
If the file does not exist or is in use, deletion may fail (returns false).

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::~Logger
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Assimp::Logger. Cleans up logger resources on destruction. Implementations may release ownership of attached LogStream instances as appropriate.

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::debug
functions.description: Writes a debug-level log message. Use for standard debug output (not verbose). Messages longer than MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) are rejected.
requirements: message must point to a null-terminated C-string
message length should be <= MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) to avoid rejection

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::verboseDebug
functions.description: Writes a verbose debug-level log message. Visible when log severity is set to VERBOSE. Messages longer than MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) are rejected.
requirements: message must point to a null-terminated C-string
message length should be <= MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) to avoid rejection

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::info
functions.description: Writes an info-level log message. Messages longer than MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) are rejected.
requirements: message must point to a null-terminated C-string
message length should be <= MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) to avoid rejection

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::warn
functions.description: Writes a warning-level log message. Messages longer than MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) are rejected.
requirements: message must point to a null-terminated C-string
message length should be <= MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) to avoid rejection

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::error
functions.description: Writes an error-level log message. Messages longer than MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) are rejected.
requirements: message must point to a null-terminated C-string
message length should be <= MAX_LOG_MESSAGE_LENGTH (1024) to avoid rejection

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::setLogSeverity
functions.description: Sets the current logging severity threshold for the logger instance. Controls which messages are emitted to attached streams.
requirements: log_severity must be one of Assimp::Logger::NORMAL, Assimp::Logger::DEBUGGING, or Assimp::Logger::VERBOSE

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::getLogSeverity
functions.description: Returns the current logging severity threshold of the logger.

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::attachStream
functions.signature: virtual bool attachStream(Assimp::LogStream* pStream, unsigned int severity = Assimp::Logger::Debugging | Assimp::Logger::Err | Assimp::Logger::Warn | Assimp::Logger::Info) = 0
functions.description: Attaches a log stream to the logger. The logger takes ownership of the stream and will destroy it on logger destruction unless detached. The severity mask filters which message types are dispatched to the stream.
requirements: pStream is expected to be a valid pointer to an Assimp::LogStream instance
severity must be a bitwise OR combination of ErrorSeverity flags (Assimp::Logger::Debugging, Info, Warn, Err)
After successful attachment, the logger owns pStream; callers must not delete it directly
Use detachStream to regain ownership if needed

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::detachStream
functions.signature: virtual bool detachStream(Assimp::LogStream* pStream, unsigned int severity = Assimp::Logger::Debugging | Assimp::Logger::Err | Assimp::Logger::Warn | Assimp::Logger::Info) = 0
functions.description: Modifies a stream's severity mask or detaches it from the logger. The provided severity bits are cleared from the stream’s current mask; if the resulting mask becomes 0, the stream is detached and ownership returns to the caller.
requirements: pStream is expected to refer to a stream previously attached to this logger
severity must be a bitwise OR combination of ErrorSeverity flags (Assimp::Logger::Debugging, Info, Warn, Err)
If the resulting mask is 0, the stream is detached and the caller retakes ownership and becomes responsible for its lifetime

functions.name: Assimp::Logger::Logger
functions.description: Default constructor for Logger. Initializes a logger with default severity (NORMAL). Intended for use by derived classes.

functions.name: Assimp::LogStream::~LogStream
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Assimp::LogStream. Ensures proper cleanup through the base interface when deleting derived log stream instances via a base pointer. Typical usage: delete a LogStream* you own (e.g., returned by createDefaultStream or a custom implementation).
requirements: The LogStream instance must be a valid, fully constructed object when destroyed.
Do not use the object after destruction (standard C++ object lifetime rules).
If you allocated a derived LogStream dynamically, delete it exactly once to avoid leaks or double-free (inferred from standard ownership patterns).

functions.name: Assimp::LogStream::write
functions.description: Pure-virtual sink method to output a log message to the stream. Messages may contain multiple lines and formatting is not guaranteed. In practice, most messages are single-line and terminated with a single '\n'. Implemented by concrete LogStream subclasses; called by Assimp's logging system to emit log text.
requirements: message must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
The LogStream object must be a valid, initialized instance of a concrete subclass (this function is pure virtual).
Callers must not assume consistent formatting; messages may contain multiple lines and arbitrary content (per documentation).
Thread-safety and blocking behavior are unspecified; callers should not assume write is thread-safe unless guaranteed by a specific implementation (unknown).

functions.name: Assimp::LogStream::createDefaultStream
functions.signature: static Assimp::LogStream *createDefaultStream(aiDefaultLogStream stream, const char *name = "AssimpLog.txt", Assimp::IOSystem *io = nullptr);
functions.description: Factory to create one of Assimp’s default log stream implementations. Selects the type using the aiDefaultLogStream value. For aiDefaultLogStream_FILE, the output file name can be specified via name; optionally provide an IOSystem to open the file, or pass nullptr to use the default IO implementation. Returns a newly created LogStream instance on success.
requirements: stream must be a valid aiDefaultLogStream selector value.
For aiDefaultLogStream_FILE, name should be a valid path/filename for the output file (per documentation).
For aiDefaultLogStream_FILE, if io is not nullptr it must be a valid Assimp::IOSystem instance usable for opening the output file; pass nullptr to use the default implementation.
The returned LogStream* is a newly created object; the caller assumes ownership and must delete it to avoid memory leaks (inferred from "New LogStream instance" and raw-pointer return).
If a non-default IOSystem is supplied, ensure it remains valid/alive for as long as the created LogStream may use it (inferred from typical IO ownership patterns).
Return value nullability on failure is not documented; callers should defensively check for nullptr before use (unknown behavior, recommended precaution).

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::OnDebug
functions.description: Logs a debug message using the NullLogger. This implementation is a no-op and intentionally ignores the input. Useful as a default logger when no custom logger is configured.
requirements: No side effects: the function does nothing regardless of input.
message may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
Return value: none; callers should not expect any logging output.

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::OnVerboseDebug
functions.description: Logs a verbose debug message using the NullLogger. This implementation is a no-op and ignores the input.
requirements: No side effects: the function does nothing regardless of input.
message may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
Return value: none; callers should not expect any logging output.

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::OnInfo
functions.description: Logs an informational message using the NullLogger. This implementation does nothing and ignores the input message.
requirements: No side effects: the function does nothing regardless of input.
message may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
Return value: none; callers should not expect any logging output.

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::OnWarn
functions.description: Logs a warning message using the NullLogger. This implementation is a no-op.
requirements: No side effects: the function does nothing regardless of input.
message may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
Return value: none; callers should not expect any logging output.

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::OnError
functions.description: Logs an error message using the NullLogger. This implementation is a no-op.
requirements: No side effects: the function does nothing regardless of input.
message may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
Return value: none; callers should not expect any logging output.

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::attachStream
functions.description: Attempts to attach a LogStream to the NullLogger. This implementation ignores the request and always returns false, indicating that streams cannot be attached to NullLogger.
requirements: pStream may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
severity is ignored; any value is accepted.
Callers must handle the return value: this function always returns false (no stream is attached).

functions.name: Assimp::NullLogger::detachStream
functions.description: Attempts to detach a LogStream from the NullLogger. This implementation ignores the request and always returns false, indicating that no streams are managed by NullLogger.
requirements: pStream may be nullptr; it is not dereferenced by this implementation.
severity is ignored; any value is accepted.
Callers must handle the return value: this function always returns false (no stream was detached).

functions.name: aiGetExportFormatCount
functions.description: Returns the number of export file formats available in the current Assimp build. Use the count to index into aiGetExportFormatDescription(). Typical usage: query the count, then iterate 0..count-1 to get each format description.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time after Assimp is available/initialized.
Return value is a non-negative size_t count; use it to bound indices for aiGetExportFormatDescription().

functions.name: aiGetExportFormatDescription
functions.description: Returns a heap-allocated description of the pIndex-th export file format supported by Assimp. The returned pointer must be released with aiReleaseExportFormatDescription(). Returns NULL if pIndex is out of range.
requirements: pIndex must be in the range [0, aiGetExportFormatCount()).
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, must be released by calling aiReleaseExportFormatDescription() exactly once.
If NULL is returned, do not call aiReleaseExportFormatDescription().
Do not modify the returned structure; treat it as read-only.

functions.name: aiReleaseExportFormatDescription
functions.description: Releases a format description previously obtained from aiGetExportFormatDescription(). This frees internal resources associated with that description.
requirements: desc must be a pointer previously returned by aiGetExportFormatDescription().
Do not pass pointers not obtained from aiGetExportFormatDescription().
Call exactly once for each successful aiGetExportFormatDescription() that returned a non-NULL pointer.
The pointer must not be used after being released.

functions.name: aiCopyScene
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void aiCopyScene(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pIn, C_STRUCT aiScene **pOut);
functions.description: Creates a modifiable deep copy of an aiScene. Use this to take a const scene returned by import, modify it, and later export it. The copy must be freed with aiFreeScene().
requirements: pIn must point to a valid aiScene.
pOut must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated aiScene*; on success, *pOut is set to a new scene owned by the caller.
The returned scene must be freed with aiFreeScene().
Do not pass the original (const) importer-owned scene to aiFreeScene(); only free scenes created by aiCopyScene().

functions.name: aiFreeScene
functions.description: Frees a scene copy that was created with aiCopyScene(). Releases all associated memory.
requirements: pIn must be a scene previously created by aiCopyScene().
Do not pass importer-owned scenes returned by assimp import APIs.
Do not call more than once for the same scene pointer.
Pointer must not be used after being freed.

functions.name: aiExportScene
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiExportScene(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pScene, const char *pFormatId, const char *pFileName, unsigned int pPreprocessing);
functions.description: Exports the given scene to the specified file format and writes the output file(s) to disk using default IO. Returns an aiReturn status. Intended for exporting an Assimp-format-compliant scene, optionally applying preprocessing to adapt conventions.
requirements: pScene must point to a valid aiScene; it is not modified by this function.
pFormatId must be a valid exporter ID string as returned in aiExportFormatDesc::id (e.g., from aiGetExportFormatDescription()).
pFileName must specify a writable destination path/filename for the primary output.

pPreprocessing is a bitmask of aiPostProcessSteps; only a subset meaningfully applies on export. Flags like aiProcess_MakeLeftHanded, aiProcess_FlipUVs, aiProcess_FlipWindingOrder invert defaults on export.

If the scene comes directly from Assimp’s importer and wasn’t copied via aiCopyScene, previously applied post-process steps are not re-applied unless non-idempotent (MakeLeftHanded/FlipUVs/FlipWindingOrder).
Check the return value (aiReturn) for success/failure and handle errors accordingly.
If the format generates multiple files, auxiliary files may be written alongside the primary file.

functions.name: aiExportSceneEx
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiReturn aiExportSceneEx(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pScene, const char *pFormatId, const char *pFileName, C_STRUCT aiFileIO *pIO, unsigned int pPreprocessing);
functions.description: Exports the given scene to the specified file format using a caller-supplied aiFileIO for custom IO. Returns an aiReturn status. Use this to redirect export output to custom storage backends.
requirements: pScene must point to a valid aiScene; it is not modified by this function.
pFormatId must be a valid exporter ID string as returned in aiExportFormatDesc::id.
pFileName names the output (used by exporters and may inform auxiliary file naming).
pIO may be NULL to use default file IO; otherwise it must point to a properly initialized aiFileIO implementation (include <aiFileIO.h>).
pPreprocessing is a bitmask of aiPostProcessSteps with the same considerations as aiExportScene().
Check the aiReturn result and handle failures.
Your aiFileIO callbacks must successfully handle all file operations requested by the exporter, including creation of auxiliary files if the format requires them.

functions.name: aiExportSceneToBlob
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API const C_STRUCT aiExportDataBlob *aiExportSceneToBlob(const C_STRUCT aiScene *pScene, const char *pFormatId, unsigned int pPreprocessing);
functions.description: Exports the given scene to the specified file format and returns the result as an in-memory aiExportDataBlob chain. Use aiReleaseExportBlob() to free it. The primary blob (name empty) contains the main file data; additional chained blobs may represent auxiliary files.
requirements: pScene must point to a valid aiScene; it is not modified by this function.
pFormatId must be a valid exporter ID string.
pPreprocessing is a bitmask of aiPostProcessSteps with the same considerations as aiExportScene().
On success, the returned pointer is non-NULL and owned by Assimp; the caller must free it using aiReleaseExportBlob().
Do not attempt to free or reallocate the memory manually; do not cast away const to modify data.
If multiple files are produced by the exporter, traverse the linked list via blob->next to access auxiliary blobs; blob->name may indicate suggested file extensions.

functions.name: aiReleaseExportBlob
functions.description: Frees an aiExportDataBlob chain previously returned by aiExportSceneToBlob(). Releases all associated memory (including chained blobs).
requirements: pData must be a pointer returned by aiExportSceneToBlob() (or NULL if you choose to no-op; behavior for NULL not specified).
Call exactly once for each successful aiExportSceneToBlob() that returned a non-NULL pointer.
Do not use the blob or any chained blobs after releasing.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::Exporter
functions.description: Constructs an Exporter instance that provides C++ export functionality for Assimp. Sets up internal state, default IO handler, and no current blob.
requirements: None beyond standard construction semantics.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::~Exporter
functions.description: Destructor for Exporter. Automatically frees any current export blob and releases owned resources, including any custom IOSystem previously set.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Any orphaned blobs obtained via GetOrphanedBlob() remain the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::SetIOHandler
functions.description: Sets a custom IOSystem to control file access during exporting. Exporter takes ownership of the provided IOSystem. Passing NULL resets to the default file-based IO and returns ownership to the caller of any previously set handler.
requirements: pIOHandler may be NULL to restore default IO.
Caller must not delete the IOSystem after passing it to SetIOHandler; Exporter destroys it.
Setting a new handler deletes the previously assigned handler.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetIOHandler
functions.description: Returns the currently active IOSystem used by the exporter. Never NULL.
requirements: None. Returned pointer remains valid as long as the Exporter owns the handler and until it is replaced or the Exporter is destroyed.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::IsDefaultIOHandler
functions.description: Reports whether the default IO handler is active (i.e., no custom IOSystem has been supplied).
requirements: None.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::SetProgressHandler
functions.description: Installs a progress callback interface invoked periodically during export; can be used to show progress or abort the operation. Pass nullptr to disable progress reporting.
requirements: pHandler may be nullptr to disable progress.
Progress handlers can be used to abort the loading/exporting at almost any time.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::ExportToBlob
functions.signature: const aiExportDataBlob *Assimp::Exporter::ExportToBlob(const aiScene *pScene, const char *pFormatId, unsigned int pPreprocessing = 0u, const Assimp::ExportProperties *pProperties = nullptr)
functions.description: Exports the given scene to the specified format and returns the output as a linked list of in-memory blobs. Useful for in-memory processing. Any previously held blob is disposed by this call.
requirements: pScene must be a valid scene pointer owned by the caller; it is not modified.
pFormatId must match a supported exporter id (see GetExportFormatCount/GetExportFormatDescription).
pPreprocessing may include aiPostProcessSteps flags; only a subset is meaningful for exporting.
pProperties may be nullptr or point to an ExportProperties with relevant options.
Returns nullptr on error.
Any IO handlers set via SetIOHandler are ignored for this method.

If the input scene originates directly from the importer side and has post-processing already applied, idempotent steps are not re-applied (non-idempotent ones like MakeLeftHanded/FlipUVs/FlipWindingOrder may be).
The returned blob remains owned by the Exporter until GetOrphanedBlob() is called or the Exporter is destroyed or a subsequent ExportToBlob() frees/replaces it.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::Export
functions.signature: aiReturn Assimp::Exporter::Export(const aiScene *pScene, const char *pFormatId, const char *pPath, unsigned int pPreprocessing = 0u, const Assimp::ExportProperties *pProperties = nullptr)
functions.description: Exports the given scene directly to a file using the current IOSystem (default or custom). Applies optional preprocessing steps relevant to the target format.
requirements: pScene must be valid and is not modified by the function.
pFormatId must be a supported exporter id.
pPath must be a full target file name that is accessible for writing by the current IOSystem.
pPreprocessing may include aiPostProcessSteps flags; only a subset is meaningful for exporting.
If the input scene was directly taken from the importer side, already-applied steps won’t be re-applied unless non-idempotent (MakeLeftHanded, FlipUVs, FlipWindingOrder).
Returns AI_SUCCESS on success; other aiReturn codes indicate failure.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetErrorString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description of the last error that occurred in Export or ExportToBlob, or an empty string if no error occurred. The pointer is never NULL.
requirements: Caller must not hold the returned pointer beyond the next call to Export, ExportToBlob, or FreeBlob, which may invalidate it.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetBlob
functions.description: Returns the blob from the most recent successful ExportToBlob call, if any.
requirements: Returns nullptr if no blob is currently held. Blob remains owned by the Exporter until freed, replaced, destroyed, or orphaned.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetOrphanedBlob
functions.description: Transfers ownership of the current export blob to the caller. After this call, the Exporter no longer manages the blob.
requirements: Caller must release the blob using the C API function aiReleaseExportBlob.
If no blob is held, returns nullptr.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::FreeBlob
functions.description: Frees the current in-memory export blob (if any) held by the Exporter.
requirements: Safe to call if no blob is held; it then does nothing.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetExportFormatCount
functions.description: Returns the number of export formats available in the current build and registered with this Exporter instance (built-in and custom).
requirements: None.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::GetExportFormatDescription
functions.description: Retrieves the description of the export format at the given index.
requirements: pIndex must be in the range [0, GetExportFormatCount()).
Returns nullptr if pIndex is out of range.
For built-in exporters, the returned pointer has static storage duration; otherwise its lifetime is tied to the Exporter instance.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::RegisterExporter
functions.description: Registers a custom exporter format for this Exporter instance. Assigns it the next available index for format queries.
requirements: desc.mDescription.id must be unique among already-registered formats; otherwise registration fails.
Registered formats are limited to the lifetime and scope of this Exporter instance.

functions.name: Assimp::Exporter::UnregisterExporter
functions.description: Unregisters an export format (built-in or custom) by its format id for this Exporter instance.
requirements: id must refer to an 'id' of an aiExportFormatDesc previously registered with this Exporter; calling with an unknown id has no effect.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::ExportProperties
functions.description: Constructs an empty set of export configuration properties used to influence exporter behavior.
requirements: None.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::ExportProperties
functions.description: Copy-constructs an ExportProperties, duplicating all configuration properties from another instance.
requirements: other must be a valid ExportProperties instance.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyInteger
functions.description: Sets an integer configuration property by name. Returns true if the property was already set (and thus replaced).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Properties of different types are stored independently; setting an integer does not affect properties of other types.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyBool
functions.description: Sets a boolean configuration property. Booleans are stored in the integer property map.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
May be queried via GetPropertyBool or GetPropertyInteger.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyFloat
functions.description: Sets a floating-point configuration property by name. Returns true if the property was already set (and thus replaced).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Setting a float does not affect properties of other types.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyString
functions.description: Sets a string configuration property by name. Returns true if the property was already set (and thus replaced).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Setting a string does not affect properties of other types.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyMatrix
functions.description: Sets a matrix configuration property by name. Returns true if the property was already set (and thus replaced).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Setting a matrix does not affect properties of other types.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::SetPropertyCallback
functions.description: Sets a callback configuration property by name, storing a function of signature void*(void*).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
f must be callable as void*(void*).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyInteger
functions.description: Gets an integer configuration property by name. Returns iErrorReturn if the property is not found.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyBool
functions.signature: bool Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyBool(const char *szName, bool bErrorReturn = false) const
functions.description: Gets a boolean configuration property by name. Returns bErrorReturn if not found. Internally reads from the integer property map.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyFloat
functions.description: Gets a floating-point configuration property by name. Returns fErrorReturn if the property is not found.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyString
functions.signature: const std::string Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyString(const char *szName, const std::string &sErrorReturn = "") const
functions.description: Gets a string configuration property by name. Returns sErrorReturn if not found. The returned value remains valid until the property is modified.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Caller should not assume the returned string remains valid after the property is next modified.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyMatrix
functions.signature: const aiMatrix4x4 Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyMatrix(const char *szName, const aiMatrix4x4 &sErrorReturn = aiMatrix4x4()) const
functions.description: Gets a matrix configuration property by name. Returns sErrorReturn if not found. The returned value remains valid until the property is modified.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).
Caller should not assume the returned matrix remains valid after the property is next modified.

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::GetPropertyCallback
functions.description: Gets a callback configuration property by name (function of signature void*(void*)). Returns an empty function if not found.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyInteger
functions.description: Checks whether an integer property with the given name has been set.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyBool
functions.description: Checks whether a boolean property with the given name has been set (stored in the integer map).
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyFloat
functions.description: Checks whether a floating-point property with the given name has been set.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyString
functions.description: Checks whether a string property with the given name has been set.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyMatrix
functions.description: Checks whether a matrix property with the given name has been set.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::ExportProperties::HasPropertyCallback
functions.description: Checks whether a callback property with the given name has been set.
requirements: szName must be a non-null property name (AI_CONFIG_XXX).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::DefaultIOStream
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates a DefaultIOStream not bound to any file handle. All subsequent I/O operations will fail but the instance can be safely used and destroyed. Intended for later association by the IOSystem or as a placeholder.
requirements: No valid FILE* is attached after construction; callers must expect all I/O methods to fail until a file handle is associated (per class note).
Object can be created and destroyed without additional setup.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::~DefaultIOStream
functions.description: Destructor. Closes the underlying FILE* if one is attached and releases resources. Public to allow simple deletion to close the file.
requirements: After destruction the FILE* is no longer valid; callers must not use the stream or underlying FILE* afterwards.
Do not manually close the FILE* owned by this stream before destruction to avoid double-close.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Read
functions.signature: size_t Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Read(void* pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount)
functions.description: Reads up to pCount items of size pSize from the stream into pvBuffer, returning the number of items successfully read. Semantics mirror fread on the underlying FILE*. If no file is attached, the call fails (returns 0).
requirements: pvBuffer must point to a writable memory block of at least pSize * pCount bytes when pSize > 0 and pCount > 0.
pSize and pCount may be zero; in that case no bytes are read and the function returns 0.
The stream must have a valid file handle attached for the read to succeed; otherwise expect a short read (0).
Callers must check the return value to detect EOF or partial reads.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Write
functions.signature: size_t Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Write(const void* pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount)
functions.description: Writes up to pCount items of size pSize from pvBuffer to the stream, returning the number of items successfully written. Semantics mirror fwrite on the underlying FILE*. If no file is attached, the call fails (returns 0).
requirements: pvBuffer must point to a readable memory block of at least pSize * pCount bytes when pSize > 0 and pCount > 0.
pSize and pCount may be zero; in that case no bytes are written and the function returns 0.
The stream must have a valid file handle attached and opened with write permissions for the write to succeed; otherwise expect a short write (possibly 0).
Callers must check the return value to detect partial writes or failures.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Seek
functions.description: Changes the current file position according to pOrigin (begin, current, end) and offset pOffset. Returns an aiReturn status indicating success or failure. Semantics mirror fseek on the underlying FILE*.
requirements: The stream must have a valid file handle attached for the seek to succeed.
pOrigin must be a valid aiOrigin value (e.g., aiOrigin_SET, aiOrigin_CUR, aiOrigin_END).
pOffset must be representable as the platform’s file offset for the underlying FILE*; large offsets or seeking before start are invalid and will fail.
Callers must check the aiReturn result to handle errors.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current file position as a byte offset from the beginning of the file. Mirrors ftell on the underlying FILE*. If no file is attached, the value is implementation-defined/unknown.
requirements: The stream should have a valid file handle attached to obtain a meaningful position.
Callers should be prepared to handle error/invalid positions according to library behavior (exact error signaling is not documented here).

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::FileSize
functions.description: Returns the total size of the file in bytes. May use cached size. If no file is attached, the returned value is unspecified/unknown.
requirements: The stream should have a valid file handle attached to obtain the actual size.
Callers should not assume a particular value on error; verify results as appropriate.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOStream::Flush
functions.description: Flushes the stream’s buffered output to the underlying file (equivalent to fflush on the FILE*). No effect if no file is attached.
requirements: The stream should have a valid file handle attached for flushing to have an effect.
No return value; callers cannot directly detect failure; handle I/O errors via subsequent operations as needed.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOSystem::Exists
functions.signature: bool Assimp::DefaultIOSystem::Exists(const char* pFile) const override
functions.description: Checks whether a file exists at the given path using the platform’s standard C file APIs. Use to guard file operations before opening a file.
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer; passing null is invalid.
The path may be absolute or relative; behavior depends on current working directory and OS-specific rules.
Return value is true if a file (or path) is found accessible per the IOSystem’s policy; false otherwise.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOSystem::getOsSeparator
functions.description: Returns the operating system’s directory separator character used by this IOSystem (for example, '/' on POSIX or '\\' on Windows). Useful for building and normalizing paths.
requirements: No input parameters; can be called at any time after a DefaultIOSystem instance is constructed.

functions.name: Assimp::DefaultIOSystem::Open
functions.signature: Assimp::IOStream* Assimp::DefaultIOSystem::Open(const char* pFile, const char* pMode = "rb") override
functions.description: Opens a file at the given path with the provided stdio-style mode string and returns an IOStream for reading/writing through Assimp’s I/O abstraction. Typical usage is to open assets for reading using the default mode "rb".
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated C string path; null is invalid.

functions.name: Assimp::fast_atoreal_move
functions.signature:
template <typename Real, typename ExceptionType = Assimp::DeadlyImportError>
inline const char* Assimp::fast_atoreal_move(const char* c, Real& out, bool check_comma = true)
functions.description: High-performance parser for floating-point literals. Parses an optional sign, special values "nan"/"inf" (case-insensitive; "infinity" also recognized), an integer part, an optional fractional part (using '.' or, if check_comma is true, ',' as decimal separator), and an optional exponent 'e' or 'E' with optional sign. Reads up to AI_FAST_ATOF_RELAVANT_DECIMALS fractional digits to limit precision loss, then applies exponent via pow(10,exp). Stores the parsed value in out and returns a pointer to the first unconsumed character. Throws ExceptionType if the input does not start with a digit or a valid decimal point followed by a digit (unless it matches the special forms).
requirements: c must be a valid, non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated character buffer.
On entry, c may start with '+' or '-' to indicate sign.
Special tokens: starting with "nan" yields a quiet NaN; starting with "inf" or "infinity" yields ±infinity according to the sign. The parser consumes the matched characters.
If the number starts with a decimal separator ('.' or ',' when check_comma is true), the next character must be a digit; otherwise ExceptionType is thrown.
If an exponent 'e' or 'E' is present, it may be followed by an optional sign and must be followed by at least one digit; otherwise ExceptionType is thrown by the underlying integer parser.
If check_comma is true, ',' is accepted as the decimal separator in the fractional part; trailing '.' is consumed for backward compatibility, but trailing ',' is not.
out must be a valid reference; it will be assigned the parsed value. The function returns the pointer to the first unparsed character for continued scanning.
Template parameter Real must be a floating-point type capable of representing the result; ExceptionType must be constructible from message fragments used by Assimp for error reporting.
