Function is pure and has no side effects; callers should use the boolean return to branch as needed.

functions.name: is_special_float
functions.description: Returns true if the input float is NaN or ±∞ (i.e., exponent is all ones). Denormal/subnormal values return false and are treated as normal values. Uses a bitwise exponent check via an internal IEEE-754 layout union.
requirements: Argument in may be any 32-bit IEEE-754 float bit pattern; no initialization beyond a valid float object is required.
Function is pure and has no side effects; callers should use the boolean return to branch as needed.

functions.name: is_not_qnan
functions.description: Returns true if the input is not a quiet NaN. Thin wrapper that negates the result of is_qnan(in). Intended for convenience in generic code.
requirements: TReal must be a type for which a viable overload of is_qnan can be called via argument-dependent conversion (typically float or double, or types implicitly convertible to one of them).
Argument in may be any valid value of TReal satisfying the above.
Function is pure and has no side effects; callers should use the boolean return to branch as needed.

functions.name: get_qnan
functions.description: Returns a quiet NaN value of type ai_real (Assimp’s real-number typedef). Implemented using std::numeric_limits<ai_real>::quiet_NaN(). Useful for initializing or marking undefined numeric data.
requirements: ai_real must be a floating-point type that supports std::numeric_limits<T>::quiet_NaN() (as defined by the Assimp configuration).
Callers should be prepared to handle NaN semantics (comparisons with NaN are false except !=, NaN propagation in arithmetic, etc.).

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::BaseImporter
functions.description: Constructs a BaseImporter. Used internally by Assimp::Importer. No side effects beyond member initialization.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::~BaseImporter
functions.description: Destroys a BaseImporter instance. Defaulted destructor; performs standard cleanup of members.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::CanRead
functions.signature: virtual bool Assimp::BaseImporter::CanRead(const std::string &pFile, Assimp::IOSystem *pIOHandler, bool checkSig) const = 0
functions.description: Determine whether this importer can handle the format of the given file. Implementations are expected to perform a structural/magic check (often by inspecting header bytes) and return true if the format is recognized.
requirements: Implementations should perform a case-insensitive search or magic check as appropriate for the format (per comments).
Parameter pIOHandler is the IO system to use for file access; it must be valid for any file reads performed by the implementation.
Parameter checkSig is legacy and should not be relied upon by callers (may be ignored by implementations).

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::ReadFile
functions.description: Import the specified file and return the populated aiScene on success, or nullptr on failure. This wrapper calls InternReadFile() and catches exceptions, ensuring partially constructed data is discarded and error state is captured (retrievable via GetErrorText()/GetException()). Not intended to be overridden by importers.
requirements: On success, ownership of the returned aiScene is transferred to the caller.
On failure, returns nullptr; callers can query GetErrorText() for a human-readable error and GetException() for the captured exception (if any).
pImp must be the Importer hosting this loader (used internally).
pIOHandler is used to open the main and auxiliary files; it must be suitable for any file reads performed during import.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::GetErrorText
functions.description: Retrieve the text description of the last error, if any. Returns an empty string if no error occurred.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::GetException
functions.description: Retrieve the last captured exception (if any) from a previous import attempt. Not all errors originate from exceptions; consult GetErrorText() as well.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::SetupProperties
functions.description: Hook called before ReadFile() to let the importer update its configuration from the Importer’s property list.
requirements: pImp points to the Importer providing configuration properties and must remain valid for the duration of this call.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::GetInfo
functions.description: Return a static description of this importer’s capabilities and supported file extensions. Importers must implement this.
requirements: Implementations must return a valid aiImporterDesc pointer describing the loader and its extensions.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::SetFileScale
functions.description: Set a per-file scale factor, used by the scaling process when requested.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::GetExtensionList
functions.description: Insert all file extensions supported by this importer into the provided set, using the information from GetInfo().
requirements: Caller provides a reference to a std::set<std::string> to receive extensions; it will be appended to.
Requires GetInfo() to provide an extension list; if none, no entries are added.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::SearchFileHeaderForToken
functions.signature: static bool Assimp::BaseImporter::SearchFileHeaderForToken(Assimp::IOSystem *pIOSystem, const std::string &file, const char **tokens, std::size_t numTokens, unsigned int searchBytes = 200, bool tokensSol = false, bool noGraphBeforeTokens = false)
functions.description: Utility for CanRead(): scan the beginning of a text file for any of the specified tokens in a case-insensitive manner (with rudimentary UNICODE handling). Returns true if any token is found within the first searchBytes.
requirements: pIOSystem must be valid and capable of opening the file path provided in file.
tokens must point to an array of C strings of length numTokens; each C string must be null-terminated.
searchBytes specifies how many bytes from the start of the file to search.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::SimpleExtensionCheck
functions.signature: static bool Assimp::BaseImporter::SimpleExtensionCheck(const std::string &pFile, const char *ext0, const char *ext1 = nullptr, const char *ext2 = nullptr, const char *ext3 = nullptr)
functions.description: Check whether pFile ends with one of up to four specified extensions. Case-insensitive. Intended for quick extension-based format checks.
requirements: ext0 must be a non-null, lowercase extension string without a leading dot.
Optional ext1, ext2, ext3 (if provided) should also be lowercase and provided without a leading dot.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::HasExtension
functions.signature: static bool Assimp::BaseImporter::HasExtension(const std::string &pFile, const std::set<std::string> &extensions)
functions.description: Check whether pFile has any extension listed in extensions. Case-insensitive.
requirements: The extensions set should contain lowercase extensions without leading dots.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::GetExtension
functions.description: Extract the file extension (without dot) from pFile and return it in lowercase.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::CheckMagicToken
functions.signature: static bool Assimp::BaseImporter::CheckMagicToken(Assimp::IOSystem *pIOHandler, const std::string &pFile, const void *magic, std::size_t num, unsigned int offset = 0, unsigned int size = 4)
functions.description: Check whether the file at pFile contains any of the provided magic tokens at the given byte offset. For convenience, tokens of size 2 or 4 are also checked in byte-swapped (big-endian) form. Returns true on any match.
requirements: pIOHandler must be valid and able to open file.
magic must point to a contiguous array of num tokens, each of length size bytes.
size must be at most 16 bytes.
offset specifies the byte position from the start of the file where tokens are expected.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::ConvertToUTF8
functions.description: Convert the contents of data (assumed to be a text file buffer) to UTF-8 in place. The buffer may be resized. Conversion errors are reported but ignored.
requirements: data should contain the entire file content to be converted; it will be modified in place.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::ConvertUTF8toISO8859_1
functions.description: Convert the UTF-8 text in data to ISO-8859-1 in place. The string may be resized. Conversion errors are reported but ignored.
requirements: data should contain UTF-8 encoded text and will be modified in place.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::TextFileToBuffer
functions.signature: static void Assimp::BaseImporter::TextFileToBuffer(Assimp::IOStream *stream, std::vector<char> &data, Assimp::BaseImporter::TextFileMode mode = Assimp::BaseImporter::FORBID_EMPTY)
functions.description: Read a text file from stream into data and convert it to UTF-8 representation. The output buffer is resized as needed and terminated with a binary 0. Empty files can be allowed or forbidden via mode.
requirements: stream must be a valid IOStream for reading the file content.
data is an output buffer that will be resized and populated; its previous contents will be overwritten.
If mode is FORBID_EMPTY, the implementation will report an error if the file is empty (the exact behavior beyond reporting is not detailed).

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::CopyVector
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static AI_FORCE_INLINE void Assimp::BaseImporter::CopyVector(std::vector<T> &vec, T *&out, unsigned int &outLength)
functions.description: Move the contents of a std::vector<T> into a newly allocated C array of T. Sets outLength to the element count and assigns out to the new array. Elements are moved via std::swap_ranges, leaving vec elements in a moved-from state.
requirements: On entry, out is ignored and will be assigned to a newly allocated array via new T[outLength] when vec is non-empty.
Caller takes ownership of out and must release it with delete[] when no longer needed.
outLength is set to static_cast<unsigned int>(vec.size()).
vec will be logically emptied/moved-from; do not rely on its previous contents after the call.

functions.name: Assimp::BaseImporter::CopyVector
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static AI_FORCE_INLINE void Assimp::BaseImporter::CopyVector(std::vector<std::unique_ptr<T>> &vec, T **&out, unsigned int &outLength)
functions.description: Move the contents of a std::vector<std::unique_ptr<T>> into a newly allocated array of raw pointers T*. Each unique_ptr is released into the output array. Sets outLength to the count.
requirements: On entry, out is ignored and will be assigned to a newly allocated array via new T*[outLength] when vec is non-empty.
Caller takes ownership of the array and all pointed-to T objects: delete each T* and delete[] the pointer array when no longer needed.
outLength is set to static_cast<unsigned int>(vec.size()).
Each unique_ptr in vec is released; after the call those unique_ptrs become empty.

functions.name: SuperFastHash
functions.signature: inline uint32_t SuperFastHash(const char* data, uint32_t len = 0, uint32_t hash = 0)
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit hash of a byte sequence using Paul Hsieh’s SuperFastHash (incremental version). If len is 0, the function treats data as a NUL-terminated C-string and hashes up to the first '\0'. The hash parameter is an initial seed that enables incremental hashing (e.g., hashing chunks in sequence by feeding the previous result as the next seed). If data is null, the function returns 0. Pure, reentrant, and does not allocate memory.
requirements: data must not be null unless the caller intentionally wants a return value of 0.
If len == 0, data must point to a valid NUL-terminated string (reachable by strlen without reading out of bounds).
If len > 0, data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.

On platforms where get16bits is defined as dereferencing a const uint16_t* (e.g., many x86/x64 compilers), data should be suitably aligned for 16-bit reads to avoid undefined behavior on architectures that require alignment.
The seed parameter hash can be any 32-bit value; for incremental hashing, pass the previous hash output as the next call’s hash input.
The function performs read-only access; the buffer pointed to by data must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::MemoryIOStream
functions.signature: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::MemoryIOStream(const uint8_t* buff, size_t len, bool own = false)
functions.description: Constructor for a read-only IOStream that serves data directly from a caller-provided memory buffer. Use to adapt an in-memory blob to Assimp’s IOStream interface. If own is true, the stream will delete[] the buffer in its destructor; otherwise the caller retains ownership and must keep the buffer valid for the stream’s lifetime.
requirements: buff must point to at least len bytes of valid readable memory.
If own is true, buff must have been allocated with new[] (array form) and must be the exact pointer to that allocation; the stream will delete[] it in the destructor.
If own is false, the caller must ensure the buffer remains alive and unchanged for the entire lifetime of the MemoryIOStream instance.
len can be zero; in that case Read will always return 0 and Seek bounds are based on length==0.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::~MemoryIOStream
functions.description: Destructor. If constructed with own == true, deletes the underlying buffer with delete[]. Otherwise, no buffer ownership action is taken.
requirements: Do not use the stream after destruction.
If own was true, the provided buffer must have been allocated with new[] and must not be freed elsewhere (to avoid double free).

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Read
functions.signature: size_t Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Read(void* pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount)
functions.description: Reads up to pCount items of size pSize from the internal memory buffer into pvBuffer, advancing the read position. Returns the number of complete items read. Stops at end-of-buffer without error.
requirements: pvBuffer must be non-null (enforced by ai_assert).
pSize must be non-zero (enforced by ai_assert).
The function may return fewer than pCount items if there is not enough data remaining.
The read position advances by pSize * returned_count bytes; subsequent reads continue from the new position.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Write
functions.description: Write is not supported for MemoryIOStream; this is a read-only stream. The implementation asserts false and returns 0.
requirements: Callers must not rely on writing; this function is effectively unsupported.
Invoking Write may trigger an assertion failure in debug builds.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Seek
functions.description: Moves the current read position according to pOrigin and pOffset within the in-memory buffer. Returns AI_SUCCESS on success or AI_FAILURE if the resulting position would be out of bounds.
requirements: If pOrigin is aiOrigin_SET, pOffset must be <= length of the buffer.
If pOrigin is aiOrigin_END, pOffset must be <= length of the buffer (position becomes length - pOffset).
If pOrigin is aiOrigin_CUR, (pOffset + current_position) must be <= length of the buffer.
On AI_FAILURE, the position is not modified (per code paths shown).

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current read position (byte offset from the start) within the internal buffer.
requirements: None beyond having a valid MemoryIOStream instance.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::FileSize
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the underlying memory buffer.
requirements: None beyond having a valid MemoryIOStream instance.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOStream::Flush
functions.description: No-op for this read-only stream. The implementation asserts false; there is nothing to flush.
requirements: Callers should not call Flush on this read-only stream; it may assert in debug builds.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::MemoryIOSystem
functions.signature: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::MemoryIOSystem(const uint8_t* buff, size_t len, IOSystem* io)
functions.description: Constructs an IOSystem that serves a single in-memory file when accessed with a special magic filename, while delegating all other IO operations to an existing IOSystem (io). Useful to feed a memory buffer to APIs that expect file-based IO.
requirements: buff must point to at least len bytes of valid readable memory for as long as any created MemoryIOStream may exist.
io may be null; in that case, only the magic in-memory file is available and all other operations will behave conservatively (typically false/null/empty).
The buffer is not owned by the MemoryIOSystem or created streams in this path (streams created via Open use own=false); the caller retains ownership and lifetime management.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::~MemoryIOSystem
functions.description: Destructor. Defaulted. Cleans up any streams created via Open by relying on Close or normal container destruction during object teardown.
requirements: Ensure any streams created by this IOSystem are closed (Close) or that the IOSystem outlives its created streams to avoid dangling pointers.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::Exists
functions.description: Reports whether a path exists. Returns true if pFile matches the magic in-memory filename; otherwise defers to the wrapped IOSystem if present.
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated string.
If pFile equals the magic filename "$$$___magic___$$$" (length 17), the function returns true regardless of the wrapped IO system.
If existing_io is null and pFile is not the magic filename, returns false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::getOsSeparator
functions.description: Returns the directory separator character. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem when available; otherwise returns '/'.
requirements: None beyond having a valid MemoryIOSystem instance.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::Open
functions.signature: Assimp::IOStream* Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::Open(const char* pFile, const char* pMode = "rb")
functions.description: Opens a file. If pFile matches the magic filename, returns a new MemoryIOStream over the provided buffer; pMode is ignored for the magic case. Otherwise delegates to the wrapped IOSystem. Keeps track of streams it created to manage Close correctly.
requirements: pFile must be a valid, null-terminated string.
If opening the magic filename, the returned stream is owned by the caller and must be closed via MemoryIOSystem::Close; it is a read-only MemoryIOStream and does not own the buffer.
If opening a non-magic path and existing_io is null, the function returns nullptr.
pMode may be any string but is ignored for the magic filename path.
Each successful Open for the magic filename adds the created stream to internal tracking; callers should not delete it directly but should call Close.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::Close
functions.description: Closes a file stream. If pFile was created by this MemoryIOSystem (for the magic filename), it deletes the stream and removes it from internal tracking. Otherwise delegates to the wrapped IOSystem if present.
requirements: pFile must be a pointer previously returned by an Open call, either from this MemoryIOSystem or the wrapped IOSystem.
Do not pass the same pFile twice; after Close it is invalid.
If pFile corresponds to a created magic-file stream, callers must use this Close (not manual delete) to ensure internal tracking is updated.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::ComparePaths
functions.signature: bool Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::ComparePaths(const char* one, const char* second) const
functions.description: Compares two paths for equivalence. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem when available; otherwise returns false.
requirements: one and second must be valid, null-terminated strings when delegating.
If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, comparison will always return false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::PushDirectory
functions.description: Pushes a directory onto an internal directory stack. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns false.
requirements: path must be a valid directory path as expected by the wrapped IOSystem when delegating.
If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, this will return false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::CurrentDirectory
functions.description: Returns the current directory from the top of the internal directory stack. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns a reference to a static empty string.
requirements: If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, the returned reference refers to an internal static empty string; callers must not attempt to modify or store it beyond typical const-reference use.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::StackSize
functions.description: Returns the size of the directory stack. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns 0.
requirements: None beyond having a valid MemoryIOSystem instance.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::PopDirectory
functions.description: Pops the top directory from the internal directory stack. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns false.
requirements: If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, this will return false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::CreateDirectory
functions.description: Creates a directory. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns false.
requirements: path must be a valid directory path as expected by the wrapped IOSystem when delegating.
If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, this will return false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::ChangeDirectory
functions.description: Changes the current working directory. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns false.
requirements: path must be a valid directory path as expected by the wrapped IOSystem when delegating.
If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, this will return false.

functions.name: Assimp::MemoryIOSystem::DeleteFile
functions.description: Deletes a file by path. Delegates to the wrapped IOSystem; otherwise returns false.
requirements: file must be a valid file path as expected by the wrapped IOSystem when delegating.
If no wrapped IOSystem is provided, this will return false.

functions.name: Assimp::IsUpper
functions.description: Returns true if the given character is an ASCII uppercase letter ('A'..'Z'). Locale-independent. Works with any character type that can represent ASCII values.
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined (non-ASCII behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::IsLower
functions.description: Returns true if the given character is an ASCII lowercase letter ('a'..'z'). Locale-independent. Works with any character type that can represent ASCII values.
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined (non-ASCII behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::IsSpace
functions.description: Returns true if the character is an ASCII space or horizontal tab (' ' or '\t').
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined (non-ASCII behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::IsLineEnd
functions.description: Returns true if the character denotes an end-of-line or terminator: CR ('\r'), LF ('\n'), NUL ('\0'), or form feed ('\f').
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined (non-ASCII behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::IsSpaceOrNewLine
functions.description: Returns true if the character is whitespace as defined by IsSpace or an end-of-line as defined by IsLineEnd.
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined (non-ASCII behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::SkipSpaces
functions.signature: template <class char_t> bool Assimp::SkipSpaces(const char_t *in, const char_t **out, const char_t *end)
functions.description: Skips ASCII spaces and tabs starting at in up to end, writes the first non-space position to out, and returns whether the current character is not a line end. Intended for in/out parsing over a bounded buffer.
requirements: in must be a valid readable pointer and strictly before end (in < end); the function dereferences *in before comparing with end.
end must point to the one-past-the-last element of the readable range.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the advanced position.
The memory at in..end must be readable until a non-space/tab or end is reached.
Behavior is defined only for ASCII spaces/tabs; content may be NUL-terminated but is not required.

functions.name: Assimp::SkipLine
functions.signature: template <class char_t> bool Assimp::SkipLine(const char_t *in, const char_t **out, const char_t *end)
functions.description: Advances the input to the start of the next line by scanning until a comment start ('#') or line end (CR/LF/NUL) or end is reached, then skips trailing CR/LF. Writes the resulting position to out. Returns false only if NUL is hit at the resulting position.
requirements: in must be a valid readable pointer and strictly before end (in < end); the function dereferences *in before comparing with end.
end must point to the one-past-the-last element of the readable range.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the advanced position.
Input must be readable until a line end, comment marker '#', or end is reached.
Files are assumed opened in binary; both CR and LF may appear.

functions.name: Assimp::SkipSpacesAndLineEnd
functions.signature: template <class char_t> bool Assimp::SkipSpacesAndLineEnd(const char_t *in, const char_t **out, const char_t *end)
functions.description: Skips ASCII spaces, tabs, and line-end characters (CR/LF) starting at in up to end, writes the first non-skipped position to out, and returns whether the current character is not NUL.
requirements: in must be a valid readable pointer and strictly before end (in < end); the function dereferences *in before comparing with end.
end must point to the one-past-the-last element of the readable range.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the advanced position.
The memory at in..end must be readable until a non-space/tab/CR/LF or end is reached.

functions.name: Assimp::GetNextLine
functions.signature: template <class char_t> bool Assimp::GetNextLine(const char_t *&buffer, char_t out[BufferSize])
functions.description: Copies the next line from buffer into out (up to BufferSize-1 chars), stopping at CR/LF/NUL. Appends a NUL terminator. Advances buffer past any trailing line-end characters. Returns false only if buffer already points to NUL at entry.
requirements: buffer must point to a NUL-terminated character sequence; there is no end pointer and the function dereferences *buffer.
out must reference writable storage for at least BufferSize elements to accommodate the copied line and terminating NUL.
Only ASCII line-end characters (CR/LF) are recognized in addition to NUL.
The function stops copying when either a line end is encountered or the output buffer would overflow (it reserves one byte for NUL).

functions.name: Assimp::IsNumeric
functions.description: Returns true if the character is an ASCII digit ('0'..'9') or a sign ('-' or '+'). Intended for quick numeric token detection.
requirements: Input character must be comparable to ASCII codes; only ASCII semantics are defined.

functions.name: Assimp::TokenMatch
functions.signature: template <class char_t> bool Assimp::TokenMatch(char_t *&in, const char *token, unsigned int len)
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer at in begins with token[0..len-1] and the next character is whitespace or line end. If matched, advances in by len plus one delimiter (if present); otherwise leaves in unchanged. Returns true on match.
requirements: in must point to a readable C-style buffer with at least len bytes plus one extra byte readable to examine in[len].
token must point to a readable buffer with at least len bytes.
len must not exceed the actual lengths of token and the available data at in; ::strncmp is used for comparison.
The character at in[len] must be a space, tab, CR, LF, NUL, or similar as defined by IsSpaceOrNewLine; if it is NUL, the pointer is advanced only by len.
Although templated, the implementation uses ::strncmp and IsSpaceOrNewLine with char semantics; practical use requires char_t to be char or a type compatible with char data.

functions.name: Assimp::TokenMatchI
functions.signature: bool Assimp::TokenMatchI(const char *&in, const char *token, unsigned int len)
functions.description: Case-insensitive version of TokenMatch using ASSIMP_strincmp. If token[0..len-1] matches at in and the next character is whitespace or line end, advances in by len+1 and returns true; otherwise returns false.
requirements: in must point to a readable C-style buffer with at least len+1 bytes readable to examine in[0..len].
token must point to a readable buffer with at least len bytes.
len must not exceed the actual lengths used in comparison; ASSIMP_strincmp assumes len bytes are readable at both pointers.
The character at in[len] must be a space, tab, CR, LF, or NUL as defined by IsSpaceOrNewLine; the function unconditionally advances by len+1 on match.

functions.name: Assimp::SkipToken
functions.description: Skips leading spaces/tabs and then advances in to the end of the next non-whitespace token (stopping before the following space or line end).
requirements: in must be a valid readable pointer and strictly before end at call time; the function dereferences *in before comparing with end inside helpers/loops.
end must point to the one-past-the-last element of the readable range.
The memory at in..end must be readable until whitespace or end is reached.

functions.name: Assimp::GetNextToken
functions.description: Skips any spaces and line ends, then returns the next token as a std::string (characters up to the next space or line end). Advances in to the first delimiter after the token.
requirements: in must be a valid readable pointer and strictly before end at call time; the function dereferences *in before comparing with end in loops.
end must point to the one-past-the-last element of the readable range.
The memory at in..end must be readable until a space/line-end delimiter or end is reached.
Tokens are split on ASCII whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF).

functions.name: Assimp::tokenize
functions.signature: template <class string_type> unsigned int Assimp::tokenize(const string_type &str, std::vector<string_type> &tokens, const string_type &delimiters)
functions.description: Splits str into tokens separated by any character in delimiters using string_type::find_first_not_of/find_first_of. Non-empty tokens not starting with a space are appended to tokens. Returns the number of tokens collected.
requirements: string_type must provide npos, size_type, find_first_not_of, find_first_of, substr, empty, operator[], and be copyable into std::vector<string_type>.
tokens must be a valid vector reference; it will be appended to (not cleared).
delimiters defines the set of separator characters; tokens beginning with a space character are filtered out by the implementation.

functions.name: Assimp::ai_stdStrToLower
functions.description: Returns a lowercase copy of the input string by applying tolower to each byte using unsigned-char promotion. Locale-dependent tolower from <cctype> is used, but input is treated as bytes; multi-byte encodings are not handled specially.
requirements: Input may contain arbitrary bytes; transformation is applied per-byte via standard tolower((unsigned char)c).
No side effects on the input string; the function allocates and returns a new std::string of the same size.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::StreamReader
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::StreamReader(std::shared_ptr<Assimp::IOStream> stream, bool le = false)
functions.description: Constructs a StreamReader over the remaining content of an IOStream, reading from the stream’s current position to EOF. The reader buffers the data in memory and reads values with a fixed or runtime-selected endianness (le is only used when RuntimeSwitch is true).
requirements: stream must not be null; otherwise a DeadlyImportError is thrown.
Construction fails with DeadlyImportError if the stream cannot be opened, if FileSize()-Tell() is 0, or if the stream is already at EOF.
The reader reads the remainder of the stream starting at the current file position; callers should position the IOStream as needed before construction.
If RuntimeSwitch is true, 'le' must correctly indicate the byte order of the source data; if false, 'le' is ignored.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::~StreamReader
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::~StreamReader()
functions.description: Destructor; releases the internally allocated buffer and the held stream reference.
requirements: All pointers obtained via GetPtr become invalid after destruction.
No explicit caller action required; invoked when the object goes out of scope or is deleted.
