functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::GetRemainingSize
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
size_t Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::GetRemainingSize() const
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes remaining from the current read position to the end of the buffered stream.
requirements: None beyond a valid constructed reader.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::GetRemainingSizeToLimit
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
size_t Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::GetRemainingSizeToLimit() const
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes remaining from the current position to the currently set read limit. If no custom limit is set, this equals the remaining size to the end of the stream.
requirements: A read limit may optionally have been set via SetReadLimit; otherwise it returns the remaining size to EOF.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::IncPtr
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
void Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::IncPtr(intptr_t plus)
functions.description: Advances (or retreats, if negative) the current read pointer by the specified offset. Throws if advancing goes past the current read limit.
requirements: The resulting position must not exceed the current read limit; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.
Note: The implementation does not guard against moving before the beginning of the buffer; callers should avoid negative seeks that would underflow the start.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::GetPtr
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
int8_t* Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::GetPtr() const
functions.description: Returns a raw pointer to the current position in the internal buffer for manual pointer-based access.
requirements: The returned pointer is only valid while the StreamReader remains alive.
Callers must ensure any subsequent pointer arithmetic and reads remain within [buffer start, current read limit]; out-of-bounds use can cause exceptions or undefined behavior.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::SetPtr
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
void Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::SetPtr(int8_t* p)
functions.description: Sets the current read pointer to p after validating that it lies within the valid buffer range up to the current read limit.
requirements: p must be within [buffer start, current read limit]; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.
p should be a pointer previously obtained from GetPtr or derived from it via safe arithmetic.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::CopyAndAdvance
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
void Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::CopyAndAdvance(void* out, size_t bytes)
functions.description: Copies bytes from the current position into an external buffer and advances the current pointer by that number of bytes. Bounds are validated via SetPtr.
requirements: There must be at least 'bytes' bytes remaining to the read limit; otherwise SetPtr will throw DeadlyImportError.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least 'bytes' bytes.
out must not be null.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::GetCurrentPos
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
int Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::GetCurrentPos() const
functions.description: Returns the byte offset of the current read position from the start of the buffered stream.
requirements: None beyond a valid constructed reader.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::SetCurrentPos
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
void Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndiannness, RuntimeSwitch>::SetCurrentPos(size_t pos)
functions.description: Sets the current read position to the given byte offset from the start of the buffered stream by adjusting the internal pointer.
requirements: pos must translate to a pointer within [buffer start, current read limit]; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::SetReadLimit
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
unsigned int Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::SetReadLimit(unsigned int _limit)
functions.description: Sets a temporary read limit measured from the start of the buffer. Attempts to read beyond this limit will throw. Passing UINT_MAX resets the limit to the end of the buffered stream. Returns the previously set limit.
requirements: _limit must be <= total buffered size; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.
To remove a custom limit, pass UINT_MAX.
Callers should handle the returned previous limit if they plan to restore it later.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::GetReadLimit
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
unsigned int Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::GetReadLimit() const
functions.description: Returns the current read limit in bytes from the start of the buffer.
requirements: None.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::SkipToReadLimit
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
void Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::SkipToReadLimit()
functions.description: Moves the current read pointer to the current read limit, effectively skipping all remaining bytes up to the limit.
requirements: A read limit must be set for meaningful effect; otherwise it jumps to EOF (default limit).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::operator>>
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
template <typename T>
Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>& Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::operator>>(T& f)
functions.description: Extraction operator that reads a value of type T from the stream using Get<T>(), storing it in f. Allows chaining of >> operations.
requirements: There must be at least sizeof(T) bytes remaining to the current read limit; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.
T must be supported by Intern::Getter (and effectively by ByteSwapper) for byte-order handling, and safe to memcpy into (i.e., trivially copyable POD-like).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamReader::Get
functions.signature:
template <bool SwapEndianness, bool RuntimeSwitch>
template <typename T>
T Assimp::StreamReader<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::Get()
functions.description: Generic typed read. Copies sizeof(T) bytes from the current position into a T, applies endianness handling via Intern::Getter, advances the pointer, and returns the value.
requirements: There must be at least sizeof(T) bytes remaining to the current read limit; otherwise DeadlyImportError is thrown.
T must be compatible with memcpy and the byte-swap mechanism (i.e., ByteSwap::Swap(T*)/Intern::Getter must be defined).
If RuntimeSwitch is true, the runtime little-endian flag provided in the constructor determines byte order; otherwise the compile-time SwapEndianness template parameter applies.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::StreamWriter
functions.description: Constructs a StreamWriter over a writable IOStream with a defined output endianness. Holds a strong shared_ptr reference to the stream and buffers writes until flushed or destruction. The le parameter selects little-endian output only when RuntimeSwitch is true; otherwise endianness is fixed by the template parameter SwapEndianness.
requirements: stream must be non-null (asserted via ai_assert).
stream must refer to an open, writable Assimp::IOStream that supports Write, Flush, Seek, and Tell.
If RuntimeSwitch == true, the caller must pass le=true for little-endian output and le=false for big-endian output; if RuntimeSwitch == false, the le parameter is ignored.
Construction does not reseek the stream; writing continues at the stream’s current cursor position.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::~StreamWriter
functions.description: Destructor that flushes the internal buffer to the underlying IOStream by writing all buffered bytes and calling Flush on the IOStream.
requirements: The underlying IOStream::Write and IOStream::Flush must succeed for data to be fully persisted; errors/exceptions are not handled here.
Do not rely on destructor flushing in contexts where deterministic flushing is required; explicitly call Flush() if needed before destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::Flush
functions.description: Writes the internal buffer to the underlying IOStream, flushes the IOStream, clears the buffer, and resets the internal cursor to 0.
requirements: Underlying IOStream must support Write and Flush operations.

After Flush(), previously buffered data is written and the internal write position is reset, so subsequent Put/PutString calls start at offset 0 of the buffer (current stream position continues from the underlying stream).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::Seek
functions.signature: Assimp::aiReturn Assimp::StreamWriter<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::Seek(std::size_t pOffset, Assimp::aiOrigin pOrigin = aiOrigin_SET)
functions.description: Flushes the internal buffer and seeks the underlying IOStream to the specified offset and origin. Returns the result of IOStream::Seek.
requirements: pOffset and pOrigin must specify a valid target position for the underlying IOStream; seeking outside the stream’s valid range is implementation-defined and may fail.
Calling Seek() flushes any buffered data before performing the seek.
Caller should check the returned aiReturn for success or failure.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::Tell
functions.description: Flushes the internal buffer and returns the current position from the underlying IOStream via IOStream::Tell.
requirements: Underlying IOStream must support Tell().
Calling Tell() flushes any buffered data before querying position.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutF4
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit floating-point value to the stream using the writer’s configured endianness, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type float must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter (provided via ByteSwapper/Intern::Getter).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutF8
functions.description: Writes a 64-bit floating-point value to the stream using the writer’s configured endianness, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type double must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter (provided via ByteSwapper/Intern::Getter).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutI2
functions.description: Writes a signed 16-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type int16_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutI1
functions.description: Writes a signed 8-bit integer to the stream (endianness is irrelevant for 1 byte), buffering the byte until flushed or destroyed.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutI4
functions.description: Writes a signed 32-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type int32_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutI8
functions.description: Writes a signed 64-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type int64_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutU2
functions.description: Writes an unsigned 16-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type uint16_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutU1
functions.description: Writes an unsigned 8-bit integer to the stream (endianness is irrelevant for 1 byte), buffering the byte until flushed or destroyed.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutU4
functions.description: Writes an unsigned 32-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type uint32_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutU8
functions.description: Writes an unsigned 64-bit integer to the stream with proper endianness conversion as configured, buffering the bytes until flushed or destroyed.
requirements: Type uint64_t must be supported by the endianness conversion mechanism used by StreamWriter.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutChar
functions.description: Writes a single character byte to the stream, buffering it until flushed or destroyed.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::PutString
functions.description: Writes the raw bytes of an aiString’s character buffer (exactly s.length bytes, no terminator) into the internal buffer.
requirements: s.length bytes will be written; no null terminator is appended.
s.C_Str() must point to at least s.length valid bytes (aiString should be properly initialized).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
Assimp::StreamWriter<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>& Assimp::StreamWriter<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::operator<<(T f)
functions.description: Streams a value of type T into the writer by delegating to Put(T). Allows chaining via returned reference.
requirements: T must be acceptable to Put(T), which requires that Assimp::Intern::Getter<SwapEndianness, T, RuntimeSwitch> is defined and callable and that endianness handling for T is supported.
Any large or non-trivially copyable T will be memcpy’d as implemented by Put(T); ensure this is intended for custom types.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::GetCurrentPos
functions.description: Returns the current write cursor position within the internal buffer (not the underlying stream position).

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::SetCurrentPos
functions.description: Sets the internal buffer write cursor to a specified position. Subsequent writes will start at this offset within the buffer.
requirements: new_cursor should be within or at the end of the current buffer range; otherwise subsequent writes will trigger buffer growth. The function does not perform bounds checking.

functions.name: Assimp::StreamWriter::Put
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
void Assimp::StreamWriter<SwapEndianness, RuntimeSwitch>::Put(T f)
functions.description: Generic write method that endian-adjusts the value via Intern::Getter and then copies sizeof(T) bytes of f into the internal buffer. This is the underlying implementation for all typed PutX methods and operator<<.
requirements: Assimp::Intern::Getter<SwapEndianness, T, RuntimeSwitch> must be defined and callable with signature void operator()(T*, bool le).
For types requiring byte swapping, the ByteSwapper/Intern infrastructure must support T; otherwise this will fail to compile.
T must be safely memcpy’able; this function copies the object’s raw bytes into the buffer without additional serialization logic.

functions.name: Assimp::ASSIMP_itoa10
functions.signature: unsigned int Assimp::ASSIMP_itoa10(char *out, unsigned int max, int32_t number)
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit signed integer to its base-10 textual representation and writes it into the provided buffer. Returns the length of the written string excluding the terminating NUL. Intended as a small, platform-independent replacement for itoa/sprintf for base-10 output.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to writable memory.
max must be greater than 0 and denotes the maximum number of characters written including the terminating '\0'.
The buffer at out must have space for at least max bytes.
For safe use, max should be large enough to hold the full decimal form of number including sign and terminating '\0' (for int32_t, up to 12 bytes for "-2147483648\0").
Inputs are arbitrary int32_t; negative values are supported (a leading '-' is emitted).

functions.name: Assimp::ASSIMP_stricmp
functions.description: Performs a case-insensitive comparison of two C-style strings in a platform-independent way (maps to _stricmp/strncasecmp as available). Returns 0 if the strings are equal ignoring case; otherwise returns the difference of the first pair of differing characters (implementation-defined sign).
requirements: s1 must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
s2 must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C string.
Return value should be checked: 0 indicates equality ignoring case.

functions.name: Assimp::ASSIMP_strincmp
functions.signature: int Assimp::ASSIMP_strincmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, unsigned int n)
functions.description: Performs a case-insensitive comparison of at most n characters of two C-style strings in a platform-independent way (maps to _strnicmp/strncasecmp as available). Returns 0 if the first n characters are equal ignoring case, or if n == 0.
requirements: s1 must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (or at least n readable characters).
s2 must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C string (or at least n readable characters).
n may be 0; when n == 0 the function returns 0.
Return value should be checked: 0 indicates equality over the compared range ignoring case.

functions.name: Assimp::integer_pow
functions.signature: unsigned int Assimp::integer_pow(unsigned int base, unsigned int power)
functions.description: Computes base raised to the integer exponent power using repeated multiplication. Returns 1 when power is 0. No overflow checking is performed; results wrap according to unsigned int arithmetic.
requirements: base and power are unsigned integers; any values are accepted.
Callers should not rely on overflow checks—ensure the expected result fits in unsigned int if required.

functions.name: ai_snprintf
functions.signature: int ai_snprintf(char *outBuf, size_t size, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Portable snprintf wrapper. On MSVC < 1900 it is provided as an inline function that calls _vsnprintf_s/_vscprintf; on other platforms it aliases to snprintf (or __mingw_snprintf). Use it to format a string into a caller-provided buffer with C printf-style formatting.
requirements: If size > 0, outBuf must point to a valid, writable buffer of at least size bytes (including space for the terminating null).
format must be non-null and contain a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided variadic arguments.
When size == 0, the function returns the number of characters that would have been written; outBuf may be null in this case.
Return value: non-negative number of characters that would have been written (excluding the null terminator) on success; a negative value indicates an encoding/formatting error.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers to avoid undefined behavior.
Behavior and locale/encoding semantics are those of the underlying C library on the target platform.

functions.name: ai_to_string
functions.description: Stream-based conversion of a value to std::string. Uses std::ostringstream and operator<< to serialize the value.
requirements: Type T must be stream-insertable into std::ostream (i.e., there must be an operator<<(std::ostream&, const T&)).
Locale and formatting of the resulting string are determined by the default std::ostringstream settings.

functions.name: ai_strtof
functions.description: Converts a character range or C-string to a float. If end is non-null, parses the substring [begin, end); otherwise uses begin as a null-terminated C-string. Returns 0.0f if begin is null.
requirements: If end is provided, it must point to the same buffer as begin and be >= begin; the function constructs a temporary std::string of length (end - begin).
If end is null, begin must point to a null-terminated C-string.
Parsing is performed via ::atof and is locale-dependent (uses the C library locale).
On invalid input, ::atof semantics apply; function returns 0.0f when begin is null.

functions.name: ai_decimal_to_hexa
functions.description: Converts a value to its hexadecimal representation as an uppercase string using stream formatting (std::hex) and then uppercasing the result.
requirements: Type T must be stream-insertable into std::ostream with std::hex (typically an integral type).
For negative values of signed types, the formatting follows standard iostream rules (a leading '-' may appear).
Output uses uppercase A–F; no 0x prefix is added.

functions.name: ai_rgba2hex
functions.signature: std::string ai_rgba2hex(int r, int g, int b, int a, bool with_head);
functions.description: Formats RGBA components into an 8-hex-digit string (RRGGBBAA). Optionally prefixes the string with '#'. Uses lowercase hex digits and zero-padding to width 8.
requirements: Inputs r, g, b, a are combined as (r << 24) | (g << 16) | (b << 8) | a; values outside 0..255 are not masked and may produce unexpected results.
If with_head is true, the result begins with '#'; otherwise no prefix is included.
Output always has exactly 8 hex digits (plus optional '#').
Hex digit case is lowercase per std::hex default (no explicit uppercasing is applied).

functions.name: ai_trim_left
functions.description: In-place trim of leading whitespace characters from a std::string. Whitespace is determined by std::isspace on unsigned char values.
requirements: s must reference a valid, mutable std::string.
Whitespace classification depends on the current C locale used by std::isspace.

functions.name: ai_trim_right
functions.description: In-place trim of trailing whitespace characters from a std::string. Whitespace is determined by std::isspace on unsigned char values.
requirements: s must reference a valid, mutable std::string.
Whitespace classification depends on the current C locale used by std::isspace.

functions.name: ai_trim
functions.description: Returns a trimmed copy of the input string: removes leading and trailing whitespace. Note: despite taking a non-const reference, this function does not modify s; it operates on a copy and returns it.
requirements: s must reference a valid std::string.
Whitespace classification depends on the current C locale used by std::isspace via ai_trim_left/right.

functions.name: ai_tolower
functions.description: Lowercases a single ASCII letter. If in is between 'A' and 'Z', adds 0x20; otherwise returns in unchanged.
requirements: intended for ASCII letters only; behavior on non-ASCII or locale-specific characters is a no-op.
char_t must be an integral character type supporting comparison and addition with character literals.

functions.name: ai_toupper
functions.description: Uppercases a single ASCII letter. If in is between 'a' and 'z', subtracts 0x20; otherwise returns in unchanged.
requirements: intended for ASCII letters only; behavior on non-ASCII or locale-specific characters is a no-op.
char_t must be an integral character type supporting comparison and subtraction with character literals.

functions.name: ai_str_toupper
functions.description: Returns an uppercase copy of the input string by applying the ASCII-only ai_toupper(char_t) to each character. No trimming is performed.
requirements: in is not modified; the function returns a new std::string.
Uppercasing is ASCII-only; non-ASCII characters are left unchanged.

functions.name: ai_str_toprintable
functions.description: Replaces all non-printable characters in a string with a specified placeholder (default '?'). Printable test uses isprint on each byte.
requirements: Printable determination is locale-dependent via isprint and operates on unsigned char values cast to int.
in is not modified; the function returns a new std::string.
placeholder is used verbatim to replace non-printable bytes.

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::SGSpatialSort
functions.description: Default constructor for a spatial sorter specialized for smoothing-group-aware vertex queries. Use this to create an empty sorter, then add vertices and prepare it before performing searches.
requirements: After constructing, add all desired vertices via Add() and then call Prepare() before calling FindPositions().
Object must remain alive for the duration of any calls that operate on it (non-static member functions).

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::SGSpatialSort
functions.description: Constructs a spatial sorter initialized with a collection of vertex positions. Intended for smoothing-group-aware proximity queries used by importers such as 3DS/ASE/LWO. The constructor only takes positions; smoothing groups can be associated later via Add() if needed, then the sorter should be prepared for queries.
requirements: Input vector may be empty or contain any number of positions; each element is interpreted as a vertex position.
If you need smoothing-group-aware results, ensure appropriate smoothing group information is added using Add() for the relevant indices before querying.
Call Prepare() after construction (and after any additional Add() calls) before using FindPositions().

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::Add
functions.signature: void Assimp::SGSpatialSort::Add(const Assimp::aiVector3D& vPosition, unsigned int index, unsigned int smoothingGroup);
functions.description: Adds a single vertex record to the spatial sorter with its position, a caller-defined vertex index, and an associated smoothing group. Use this to incrementally build the data set prior to preparing and searching.
requirements: index is an application-provided vertex index that will be returned from queries; it should uniquely identify the vertex within the caller’s context.
smoothingGroup is a group identifier; when used as a bitmask (the default query mode), different bits represent membership in multiple groups.
May be called multiple times before Prepare(); if called after a previous Prepare(), you must call Prepare() again before the next FindPositions() to maintain correct ordering.
vPosition must be a valid 3D position; no specific range restrictions are stated.

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::Prepare
functions.description: Prepares (sorts/indexes) the internal data to enable efficient proximity searches. This step should be performed after all vertices have been added and before any calls to FindPositions().
requirements: Call after all intended Add() operations and before the first FindPositions() call.
If additional vertices are added via Add() after Prepare(), call Prepare() again before performing further queries.
Runs in O(log n) as documented; no parameters or return values.

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::FindPositions
functions.signature: void Assimp::SGSpatialSort::FindPositions(const Assimp::aiVector3D& pPosition, uint32_t pSG, float pRadius, std::vector<unsigned int>& poResults, bool exactMatch = false) const;
functions.description: Searches for vertex indices whose positions lie within pRadius of pPosition and whose smoothing group(s) are compatible with pSG. Results are written to poResults, which is cleared by the call. If exactMatch is false (default), pSG is treated as a bitmask and any overlapping bit with a vertex’s smoothing groups qualifies it; if true, pSG is treated as a single integral group and only exact equality qualifies.
requirements: Prepare() must have been called after the last Add() and before this function to ensure correct/efficient searching.
pRadius represents the maximal distance; it should be non-negative.
poResults will be emptied/cleared by the call; caller must allow the container to be modified and overwritten.
When exactMatch is true, pSG should represent a single group value (not a bitmask).
Function is const and does not modify the sorter’s configuration other than writing to poResults.

functions.name: Assimp::SGSpatialSort::~SGSpatialSort
functions.description: Destructor for SGSpatialSort. Releases resources owned by the object. Defaulted implementation; no special cleanup required beyond standard member destruction.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
No exceptions or errors are reported; default destructor semantics.

functions.name: SetGenericProperty
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline bool SetGenericProperty(std::map<unsigned int, T> &list, const char *szName, const T &value);
functions.description: Sets or updates a named property in a hash-indexed map. The name is hashed via SuperFastHash and used as the key; if the key does not exist the pair is inserted and false is returned, otherwise the existing value is replaced and true is returned. Typical usage: maintain a property bag keyed by string names without storing the strings. Note: names are compared by hash, so distinct names with identical hashes will collide and share the same entry.
requirements: szName must be a valid, null-terminated C string (ai_assert enforces non-null).
list must be a valid, initialized std::map instance; caller must ensure exclusive access (no concurrent mutations) during the call.
value must be a valid instance of T copy-assignable into the map.
Property identity is determined solely by SuperFastHash(szName); any hash collisions will cause entries to overwrite each other.

functions.name: GetGenericProperty
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline const T &GetGenericProperty(const std::map<unsigned int, T> &list, const char *szName, const T &errorReturn);
functions.description: Retrieves a named property from a hash-indexed map. The name is hashed via SuperFastHash and used as the lookup key. If the key exists, returns a const reference to the stored value; otherwise returns errorReturn by reference. Intended for read-only access with a caller-specified fallback.
requirements: szName must be a valid, null-terminated C string (ai_assert enforces non-null).
list must be a valid, initialized std::map; caller must ensure no concurrent modification while accessing.
errorReturn must refer to a valid T object for at least as long as the returned reference is used (the function returns a reference to it on miss).
The returned reference may alias either a value inside list or errorReturn; callers must not store the reference beyond the lifetime of the aliased object.
Lookup identity is determined by SuperFastHash(szName); hash collisions may return/override an unintended entry.

functions.name: SetGenericPropertyPtr
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline void SetGenericPropertyPtr(std::map<unsigned int, T *> &list, const char *szName, T *value, bool *bWasExisting = nullptr);
functions.description: Sets, replaces, or removes a pointer-valued named property in a hash-indexed map with ownership management. If the entry exists and the stored pointer differs from value, the old pointer is deleted and replaced. Passing nullptr removes the property. If bWasExisting is non-null, it is set to true if the property existed prior to the call, false otherwise. Use when the map owns the stored pointers.
requirements: szName must be a valid, null-terminated C string (ai_assert enforces non-null).
list must be a valid, initialized std::map; caller must ensure exclusive access (no concurrent mutations) during the call.
The map takes ownership of stored pointers; any pointer previously stored may be deleted during replacement. Pointers must be allocated with operator new compatible with delete for type T.
Passing value == nullptr will erase the property (no pointer stored afterwards).
If bWasExisting is non-null, the function will write to it (true if replaced/erased an existing entry, false if inserted new).
If value equals the currently stored pointer, it is not deleted/replaced; otherwise the old pointer is deleted before storing the new one.
Key identity is determined by SuperFastHash(szName); hash collisions cause entries to share/override the same slot.

functions.name: HasGenericProperty
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline bool HasGenericProperty(const std::map<unsigned int, T> &list, const char *szName);
functions.description: Checks whether a named property exists in a hash-indexed map. The name is hashed via SuperFastHash and used to test for presence. Returns true if an entry with that hash key is present, false otherwise.
requirements: szName must be a valid, null-terminated C string (ai_assert enforces non-null).
list must be a valid, initialized std::map; caller must ensure no concurrent modification while accessing.
Presence is determined solely by SuperFastHash(szName); distinct names with identical hashes are indistinguishable.

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::SpatialSort
functions.description: Default constructor for a SpatialSort instance with no input data. Use Fill() and/or Append() to provide positions, then Finalize() (or pass pFinalize=true to Fill/Append) before calling any query methods.
requirements: Object is empty and not finalized after construction; call Finalize() after adding data, or use Fill/Append with pFinalize=true before calling query methods like FindPositions() or GenerateMappingTable().

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::SpatialSort
functions.signature: Assimp::SpatialSort::SpatialSort(const aiVector3D* pPositions, unsigned int pNumPositions, unsigned int pElementOffset)
functions.description: Constructs a SpatialSort over an array of 3D positions supplied as a strided memory block. Positions are referenced by index and internally prepared for spatial queries against a plane-based ordering. Intended for quick proximity searches in mesh vertex data.
requirements: pPositions must point to a readable block containing at least pNumPositions elements laid out with stride pElementOffset bytes between consecutive vectors.
pNumPositions may be 0; if >0, pPositions must be non-null and valid for the specified range.
pElementOffset must correctly describe the actual stride of the input array; mismatch leads to undefined behavior.

Whether the instance is immediately queryable (finalized) after construction is not explicitly stated; if queries fail or are unavailable, call Finalize() before FindPositions()/GenerateMappingTable().

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::Fill
functions.signature: void Assimp::SpatialSort::Fill(const aiVector3D* pPositions, unsigned int pNumPositions, unsigned int pElementOffset, bool pFinalize /* = true */)
functions.description: Replaces any existing data with a new set of positions from a strided array. Indices are reassigned in ascending order. Optionally finalizes the internal representation so queries can be performed immediately.
requirements: Replaces existing data; any previous contents are discarded.
pPositions must be readable for at least pNumPositions elements using stride pElementOffset; if pNumPositions > 0, pPositions must be non-null.
pElementOffset must match the actual memory layout (stride) of the supplied array.
If pFinalize is false, you must call Finalize() before calling FindPositions() or GenerateMappingTable().
poResults-like containers mentioned in other APIs are not used here; there is no return value and no error reporting.

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::Append
functions.signature: void Assimp::SpatialSort::Append(const aiVector3D* pPositions, unsigned int pNumPositions, unsigned int pElementOffset, bool pFinalize /* = true */)
functions.description: Appends additional positions from a strided array to the existing data set. Optionally finalizes the internal representation after appending.
requirements: Appends to existing data; previously stored entries remain.
pPositions must be readable for at least pNumPositions elements using stride pElementOffset; if pNumPositions > 0, pPositions must be non-null.
pElementOffset must match the actual memory layout (stride) of the supplied array.
If pFinalize is false across one or more calls to Append(), you must call Finalize() once after all appends and before calling FindPositions() or GenerateMappingTable().

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::Finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the internal spatial data (e.g., computes distances to the sorting plane, centroid, and sorts entries). Required before performing queries if prior Fill/Append calls were made with pFinalize=false.
requirements: Call after the last Fill()/Append() when pFinalize was set to false.
Must be called before FindPositions() or GenerateMappingTable() if the data was not finalized earlier.
No parameters; not thread-safe with concurrent mutation of the same SpatialSort instance (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::FindPositions
functions.signature: void Assimp::SpatialSort::FindPositions(const aiVector3D& pPosition, ai_real pRadius, std::vector<unsigned int>& poResults) const
functions.description: Finds all vertex indices whose positions lie within pRadius of pPosition, using the precomputed plane-based ordering for efficient range search. The output container is cleared and filled with matching indices.
requirements: The SpatialSort must be finalized (either via Fill/Append with pFinalize=true or by calling Finalize()).
pRadius should be non-negative; negative radii yield no meaningful results.
poResults will be emptied by the call; caller must allow it to be modified.
Input position pPosition may be any finite 3D point; NaN/Inf handling is unspecified.

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::FindIdenticalPositions
functions.signature: void Assimp::SpatialSort::FindIdenticalPositions(const aiVector3D& pPosition, std::vector<unsigned int>& poResults) const
functions.description: Finds all vertex indices whose positions are identical to pPosition within a very small tolerance (four floating-point units), as opposed to an epsilon radius. The output container is cleared and filled with matching indices.
requirements: Recommended to use on a finalized SpatialSort (constructed with finalization or after calling Finalize()); behavior without finalization is unspecified.
poResults will be emptied by the call; caller must allow it to be modified.
Exact tolerance is internal; caller should not assume a configurable epsilon here.

functions.name: Assimp::SpatialSort::GenerateMappingTable
functions.signature: unsigned int Assimp::SpatialSort::GenerateMappingTable(std::vector<unsigned int>& fill, ai_real pRadius) const
functions.description: Generates a mapping from each vertex index to a representative index such that vertices within pRadius of each other map to the same output ID. Output IDs are assigned densely from 0..n-1. The provided vector is resized/filled with one entry per input vertex; the return value is the number of unique vertices (n).
requirements: The SpatialSort must be finalized (either via Fill/Append with pFinalize=true or by calling Finalize()).
pRadius should be non-negative; negative values are not meaningful.
The vector 'fill' will be cleared/resized and populated with as many entries as there are positions managed by this SpatialSort; caller must allow mutation of this container.

functions.name: Assimp::SkeletonMeshBuilder::SkeletonMeshBuilder
functions.signature: Assimp::SkeletonMeshBuilder::SkeletonMeshBuilder(aiScene* pScene, aiNode* root = nullptr, bool bKnobsOnly = false)
functions.description: Constructs a SkeletonMeshBuilder that processes the given aiScene and inserts a dummy mesh reflecting the node hierarchy (skeleton). If the scene already contains mesh data, the constructor performs no action. Use this to create a visual/skin mesh for file formats that only provide motion/animation data. Pass root to start from a specific node (nullptr means the scene root). Set bKnobsOnly to true to generate only node “knobs” (no connecting geometry). Implementation details such as whether materials/bones are added and how errors are reported are not documented here; behavior is inferred from the header comments.
requirements: pScene must point to a valid, initialized aiScene object (inferred from the need to read/modify the scene).
If you want a dummy mesh to be generated, ensure the scene currently has no mesh data; otherwise the constructor does nothing (explicitly stated).
root may be nullptr to indicate the scene root (explicitly stated). If non-null, it should be a node that is part of the scene’s hierarchy (inferred).
bKnobsOnly controls whether connectors between node knobs are created: true = knobs only; false = knobs plus connectors (explicitly stated).
Thread-safety is unspecified; do not concurrently modify the scene while constructing (inferred/unspecified).
Error handling and exceptions are unspecified in this header; callers should not rely on specific exception behavior (unknown).

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::SmallVector
functions.description: Default constructor for a small-vector with inline storage of Capacity elements. Initializes the container to size 0, pointing storage at the inline buffer.
requirements: Template parameters: T is the element type; Capacity is the inline storage capacity (unsigned int).
T must be default-constructible because dynamic growth allocates `new T[n]` and the inline buffer is default-initialized as a member array.
T should be trivially copyable/memcpy-safe; internal growth moves existing elements using std::memcpy without invoking copy/move constructors.
Constructed vector is empty (size()==0).
No exceptions or errors are reported by the constructor; allocation for inline storage is static and immediate.

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::~SmallVector
functions.description: Destructor releases dynamically allocated storage if the vector has grown beyond the inline buffer. It does not explicitly destroy contained elements.
requirements: T should be trivially destructible; elements are not individually destroyed (no destructors are called).
Safe to destroy at any time; if dynamic storage was used it is freed with delete[].
Do not use pointers/iterators obtained from this vector after destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::push_back
functions.description: Appends an element to the end of the vector, growing capacity if needed. Growth reallocates to a larger buffer and memcpy-copies existing elements.
requirements: item must be a valid reference to T; T must be assignable from const T& (used to place the new element).
If growth is needed, T must be default-constructible (`new T[newCapacity]`) and trivially copyable/memcpy-safe (existing elements are moved with std::memcpy).
All iterators and pointers to elements may be invalidated when capacity grows.
Amortized constant time per push for many workloads; exact complexity depends on growth pattern (grows by +Capacity).

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::resize
functions.description: Changes the logical size of the vector to newSize, growing capacity if newSize exceeds current capacity. Does not initialize or destroy elements when resizing.
requirements: If newSize > current capacity, triggers allocation `new T[newSize]`: T must be default-constructible and trivially copyable/memcpy-safe for moving existing elements.
If increasing size without growth, the newly exposed elements are left as-is (may be uninitialized/indeterminate); caller must assign/initialize them before reading.
If decreasing size, elements beyond newSize are not destroyed; if T has non-trivial destructors this is unsafe.
Pointers/iterators may be invalidated when growth occurs.

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::size
functions.description: Returns the current number of elements considered part of the vector.
requirements: May be called on const and non-const instances.
Returned count may include elements that are not value-initialized if resize() was used to increase size without initializing new elements; callers must ensure they only read initialized elements.

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::begin
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first element (or end() if empty).
requirements: Pointer remains valid until the vector grows (capacity change) or the vector is destroyed.
Do not dereference if size()==0.
Not thread-safe; concurrent mutation invalidates the pointer.

functions.name: Assimp::SmallVector::end
functions.description: Returns a pointer one past the last element.
requirements: Pointer remains valid until the vector grows (capacity change) or the vector is destroyed.
Safe to use for iteration with begin(); do not dereference end().
Not thread-safe; concurrent mutation invalidates the pointer.

functions.name: ComputeNormalsWithSmoothingsGroups
functions.description: Computes normal vectors for a mesh whose faces carry smoothing-group information. Given a MeshWithSmoothingGroups<T> (positions, faces, normals), this routine calculates normals (typically per-vertex, influenced by face smoothing groups) and writes them into sMesh.mNormals. Intended for loaders like 3DS/ASE where faces (type T) are or behave like FaceWithSmoothingGroup. Implementation is provided in SmoothingGroups.inl; detailed behavior (e.g., hard/soft edge handling and normal weighting) follows Assimp’s smoothing-group logic. Specific weighting or normalization details are not documented here and remain unknown.
requirements: Template parameter T must be compatible with FaceWithSmoothingGroup (i.e., provide a 3-index array member named mIndices[3] and a 32-bit smoothing group member named iSmoothGroup), or inherit from it.
sMesh.mPositions must be initialized and contain the vertex positions used by the mesh.
sMesh.mFaces must be initialized; each face must reference exactly three indices (triangles).
All indices in each face’s mIndices[] must be valid: 0 <= index < sMesh.mPositions.size().
sMesh.mNormals will be produced/overwritten by this function; callers should not rely on pre-existing contents.
The function expects a consistent mesh: faces must reference the intended vertex set; undefined behavior may occur if the mesh is malformed.

functions.name: ComputeNormalsWithSmoothingsGroups
functions.description: Computes per-vertex normals for a mesh using smoothing-group-aware averaging. For each triangle face, a face normal is computed and then averaged among all vertices that share the same position (within a small epsilon) and belong to the same smoothing group. The result overwrites sMesh.mNormals. Typical usage: call after loading/building a MeshWithSmoothingGroups with valid positions, triangle faces, and smoothing-group IDs; the function will fill/replace the vertex normals accordingly. Notes: only triangle faces are supported (the implementation assumes 3 indices per face). The spatial merge tolerance is derived from the mesh’s bounding box (1e-5 of the diagonal).
requirements: sMesh must be a MeshWithSmoothingGroups<T> providing at least the members: mPositions (std::vector<aiVector3D>), mFaces (std::vector<T>), and mNormals (std::vector<aiVector3D>).
Type T (face type) must provide: mIndices[3] (triangle vertex indices) and iSmoothGroup (smoothing group identifier).
All face indices in mFaces must be valid indices into sMesh.mPositions (0 <= index < mPositions.size()).
Faces must be triangles; exactly three indices are accessed for every face (mIndices[0..2]).
sMesh.mPositions must be initialized with the mesh’s vertex positions before calling; their values determine the epsilon used to find coincident vertices.
Smoothing group identifiers (iSmoothGroup) must be set consistently on faces; vertices are averaged only within the same smoothing group.
The function overwrites sMesh.mNormals; any prior contents will be discarded.
Header dependency: requires SGSpatialSort (assimp/SGSpatialSort.h) to be available at compile time.

functions.name: Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeMesh
functions.signature: static aiMesh* Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeMesh(const std::vector<aiVector3D>& positions, unsigned int numIndices);

functions.name: Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeMesh
functions.description: Constructs an aiMesh by invoking a generator callback that fills a positions vector and returns the number of vertices per face. functions.signature: static aiMesh* Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeMesh(unsigned int (*GenerateFunc)(std::vector<aiVector3D>& positions, bool polygons));

functions.signature: static aiMesh* Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeMesh(unsigned int n, void (*GenerateFunc)(unsigned int n, std::vector<aiVector3D>& positions));

functions.signature: static unsigned int Assimp::StandardShapes::MakeHexahedron(std::vector<aiVector3D>& positions, bool polygons = false);

functions.name: Assimp::CommentRemover::RemoveLineComments

functions.description: Removes single-line comments from a text buffer in-place by replacing comment text with a replacement character. functions.name: Assimp::Subdivider::Create
functions.description: Factory method that creates a concrete subdivider implementing the requested subdivision algorithm (e.g., Catmull–Clark). Intended for clients to obtain a ready-to-use subdivider instance for mesh subdivision.
requirements: algo must be a valid value of Assimp::Subdivider::Algorithm (e.g., Assimp::Subdivider::CATMULL_CLARKE).
The returned pointer, if non-null, is heap-allocated; the caller is responsible for deleting it (delete) to invoke the virtual destructor.
Behavior for unsupported/unknown algorithms is not documented; callers should check for a null return or be prepared for library-defined behavior (unknown).

functions.name: Assimp::Subdivider::Subdivide
functions.signature: virtual void Assimp::Subdivider::Subdivide(aiMesh* mesh, aiMesh*& out, unsigned int num, bool discard_input = false) = 0
functions.description: Subdivides a single mesh using the selected algorithm and produces a new mesh. Optionally deletes the input mesh to improve performance by reusing memory during intermediate steps.
requirements: mesh must be in verbose format (as required by the algorithm).
out must be a reference to an aiMesh* that will receive the allocated output mesh; out must not alias mesh (precondition: out != mesh).
num specifies the number of subdivision iterations; must be a non-negative count representable by unsigned int (inferred from type).
If discard_input is true, the input mesh is deleted after subdivision; the caller must not access mesh after the call in this case.
Caller must ensure mesh is a valid, initialized aiMesh pointer.
The function allocates the output mesh and assigns it to out (ownership/cleanup policy not documented; unknown).

functions.name: Assimp::Subdivider::Subdivide
functions.signature: virtual void Assimp::Subdivider::Subdivide(aiMesh** smesh, size_t nmesh, aiMesh** out, unsigned int num, bool discard_input = false) = 0
functions.description: Subdivides multiple meshes using the selected algorithm, preserving object-level smoothing across per-material mesh splits. Produces a one-to-one set of output meshes, optionally deleting inputs to improve performance.
requirements: smesh must point to an array of aiMesh* in verbose format with at least nmesh elements.
nmesh must not be zero (precondition: nmesh != 0).
out must point to an array with capacity for at least nmesh elements and must not overlap smesh (precondition: smesh and out may not overlap).
Each output mesh is allocated by the function and maps one-to-one to the corresponding input mesh (ownership/cleanup policy not documented; unknown).
num specifies the number of subdivision iterations; must be a non-negative count representable by unsigned int (inferred from type).
If discard_input is true, the input meshes are deleted after subdivision; the caller must not access any smesh[i] after the call in this case.
Caller must ensure all smesh[i] pointers for i in [0, nmesh) are valid, initialized aiMesh pointers.

functions.name: Assimp::operator+
functions.signature: Assimp::Vertex operator+(const Assimp::Vertex& v0, const Assimp::Vertex& v1)
functions.description: Element-wise addition of two interleaved vertices. Each component (position, normal, tangent, bitangent, all texcoords, and all colors) of v0 and v1 is added and returned as a new Vertex. Useful for interpolation, subdivision, or blending operations where uniform treatment of all components is desired.
requirements: v0 and v1 must be valid, initialized Vertex instances.

All operations are applied uniformly to every component; caller must ensure this semantics is appropriate for their use case (e.g., adding normals/colors may not be physically correct in all contexts).

functions.name: Assimp::operator-
functions.signature: Assimp::Vertex operator-(const Assimp::Vertex& v0, const Assimp::Vertex& v1)
functions.description: Element-wise subtraction of two interleaved vertices. Each component (position, normal, tangent, bitangent, all texcoords, and all colors) of v1 is subtracted from the corresponding component of v0 and returned as a new Vertex.
requirements: v0 and v1 must be valid, initialized Vertex instances.
All operations are applied uniformly to every component; caller must ensure this semantics is appropriate (e.g., subtracting normals/colors may not be meaningful in all contexts).

functions.name: Assimp::operator*
functions.signature: Assimp::Vertex operator*(const Assimp::Vertex& v0, ai_real f)
functions.description: Element-wise scalar multiplication of a Vertex by f. Scales position, normal, tangent, bitangent, each texcoord set, and each color by f, returning a new Vertex.
requirements: v0 must be a valid, initialized Vertex.
f should be a finite scalar of type ai_real (typically float).
Uniform scaling of normals/colors may not be appropriate for all uses; caller is responsible for choosing correct usage.

functions.name: Assimp::operator/
functions.signature: Assimp::Vertex operator/(const Assimp::Vertex& v0, ai_real f)
functions.description: Element-wise division of a Vertex by scalar f. Implemented as multiplication by (1.f / f). Scales position, normal, tangent, bitangent, each texcoord set, and each color by 1/f, returning a new Vertex.
requirements: v0 must be a valid, initialized Vertex.
f must be non-zero to avoid division by zero (the implementation computes 1.f/f).
f should be finite and not denormal to avoid undefined or non-finite results.
Uniform scaling of normals/colors may not be appropriate for all uses; caller is responsible for choosing correct usage.

functions.name: Assimp::Vertex::SortBack
functions.signature: void Assimp::Vertex::SortBack(aiMesh* out, unsigned int idx) const
functions.description: Writes this interleaved Vertex back into a mesh at vertex index idx, de-interleaving into the mesh’s separate arrays. Position is always written; normals, tangents/bitangents, each texture coordinate set, and each color set are written only if the destination mesh reports those channels as present.
requirements: out must be non-null.
idx must be less than out->mNumVertices.

The destination mesh must have its per-vertex buffers allocated and flagged as present (out->HasNormals(), out->HasTangentsAndBitangents(), out->HasTextureCoords(i), out->HasVertexColors(i)) for any channels you expect to be written; each such buffer must contain at least idx+1 elements.
Only channels reported present by the destination mesh are written; absent channels are ignored.
No bounds or presence checks beyond the Has* queries are performed; caller must ensure mesh buffers are correctly allocated prior to calling.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::LineSplitter
functions.signature: Assimp::LineSplitter::LineSplitter(Assimp::StreamReaderLE& stream, bool skip_empty_lines = true, bool trim = true)
functions.description: Constructs a LineSplitter over an existing StreamReaderLE, preparing to iterate line-by-line over the stream. If skip_empty_lines is true, empty lines are skipped; when skipping empty lines, trimming is effectively applied as well (leading spaces after line breaks are skipped). Intended usage: create a LineSplitter and iterate with for(LineSplitter s(stream); s; ++s) to process each line.
requirements: stream must refer to a valid Assimp::StreamReaderLE that remains alive for the entire lifetime of the LineSplitter (the splitter stores a reference).
The underlying stream should contain text data separated by '\n' and/or '\r'.
If skip_empty_lines is true, leading spaces after line breaks are skipped; when false and trim is true, leading spaces and tabs are trimmed at the start of lines.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::~LineSplitter
functions.description: Default destructor. Releases LineSplitter resources; does not own or close the underlying StreamReaderLE.
requirements: The referenced StreamReaderLE is not destroyed before the LineSplitter is destroyed.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator++
functions.description: Advances to the next line (pre-increment). Populates the current line buffer and increments the internal line index. If swallow_next_increment() was called, this call is swallowed and does not advance.
requirements: Must not be called when the splitter is at end-of-file unless the caller is prepared to handle std::logic_error.
On success, the current line string and token pointers (from previous calls) become invalidated and must not be reused.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a pointer into the current line string at the start of the idx-th whitespace-separated token (0-based). Whitespace is determined by Assimp::ParsingUtils (spaces and tabs); line end terminates token scanning.
requirements: There must be at least idx+1 tokens on the current line; otherwise a std::range_error is thrown.
The returned pointer is valid only until the current line buffer changes (e.g., the next call to operator++ or any operation that modifies the current line).
The LineSplitter must currently reference a valid line (i.e., constructed successfully and not past EOF).

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::get_tokens
functions.signature: template <size_t N> void Assimp::LineSplitter::get_tokens(const char* (&tokens)[N]) const
functions.description: Extracts pointers to the starts of the first N whitespace-separated tokens from the current line and stores them in the provided array. Tokenization uses Assimp::ParsingUtils rules.
requirements: The current line must contain at least N tokens; otherwise a std::range_error is thrown.
The output token pointers remain valid only until the current line buffer changes (e.g., after operator++).
tokens must be an array of size N of const char* references as per the function signature.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the current line string (read-only). Useful for calling std::string member functions directly.
requirements: The LineSplitter must not be past EOF when used; otherwise the contents may be empty depending on state, and subsequent ++ may throw.
Do not retain the returned pointer beyond the lifetime of the LineSplitter.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator*
functions.description: Returns a copy of the current line string. Useful when a value copy is desired that remains valid after advancing.
requirements: None beyond having a valid current line; returns an empty string if current buffer is empty.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::getEnd
functions.description: Returns the end-marker pointer used during tokenization (one past an internal buffer boundary). Intended for use with Assimp::ParsingUtils functions that require an end pointer.
requirements: The returned pointer is an internal marker; it should not be dereferenced or assumed to point into externally managed memory.
Only meaningful together with pointers into the current line returned by operator[]/get_tokens.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator bool
functions.description: Conversion to bool indicating whether more data remains in the underlying stream (i.e., iteration can continue). Enables idiomatic for/while loops.
requirements: Use to guard calls to operator++ to avoid std::logic_error at EOF.
Semantics reflect StreamReaderLE::GetRemainingSize() > 0.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::operator Assimp::LineSplitter::line_idx
functions.description: Conversion to the current zero-based line index. Empty lines are included in the count even if skipped from delivery, per class comment.
requirements: Interpretation of the index is zero-based.
Do not assume any particular starting value beyond what the implementation provides; use get_index() for clarity.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::get_index
functions.description: Returns the current zero-based line index maintained by the splitter. Empty lines are included in the index accounting.
requirements: Interpretation of the index is zero-based.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::get_stream
functions.description: Provides non-const access to the underlying StreamReaderLE used by the splitter.
requirements: The returned StreamReaderLE reference must remain valid; callers must avoid mutating the stream in ways that break LineSplitter's assumptions (e.g., external pointer movement) unless they fully control subsequent usage.
The StreamReaderLE object must outlive the LineSplitter.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::match_start
functions.description: Returns true if the current line begins with the given C-string prefix check. Comparison is case-sensitive and uses the length of check.
requirements: check must be a valid, null-terminated C-string pointer (non-null).
Only matches the exact prefix; no trimming is applied beyond what the splitter already configured for lines.

functions.name: Assimp::LineSplitter::swallow_next_increment
functions.description: Swallows the next call to operator++ so that it becomes a no-op and does not advance or throw. Useful when the current line should be reprocessed on the next iteration.
requirements: Only the next increment is swallowed; subsequent increments behave normally.
Does not affect boolean state or line content until a real increment occurs.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::basic_formatter
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::basic_formatter()
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an empty formatter that accumulates text into an internal std::basic_ostringstream. Use with operator<< or operator, to append content, then implicitly convert to std::basic_string to retrieve the result.
requirements: No special preconditions. Formatter starts empty.
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; the same instance should not be used concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::basic_formatter
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TT> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::basic_formatter(const TT& sin)
functions.description: Templated converting constructor. Initializes the formatter by streaming the provided value sin into the internal stream. Useful for one-shot initialization from any streamable type.
requirements: TT must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits> (i.e., the expression 'underlying << sin' must be well-formed).
Construction may allocate memory due to underlying stream buffer growth.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::basic_formatter
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::basic_formatter(Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>&& other)
functions.description: Move constructor. Moves (or, on some older GCC toolchains, copies by string) the internal stream contents from another formatter into this one.
requirements: The source object 'other' may be in a valid but unspecified state after the move.
On older GCC (<=4.9), this constructor effectively copies the other’s string content rather than moving; no caller-visible requirement change.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator std::basic_string
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator std::basic_string<T, CharTraits, Allocator>() const
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to std::basic_string. Returns the accumulated text from the internal stream as a std::basic_string of the formatter’s character type.
requirements: May allocate memory to construct the returned string.
Safe to call on const and temporary formatter instances.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_base_of<std::exception, TToken>::value>::type* = nullptr> const Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator<<(const TToken& s) const
functions.description: Const insertion operator for non-exception types. Streams s into the internal stream and returns a const reference to this formatter, enabling chaining on temporaries.
requirements: TToken must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits>.
Modifies internal state despite being const (the internal stream is mutable). Not thread-safe for shared instances.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken, typename std::enable_if<std::is_base_of<std::exception, TToken>::value>::type* = nullptr> const Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator<<(const TToken& s) const
functions.description: Const insertion operator specialization for exception types. Appends s.what() to the internal stream and returns a const reference for chaining.
requirements: TToken must derive from std::exception and provide what().
The returned c-string from what() must be valid for the duration of the call (standard guarantees this).

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_base_of<std::exception, TToken>::value>::type* = nullptr> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator<<(const TToken& s)
functions.description: Non-const insertion operator for non-exception types. Streams s into the internal stream and returns a non-const reference to enable further modifications.
requirements: TToken must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits>.
Not thread-safe for shared instances.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken, typename std::enable_if<std::is_base_of<std::exception, TToken>::value>::type* = nullptr> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator<<(const TToken& s)
functions.description: Non-const insertion operator specialization for exception types. Appends s.what() to the internal stream and returns a non-const reference.
requirements: TToken must derive from std::exception and provide what().

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator,
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken> const Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator,(const TToken& s) const
functions.description: Const comma operator overload. Streams s into the internal stream and returns a const reference. Provides an alternative chaining syntax to operator<< for temporaries.
requirements: TToken must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits>.
Modifies internal state despite being const (internal stream is mutable).

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator,
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator,(const TToken& s)
functions.description: Non-const comma operator overload taking const reference. Streams s and returns a non-const reference to this formatter.
requirements: TToken must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits>.

functions.name: Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter::operator,
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename CharTraits = std::char_traits<T>, typename Allocator = std::allocator<T>> template <typename TToken> Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>& Assimp::Formatter::basic_formatter<T, CharTraits, Allocator>::operator,(TToken& s)
functions.description: Non-const comma operator overload taking non-const reference (MSVC8 compatibility). Streams s and returns a non-const reference to this formatter.
requirements: TToken must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<T, CharTraits>.

functions.name: Assimp::Profiling::Profiler::Profiler
functions.description: Default constructor for the lightweight profiling utility. Initializes an empty region map for timing. Typical usage: instantiate a Profiler, then call BeginRegion/EndRegion to log timings.
requirements: Must be called to create a valid Profiler object before invoking member functions.
Thread-safety is not provided; if the Profiler instance is accessed from multiple threads, external synchronization is required.

functions.name: Assimp::Profiling::Profiler::~Profiler
functions.description: Default destructor. Performs no special cleanup beyond normal object destruction; does not automatically end or report active regions.
requirements: Do not use the Profiler instance after destruction.
If there are active regions at destruction time, they are not automatically ended or reported beyond what has already been logged.

functions.name: Assimp::Profiling::Profiler::BeginRegion
functions.description: Starts timing for a named profiling region and logs a debug message indicating the start. Stores the current system_clock timestamp for the provided region key. Calling BeginRegion again with the same region overwrites the previous start time. Use together with EndRegion to log elapsed time.
requirements: The Profiler instance must be valid when called.
The region identifier may be any string; if the same key is reused, the prior start time is replaced (no nesting support per key).
This function is not thread-safe; coordinate access externally if used concurrently across threads.

functions.name: Assimp::Profiling::Profiler::EndRegion
functions.description: Stops timing for a named profiling region previously started with BeginRegion and logs a debug message with the elapsed duration. If the region was never started (not found in the map), the function returns without logging a duration. Does not remove the region entry from the map.
requirements: The Profiler instance must be valid when called.
Calling EndRegion without a prior matching BeginRegion is a no-op.
If BeginRegion was called multiple times for the same region, the elapsed time is measured from the most recent call.
This function is not thread-safe; coordinate access externally if used concurrently across threads.

functions.name: Assimp::LogFunctions::ThrowException
functions.signature:
template<class TDeriving, typename... T>
static void Assimp::LogFunctions<TDeriving>::ThrowException(T&&... args)
functions.description: Constructs and throws a DeadlyImportError that is prefixed with the class-specific prefix returned by Prefix(). Intended for importer implementations to abort processing with a detailed error message. Usage: call as LogFunctions<YourImporter>::ThrowException("message", ...); this function always throws and does not return.
requirements: This is a static function; no instance is required.
Callers must be prepared to handle (or allow to propagate) a DeadlyImportError exception; the function never returns.
The variadic arguments must be valid for constructing a DeadlyImportError message along with the prefix (types must be compatible with Assimp’s formatting/logging utilities).

functions.name: Assimp::LogFunctions::LogWarn
functions.signature:
template<class TDeriving, typename... T>
static void Assimp::LogFunctions<TDeriving>::LogWarn(T&&... args)
functions.description: Logs a warning message via Assimp’s DefaultLogger with a class-specific prefix. No-op if the null logger is active. Usage: LogFunctions<YourImporter>::LogWarn("message", ...);
requirements: This is a static function; no instance is required.
If DefaultLogger::isNullLogger() returns true, the call has no effect.
Variadic arguments must be compatible with the ASSIMP_LOG_WARN macro’s formatting (i.e., form a valid log message when combined with the prefix).

template<class TDeriving>
static const char* Assimp::LogFunctions<TDeriving>::Prefix()
