requirements: This is a static function; no instance is required.
Return value semantics beyond type are not documented in this header; callers should not rely on a specific format or lifetime beyond it being a const char* provided by the library.

functions.name: Assimp::Bitmap::Save
functions.signature: static bool Assimp::Bitmap::Save(aiTexture* texture, Assimp::IOStream* file);
functions.description: Saves the given aiTexture as a bitmap (BMP) image and writes it to the provided IOStream. Returns true on success, false on failure. Intended for formats that embed textures and need export to a standard bitmap stream. Notes: Implementation details are not shown here; based on the class internals (Header/DIB structures and mBytesPerPixel=4), the output is a BMP stream using a DIB header. Exact pixel format details beyond 4 bytes per pixel are not specified in this header.
requirements: texture must be a valid, non-null pointer to an aiTexture instance containing image data.
file must be a valid, non-null pointer to an Assimp::IOStream opened for writing (binary-safe).
Caller should interpret the return value: true indicates the bitmap was written successfully; false indicates failure.
The function writes a BMP-formatted stream; callers should provide a writable stream destination and handle positioning/rewind as needed (initial position unspecified).
Any assumptions about supported aiTexture formats, color channels, or compression are unknown from this header and should be verified against the implementation/documentation.

functions.name: Assimp::XMLEscape
functions.description: Escapes the five XML special characters in the input string to their corresponding XML entities: '&' -> "&", '"' -> """, '\'' -> "'", '<' -> "<", '>' -> ">". Use this to make arbitrary text safe for inclusion in XML content or attributes. It does not perform full XML canonicalization, encoding conversion, or escape any other characters; existing entities will be treated as plain text and may become double-escaped if already present.
requirements: Input must be a valid std::string reference; it can contain any characters.
The function allocates memory for the result; callers should be prepared for potential allocation failure exceptions from std::string operations.
Returned string contains only the specified entity substitutions; callers must not assume other XML/HTML escaping or validation.

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::IOStreamBuffer
functions.description: Constructs a cached stream buffer with an internal cache of the requested size (in elements of T). The cache is allocated immediately and initialized. Use open() to attach an Assimp::IOStream before reading. T is expected to be a character-like or byte-like element type used for line/block parsing.
requirements: cache should be > 0; a zero-sized cache would lead to invalid memory access when reading (inferred from use of &m_cache[0])
T must be a trivially copyable, character/byte compatible type where line-end characters ('\r','\n') and a continuation token make sense (e.g., char, unsigned char) (inferred from implementation)
Object is created in a closed state; open() must be called before any read operations

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::open
functions.description: Attaches an IOStream to the buffer and prepares internal state for cached reading. Computes effective cache size and the number of blocks based on the file size. Does not load data yet; the first read happens on demand by readNextBlock() or the higher-level getters.
requirements: Must be called when no stream is currently attached; calling open() while already open returns false
stream must be non-null
Underlying stream must report a FileSize() > 0; otherwise open() fails
On success, cache size may be reduced to min(initial cache, file size) (call cacheSize() after open to get the actual value)
Not thread-safe; do not share a single IOStreamBuffer across threads without external synchronization (general library expectation)

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::close
functions.description: Detaches the currently attached stream and resets internal state counters and positions. Does not free the cache buffer itself.
requirements: A stream must be open; calling close() when no stream is attached returns false
After close(), size(), cacheSize(), and block counters reset to zero-like values; buffer cannot be read until open() is called again

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::size
functions.description: Returns the total size in elements (T-sized units) of the attached stream as captured at open() time.
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful open(); otherwise returns 0

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::cacheSize
functions.description: Returns the current effective cache size (in elements). This may be reduced to the file size at open(), and further reduced to the last short read size after the final block is read.
requirements: Callers relying on the amount of valid data in the last block should re-check cacheSize() after calling readNextBlock() or line/block getters, as it may shrink on the final block (inferred from implementation)
Meaningful only after a successful open(); otherwise returns the constructed cache size (which may be 0 if not opened)

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::readNextBlock
functions.description: Reads the next block of data from the attached stream into the internal cache starting at the current file position. Updates file and cache positions and advances the current block index. Returns false on EOF or read failure.
requirements: A stream must be open (m_stream != nullptr)
Seeks to the current file position from the beginning; underlying IOStream must support Seek/Read semantics compatible with aiOrigin_SET
On short read (final block), the effective cache size is reduced to the number of elements actually read; callers should query cacheSize() after this call if they depend on the valid data length
Returns false if zero elements are read (EOF or error)

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getNumBlocks
functions.description: Returns the total number of blocks the file is divided into based on the effective cache size computed at open().
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful open(); otherwise returns 0

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getCurrentBlockIndex
functions.description: Returns the index (1-based after first read) of the next block to be read, incremented each time a block is successfully read.
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful open(); starts at 0 before the first read

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getFilePos
functions.description: Returns the current absolute file position (in elements) after the last read into the cache. Advances by the effective cache size per block read.
requirements: Meaningful only after a successful open(); initially 0 until the first successful read

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getNextDataLine
functions.signature: template <class T> bool Assimp::IOStreamBuffer<T>::getNextDataLine(std::vector<T>& buffer, T continuationToken)
functions.description: Reads the next logical data line into buffer, handling line continuation when the specified continuationToken is immediately followed by a line end. Skips physical line breaks for continued lines and appends a single '\n' sentinel at the end of the returned data. Grows the buffer as needed.
requirements: A stream must be open; function will trigger reading the first/next block on demand
buffer is resized internally; caller should not rely on its initial content or capacity
T must support comparison with continuationToken and line-end checks ('\r'/'\n'); IsLineEnd from ParsingUtils is used (inferred)
Returns false if no more data can be read (EOF) or a block cannot be fetched
The returned buffer data is terminated with a '\n' element; content length is the number of elements up to (but not including) that terminator (inferred)

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getNextLine
functions.description: Reads the next line (handling both ASCII and binary line end conventions). Skips any initial line-end characters, then collects characters until a line end, appending a single '\n' sentinel to buffer. Grows the buffer as needed and reads additional blocks transparently.
requirements: A stream must be open; function will read blocks as needed
buffer is resized internally; caller should not rely on its initial content or capacity
T must be compatible with line-end checks for '\r' and '\n' (inferred)
Returns false if a new block cannot be read when needed (EOF or error)
After completion, the buffer ends with a single '\n' element (inferred)

functions.name: Assimp::IOStreamBuffer::getNextBlock
functions.description: Provides the next chunk of data. If a line-based read left the cache mid-block, returns the remainder of the current cache; otherwise reads the next block and returns its contents. Returns true on success. Note: the returned vector may be larger than the number of valid elements for the final block; only the first cacheSize() elements contain newly read data after a read.
requirements: A stream must be open; if no cache content is pending, the function will read the next block
If called after getNextLine/getNextDataLine, the first call may return only the remaining portion of the current cache
For final partial blocks, only the first cacheSize() elements of the returned buffer contain valid new data; callers should consult cacheSize() to determine valid length (inferred)
Returns false if a new block cannot be read and no cached remainder exists

functions.name: Assimp::aiCreateAnimMesh
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API aiAnimMesh* Assimp::aiCreateAnimMesh(const aiMesh* mesh, bool needPositions = true, bool needNormals = true, bool needTangents = true, bool needColors = true, bool needTexCoords = true)
functions.description: Creates a new aiAnimMesh from an existing aiMesh, optionally copying selected attribute channels (positions, normals, tangents/bitangents, colors, texture coordinates) from the source mesh. Typical usage is to generate an animated-vertex variant of a base mesh, enabling only the channels you need to animate. Notes: allocation/lifetime management of the returned aiAnimMesh is not specified in this header; consult Assimp documentation for the correct deallocation routine. Return value and failure modes are not documented here; null on failure is possible but unknown.
requirements: mesh must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized aiMesh from assimp/mesh.h.
If needPositions is true, the input mesh should contain vertex positions; otherwise the copied data will be undefined/unspecified.
If needNormals is true, the input mesh should contain normals; otherwise the copied data will be undefined/unspecified.
If needTangents is true, the input mesh should contain tangents and bitangents; otherwise the copied data will be undefined/unspecified.
If needColors is true, the input mesh should contain one or more color channels; otherwise the copied data will be undefined/unspecified.
If needTexCoords is true, the input mesh should contain one or more texture coordinate channels; otherwise the copied data will be undefined/unspecified.
Caller should manage the lifetime of the returned aiAnimMesh using the appropriate Assimp deallocation API (exact function not specified in this header; consult library docs).
Thread-safety and error-return conventions (e.g., null on failure) are not documented here and remain unknown.

functions.name: Assimp::find_node_by_name_predicate::operator()
functions.description: Predicate functor that returns true if the given XML node's name matches the predicate's stored name string. Used with pugixml find/search helpers.
requirements: node must be a valid pugi::xml_node (not empty) to get a meaningful comparison; otherwise comparison will return false.
The predicate must have been constructed with the intended name (mName) prior to use.

functions.name: Assimp::NodeConverter::to_int
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static int Assimp::NodeConverter<TNodeType>::to_int(TNodeType &node, const char *attribName)
functions.description: Helper that converts the specified attribute of an XML-like node to an int using pugixml's attribute conversion. Returns the integer value of the attribute.
requirements: attribName must not be null (asserted via ai_assert).
node must expose attribute(const char*) returning a pugi::xml_attribute; if the attribute is missing, the returned value will be 0 per pugixml conversion semantics.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::TXmlParser
functions.description: Default constructor for the templated XML parser. Initializes internal document pointer to null and clears internal buffers.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::~TXmlParser
functions.description: Destructor that clears any loaded document and internal buffers via clear().

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::clear
functions.description: Releases the currently parsed XML document and clears internal buffer storage. Safe to call multiple times.
requirements: If an XML document was allocated (mDoc not null), caller must not continue to use any previously obtained node references after clear().

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::findNode
functions.description: Searches the loaded document for the first node with the given name and stores it as the current node. Returns a pointer to the stored current node, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: A document must have been parsed successfully before calling (mDoc != nullptr).
name must not be empty.
Returned pointer refers to an internal member (mCurrent); it becomes invalid after subsequent findNode calls or clear().

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::hasNode
functions.description: Convenience check that returns true if a node with the given name exists in the loaded document.
requirements: A document should be parsed before calling; otherwise it will return false.
name should not be empty.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::hasNode
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::hasNode(Assimp::XmlNode &node, const char *name)
functions.description: Static helper that checks whether the provided node has a child element with the specified name.
requirements: name must not be null.
node should be a valid (non-empty) XML node for meaningful results.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::parse
functions.description: Parses an XML document from an Assimp IOStream into an internal pugixml document. Reads the entire stream into an internal buffer and loads it with pugixml.
requirements: stream must not be null.
The stream must be positioned at the start of the XML data and its FileSize must reflect the readable size.
Input must contain valid XML in the expected encoding (utf-8 per build options).
On success, previously held node references from earlier parses become invalid.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::hasRoot
functions.description: Returns true if an XML document has been parsed and the internal document pointer is non-null.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getDocument
functions.description: Returns the internal pugixml document pointer, or nullptr if no XML was parsed.
requirements: Caller must not delete the returned pointer; ownership remains with the parser.
The returned pointer becomes invalid after clear() or destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getRootNode
functions.description: Returns the document's root node (const). If no document is loaded, returns an empty node.
requirements: A document should be parsed before calling to get a meaningful node.
The returned node is a value (copy) and remains valid independently, but refers to the underlying document; using it after clear() yields an empty/invalid node behavior.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::hasAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::hasAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name)
functions.description: Static helper that checks whether the provided node has an attribute with the specified name.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should be a valid (non-empty) XML node for meaningful results.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getUIntAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getUIntAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, unsigned int &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to an unsigned int using pugixml conversion. Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.
Conversion follows pugixml semantics; non-numeric strings convert to 0.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getIntAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getIntAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, int &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to an int. Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getRealAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getRealAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, ai_real &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to ai_real (float or double depending on build). Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.
Precision depends on ASSIMP_DOUBLE_PRECISION build flag.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getFloatAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getFloatAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, float &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to float. Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getDoubleAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getDoubleAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, double &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to double. Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getStdStrAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getStdStrAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, std::string &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and copies its string value into val. Returns true on success.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getBoolAttribute
functions.signature: template <class TNodeType> static bool Assimp::TXmlParser<TNodeType>::getBoolAttribute(Assimp::XmlNode &xmlNode, const char *name, bool &val)
functions.description: Retrieves an attribute by name and converts it to bool using pugixml rules. Returns true on success and writes the result to val.
requirements: name must not be null.
xmlNode should contain the named attribute; otherwise returns false and val is unmodified.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getValueAsString
functions.description: Reads the text content of the node as a string, trims it, and writes it to text. Returns true if node is non-empty.
requirements: node must be non-empty; otherwise returns false.
Trimming is applied via ai_trim from Assimp.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getValueAsReal
functions.description: Reads the text content of the node and converts it to ai_real using pugixml's as_float(). Returns true if node is non-empty.
requirements: node must be non-empty; otherwise returns false.
Numeric conversion uses as_float(); for double-precision builds, value will be promoted to ai_real.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getValueAsFloat
functions.description: Reads the text content of the node and converts it to float. Returns true if node is non-empty.
requirements: node must be non-empty; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getValueAsInt
functions.description: Reads the text content of the node and converts it to int. Returns true if node is non-empty.
requirements: node must be non-empty; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: Assimp::TXmlParser::getValueAsBool
functions.description: Reads the text content of the node and converts it to bool. Returns true if node is non-empty.
requirements: node must be non-empty; otherwise returns false.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::XmlNodeIterator
functions.description: Constructs an iterator over all child element nodes of a parent, collecting them either in pre-order or post-order traversal, excluding the parent itself.
requirements: parent must remain valid for the lifetime of the iterator (references to nodes are stored).
mode must be either PreOrderMode or PostOrderMode.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::~XmlNodeIterator
functions.description: Default destructor for the iterator. Does not own external resources.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::collectChildrenPreOrder
functions.description: Recursively collects child nodes in pre-order (visit node, then its children), excluding the iterator's parent node, and stores them internally.
requirements: node should belong to the same document tree as the parent for meaningful traversal.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::collectChildrenPostOrder
functions.description: Recursively collects child nodes in post-order (visit children first, then node), excluding the iterator's parent node, and stores them internally.
requirements: node should belong to the same document tree as the parent for meaningful traversal.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::getNext
functions.description: Retrieves the next collected node into 'next'. Returns false when no more nodes are available.
requirements: Caller must provide a reference 'next' to receive the node.
Must be called until it returns false to exhaust the iteration.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::size
functions.description: Returns the number of collected nodes.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::isEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if no nodes are collected.

functions.name: Assimp::XmlNodeIterator::clear
functions.description: Clears the collected nodes and resets the internal index.
requirements: After clear(), any in-progress iteration should restart, as internal state is reset.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::BlobIOStream
functions.description: Constructor for a write-only in-memory IOStream that accumulates written bytes into an internal buffer, to be exported later as an aiExportDataBlob. Typically created via Assimp::BlobIOSystem::Open().
requirements: creator may be nullptr; if non-null, it should point to the BlobIOSystem that will collect the blob on stream destruction.
file is used as the logical filename for blob chaining and may influence which blob becomes the master; it should be the same as BlobIOSystem::GetMagicFileName() for the master blob.
initial is the initial buffer capacity in bytes; zero is permitted, growth occurs automatically as needed.
Stream is write-only; reading from it is unsupported and will return 0.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::~BlobIOStream
functions.description: Destructor that finalizes the in-memory stream. If a creator was provided, it transfers ownership of the buffered data to the creator as an aiExportDataBlob via BlobIOSystem::OnDestruct(). Frees any remaining internal buffer.
requirements: Ensure the stream is closed/deleted (e.g., via BlobIOSystem::Close) after finishing writes so the blob is captured by the creator.
Do not use the stream after destruction.
If creator is nullptr, no blob will be enqueued; data will be freed.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::GetBlob
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated aiExportDataBlob containing the stream’s current data. Transfers ownership of the underlying buffer to the blob and nulls the stream’s buffer pointer.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership of the returned aiExportDataBlob and is responsible for deleting it (and any linked blobs) when done.
After this call, the stream’s internal buffer is set to nullptr; further writes require the stream to grow a fresh buffer and previously returned blob content will not be modified.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::Read
functions.signature: size_t Assimp::BlobIOStream::Read(void *buffer, size_t size, size_t count)
functions.description: No-op read for a write-only stream. Always returns 0 to indicate no data is read.
requirements: Callers must not rely on reading from this stream; it is write-only.
buffer may be nullptr since the function ignores inputs, but passing a valid pointer is recommended by IOStream contracts.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::Write
functions.signature: size_t Assimp::BlobIOStream::Write(const void *pvBuffer, size_t pSize, size_t pCount)
functions.description: Appends pSize*pCount bytes from pvBuffer to the stream, auto-growing the internal buffer as needed. Advances the file cursor and updates the logical file size. Returns the number of items written (pCount).
requirements: pvBuffer must point to at least pSize*pCount bytes of readable memory.
If pSize or pCount is 0, no bytes are written and 0 is returned.
Writing may reallocate the internal buffer; previously returned raw buffer pointers (if any) become invalid.
On success, the return value equals pCount; there is no partial-write signaling.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::Seek
functions.description: Moves the stream cursor relative to SET, CUR, or END. Seeking past current end grows the buffer and extends the file size. Returns AI_SUCCESS on success, AI_FAILURE on invalid origin.
requirements: pOrigin must be one of aiOrigin_SET, aiOrigin_CUR, or aiOrigin_END; other values yield AI_FAILURE.
For aiOrigin_END, pOffset should be <= current FileSize() to avoid underflow (which would otherwise wrap size_t and lead to excessive growth).
Seeking beyond end (SET/CUR with offset past FileSize) is allowed and will grow the buffer, zero-filling the gap implicitly (buffer contents in the gap are unspecified).

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current cursor position in bytes from the start of the stream.
requirements: None beyond the stream being a valid, live instance.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::FileSize
functions.description: Returns the logical file size in bytes (the maximum position ever written or sought to).
requirements: None beyond the stream being a valid, live instance.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOStream::Flush
functions.description: No-op flush. Provided to satisfy IOStream interface; has no effect for the in-memory buffer.
requirements: Do not rely on Flush to force any additional state changes; data is already in memory.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::BlobIOSystem
functions.description: Default constructor for a blob-backed IOSystem. Uses the magic filename "$blobfile" to identify the master blob entry.
requirements: None. After constructing, use Open() to obtain write-only streams and Close() to finalize them.
To create a master blob with the default base name, open/write/close a file named exactly GetMagicFileName() ("$blobfile").

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::~BlobIOSystem
functions.description: Destructor that cleans up any aiExportDataBlob objects still owned by the IOSystem (i.e., if GetBlobChain() wasn’t called).
requirements: If you need the blob chain, call GetBlobChain() before destruction; otherwise remaining blobs will be deleted and data lost.
Do not use the IOSystem after destruction.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::GetMagicFileName
functions.description: Returns the magic file name used to identify the master blob. Defaults to "$blobfile" unless constructed with a custom base name.
requirements: None. The returned pointer remains valid as long as the BlobIOSystem object is alive.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::GetBlobChain
functions.description: Builds and returns the head of a linked aiExportDataBlob chain from all streams that were opened and closed. The master blob is the entry whose filename equals GetMagicFileName(). Names for subsequent blobs are set based on the baseName policy. Transfers ownership to the caller and clears internal storage.
requirements: All relevant BlobIOStream instances must be closed (so their destructor enqueued blobs) before calling.
There must be a blob whose filename equals GetMagicFileName(); otherwise returns nullptr and logs an error.
Caller assumes ownership of the returned blob chain and must delete it when finished.
After this call, the IOSystem relinquishes ownership of blobs; calling it again without new writes will return nullptr.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::Exists
functions.description: Reports whether a file name has been opened for writing via this IOSystem during its lifetime. Uses an internal set of created names.
requirements: pFile must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
Only files opened via Open() with a write mode are tracked.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::getOsSeparator
functions.description: Returns the path separator used by this IOSystem ('/').
requirements: None.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::Open
functions.description: Opens a write-only in-memory stream for the given logical filename. Only write modes are supported; non-write modes return nullptr.
requirements: pMode must be non-null and begin with 'w' (e.g., "w", "wb"). Other modes cause the function to return nullptr.
pFile must be a non-null, null-terminated C string indicating the logical filename.
Caller owns the returned IOStream* and must eventually pass it to Close() (or delete it) to finalize and enqueue its blob.

functions.name: Assimp::BlobIOSystem::Close
functions.description: Closes a stream previously opened by Open(). Deletes the IOStream, triggering blob finalization and enqueueing within this IOSystem.
requirements: pFile must be a pointer obtained from this IOSystem’s Open(); passing other pointers results in undefined behavior.
Do not use pFile after calling Close().

functions.name: Assimp::Math::gcd
functions.signature:
template <typename IntegerType>
inline IntegerType Assimp::Math::gcd(IntegerType a, IntegerType b);
functions.description: Computes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integer-like values using the Euclidean algorithm. Call with two values of an integral type; the function handles zero inputs (gcd(0, b) == b, gcd(a, 0) == a). Negative inputs are processed according to C++ % semantics and may yield a negative GCD. Usage: pass two integers or integer-like types supporting %, ==, and assignment.
requirements: IntegerType must support the modulus operator (%) and equality comparison (==).
IntegerType must be a type for which (IntegerType)0 is a valid zero value and modulo is well-defined (typically a built-in or custom integer-like type).
Inputs may be zero; both zero returns 0.
Behavior with negative operands follows C++ integer % semantics; sign of the result is not normalized.
No overflow checks are performed (not typically an issue for %, but copies/assignments occur).

functions.name: Assimp::Math::lcm
functions.signature:
template <typename IntegerType>
inline IntegerType Assimp::Math::lcm(IntegerType a, IntegerType b);
functions.description: Computes the least common multiple (LCM) of two integer-like values using lcm(a,b) = a / gcd(a,b) * b. If gcd(a,b) is 0 (i.e., both inputs are zero), returns 0. Intended for integral types; may overflow for large magnitudes.
requirements: IntegerType must support gcd as defined for the same type, division (/), multiplication (*), and truthiness for comparison with zero.
If both inputs are zero, the function returns 0.
Potential overflow in a / t * b is not checked; callers must ensure values fit in the IntegerType range.
Behavior with negative operands is not normalized; sign of the result follows C++ arithmetic rules for / and *.
IntegerType must be a type for which (IntegerType)0 is a valid zero value.

functions.name: Assimp::Math::getEpsilon
functions.description: Returns std::numeric_limits<T>::epsilon(), i.e., the machine epsilon for type T. For floating-point types, this is the difference between 1 and the next representable value; for integer types, it is 0. Use to obtain a tolerance suitable for type T.
requirements: T must be a type with a valid std::numeric_limits<T> specialization (standard arithmetic types qualify).
For integer types, epsilon() is 0; callers should not use it as a tolerance for integers unless this is intended.
<limits> must be available (it is included by the header).

functions.name: Assimp::Math::aiPi
functions.description: Returns the mathematical constant pi (3.14159265358979323846) cast to type T. Intended primarily for floating-point types; using integral T will truncate the value.
requirements: T must be constructible from a double via static_cast<T>.
For integral T, the returned value will be truncated; callers should prefer floating-point T (e.g., float, double, long double) for meaningful results.

functions.name: DeadlyErrorBase::DeadlyErrorBase
functions.description: Constructs the base exception with a pre-built Assimp formatter stream. Intended to build the runtime_error message used by Assimp exception types. Typical usage is internal to other Deadly*Error constructors to accumulate a formatted message.
requirements: Parameter f must be a valid Assimp::Formatter::format instance ready for streaming-in of message content.
Constructor is intended to be called by derived exception types (it is protected).

functions.name: DeadlyImportError::DeadlyImportError
functions.description: Constructs an import-failure exception with a C-string message. Importer plugins throw this to signal an unrecoverable import error; public loading APIs will return nullptr for the aiScene on such errors.
requirements: message should point to a valid null-terminated C string (unknown behavior if null or invalid).
Intended for use by importer plugins to signal fatal errors.

functions.name: DeadlyExportError::DeadlyExportError
functions.description: Variadic constructor to create an export-failure exception by formatting the provided arguments via Assimp::Formatter. Exporter plugins throw this to indicate unrecoverable export errors; exporting APIs will return nullptr for the aiScene in such cases.
requirements: Each argument in args must be stream-insertable (operator<<) into Assimp::Formatter::format.
Intended for use by exporter plugins to signal fatal errors.

functions.name: ExceptionSwallower::operator()
functions.description: Generic exception-to-default mapper. Returns a value-initialized T (e.g., T()) when invoked, intended to be used in catch blocks to produce a safe default return after swallowing an exception.
requirements: No active-exception requirement for this generic template; it does not rethrow.
Use when the function’s return type is T and you want to return a default-constructed value upon exception.

functions.name: ExceptionSwallower<T *>::operator()
functions.description: Pointer specialization that returns nullptr. Used to safely return a null pointer from an exception handler.
requirements: No active-exception requirement; it does not rethrow.
Use when the function’s return type is a pointer and you want to return nullptr upon exception.

functions.name: ExceptionSwallower<aiReturn>::operator()
functions.description: aiReturn specialization that maps the currently handled exception to an aiReturn code: std::bad_alloc -> aiReturn_OUTOFMEMORY; any other exception -> aiReturn_FAILURE. Implemented by rethrowing the current exception and catching specific types.
requirements: Must be called while handling an active exception (i.e., from within a catch context); calling with no active exception triggers a rethrow with no current exception, leading to std::terminate.
Use only when the function’s return type is aiReturn and you need consistent error codes from exceptions.

functions.name: ExceptionSwallower<void>::operator()
functions.description: void specialization that performs no action. Intended for use in catch blocks in functions returning void to swallow exceptions cleanly.
requirements: No active-exception requirement; it does not rethrow.
Use when the function’s return type is void and you want to ignore the exception.

functions.name: Assimp::ByteSwap::Swap2
functions.description: In-place byte-order swap of exactly 2 bytes at the given memory location. Intended to convert 16-bit values between little-endian and big-endian. Direct use of ByteSwap is deprecated in Assimp; prefer StreamReader when possible.
requirements: _szOut must be non-null (ai_assert enforces this in debug builds).
_szOut must point to at least 2 bytes of writable memory.
On some compilers (e.g., MSVC paths) the pointer is reinterpreted as uint16_t*, so it should be suitably aligned for 2-byte access to avoid undefined behavior.
The pointed-to data is modified in place; pass a pointer to mutable storage.

functions.name: Assimp::ByteSwap::Swap4
functions.description: In-place byte-order swap of exactly 4 bytes at the given memory location. Intended to convert 32-bit values (e.g., uint32_t, float) between little-endian and big-endian. Direct use of ByteSwap is deprecated; prefer StreamReader.
requirements: _szOut must be non-null (ai_assert enforces this in debug builds).
_szOut must point to at least 4 bytes of writable memory.
On some compilers (e.g., MSVC paths) the pointer is reinterpreted as uint32_t*, so it should be suitably aligned for 4-byte access to avoid undefined behavior.
The pointed-to data is modified in place; pass a pointer to mutable storage.

functions.name: Assimp::ByteSwap::Swap8
functions.description: In-place byte-order swap of exactly 8 bytes at the given memory location. Intended to convert 64-bit values (e.g., uint64_t, double) between little-endian and big-endian. Direct use of ByteSwap is deprecated; prefer StreamReader.
requirements: _szOut must be non-null (ai_assert enforces this in debug builds).
_szOut must point to at least 8 bytes of writable memory.
On some compilers (e.g., MSVC paths) the pointer is reinterpreted as uint64_t*, so it should be suitably aligned for 8-byte access to avoid undefined behavior.
The pointed-to data is modified in place; pass a pointer to mutable storage.

functions.name: Assimp::ByteSwap::Swap
functions.description: In-place byte-order swap of a 32-bit float value referenced by fOut. Direct use of ByteSwap is deprecated; prefer StreamReader.
requirements: fOut must be non-null (indirectly required by Swap4).
fOut must point to a valid, writable float object (4 bytes).
The pointed-to float is modified in place.

functions.name: Assimp::ByteSwap::Swapped
functions.signature: template <typename Type> static inline Type Assimp::ByteSwap::Swapped(Type tOut)
functions.description: Returns a byte-swapped copy of the input value by value (does not modify the original). Only supported for types of size 2, 4, or 8 bytes, such as 16/32/64-bit integers and 32/64-bit floating-point types. Direct use of ByteSwap is deprecated; prefer StreamReader.
requirements: Type must have sizeof(Type) equal to 2, 4, or 8; otherwise no _swapper specialization exists and compilation will fail.
Type must be safe to treat as a plain byte sequence for endianness swapping (typically integral or floating-point POD types).
Function performs an unconditional swap (not gated by runtime endianness); callers must decide when swapping is appropriate.

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Encode
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API void Encode(const uint8_t *in, size_t inLength, std::string &out);
functions.description: Encodes a binary buffer to a Base64 ASCII representation. Writes the encoded data into the provided std::string. Despite the comment mentioning UTF64, this function is a Base64 encoder based on context and naming.
requirements: in must point to a valid buffer of at least inLength bytes when inLength > 0
out must be a valid, writable std::string reference; its previous contents may be overwritten or appended depending on implementation (details not specified)
No null-termination is required for in since inLength is provided
The input data should be the content to encode; non-Base64 constraints do not apply to input since it is raw binary

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Encode
functions.description: Encodes a vector of binary bytes to a Base64 ASCII representation. Writes the encoded data into the provided std::string. The UTF64 wording in comments appears to be a typo; this performs Base64 encoding.
requirements: in may be empty; if non-empty it must contain the bytes to encode
out must be a valid, writable std::string reference; prior contents handling is unspecified
Input is treated as binary; no character encoding requirements

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Encode
functions.description: Encodes a vector of binary bytes to a Base64 ASCII string and returns it by value. Comment references to UTF64 likely mean Base64.
requirements: in may be empty; if non-empty it must contain the bytes to encode
Caller should expect a newly constructed std::string containing the Base64 data

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Decode
functions.signature: ASSIMP_API size_t Decode(const char *in, size_t inLength, uint8_t *&out);
functions.description: Decodes a Base64 ASCII buffer into its original binary form. Writes/assigns the decoded buffer to out and returns the decoded size in bytes. Ownership/allocation details for out are not specified in this header.
requirements: in must point to a valid buffer of at least inLength bytes; it need not be null-terminated
in should contain Base64-encoded ASCII data; invalid characters or padding behavior are unspecified
out must be a reference to a pointer variable suitable for receiving the decoded buffer; allocation/ownership and required deallocation method are not specified (unknown)
Caller must use the returned size to interpret the valid length of the data in out

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Decode
functions.description: Decodes a Base64 ASCII std::string into its original binary bytes, writing the result into the provided std::vector and returning the decoded size.
requirements: in should contain Base64-encoded ASCII data; handling of invalid input is unspecified
out must be a valid, writable std::vector<uint8_t> reference; its prior contents may be overwritten or cleared depending on implementation (unspecified)
Caller should use the returned size to know how many bytes were written to out

functions.name: Assimp::Base64::Decode
functions.description: Decodes a Base64 ASCII std::string and returns the decoded binary data as a std::vector<uint8_t>.
requirements: in should contain Base64-encoded ASCII data; behavior on invalid input is unspecified
